You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

The restructuring is designed to create a durable, institutionalized framework for managing current and future personnel transitions without disruption to Fund operations or investor relationships.

**[B. Governance Enhancement]{.underline}**

Under the current structure, each of the five senior principals holds direct membership interests in both the General Partner (Ardent Capital GP III LLC) and the ManCo (Ardent Capital Management LLC). This parallel ownership structure, while common at the time of the Fund\'s formation, creates significant complexity in governance and economic alignment, particularly in the context of personnel changes. Each departure or addition of a principal requires amendments to the operating agreements of both entities, separate consent processes, and independent economic negotiations at each level.

The proposed restructuring introduces a centralized holding company --- Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\") --- that will serve as the sole member of both the ManCo and a newly formed intermediate entity, Ardent GP Intermediate LLC. GP Intermediate will, in turn, serve as the sole member of the General Partner. This two-tier governance framework centralizes all ownership and governance authority in HoldCo, creating a single point of control and simplifying future changes. Personnel transitions, economic reallocations, and governance modifications can be effectuated through amendments to the HoldCo LLC Agreement alone, without the need for parallel amendments to the operating agreements of the General Partner and the ManCo.

The restructuring also formalizes decision-making authority. Under the current structure, each principal has equal governance rights proportional to their membership interests in both the GP and the ManCo, which has at times resulted in ambiguity regarding approval requirements for routine operational matters. The HoldCo LLC Agreement designates Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan as Managing Members with authority over day-to-day operations, while reserving certain material actions for supermajority consent of all HoldCo members. This clear delineation of authority is intended to enhance operational efficiency and reduce administrative burden.

**[C. Next-Generation Integration]{.underline}**

A critical objective of the restructuring is the formal integration of two next-generation principals into the Ardent platform\'s economic and governance framework:

> **Elena Marchetti** (Principal, age 38) joined Ardent Capital in 2017 and has been a key contributor to the Fund\'s investment activities, including serving as the primary deal lead on two active portfolio companies. Ms. Marchetti has demonstrated strong investment judgment and leadership capabilities, and her promotion to a carry-bearing role is viewed by the General Partner as an important step in ensuring the platform\'s continuity.
>
> **Samuel Okonkwo** (Principal, age 36) joined Ardent Capital in 2018 and has played an increasingly significant role in the Fund\'s deal origination and portfolio management activities. Mr. Okonkwo has been responsible for sourcing three of the Fund\'s eleven active investments and has earned the confidence of the senior leadership team through his analytical rigor and operational expertise.

Under the proposed restructuring, Ms. Marchetti and Mr. Okonkwo will each receive a 4% carried interest allocation in the Fund and corresponding membership interests in HoldCo. Their economic participation will be subject to vesting schedules set forth in the HoldCo LLC Agreement, which are designed to align their incentives with long-term performance and retention. The General Partner believes that formalizing the economic participation of these next-generation professionals is essential to the institutional stability of the Ardent platform and to retaining top-tier talent in a competitive market for private equity professionals.

**[III. New Entity Structure]{.underline}**

**[A. Current Structure (Pre-Restructuring)]{.underline}**

Under the Fund\'s existing organizational framework, five individual principals hold direct membership interests in both the General Partner and the ManCo:

> **Ardent Capital GP III LLC** (the \"General Partner\") is a Delaware limited liability company and the sole general partner of the Fund. Its members are the five individual principals, each holding membership interests in the following percentages:
>
> • Marcus Aldridge: 35%
>
> • Priya Narayanan: 30%
>
> • David Kellner: 15%
>
> • Joanna Trask: 12%
>
> • Robert Hsiao: 8%
>
> **Ardent Capital Management LLC** (the \"ManCo\") is a Delaware limited liability company that serves as the Fund\'s investment adviser and manager. The ManCo is registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as an investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (CRD #298417). Its members are the same five individual principals, holding membership interests in identical percentages to those set forth above.

The General Partner is the sole general partner of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the Fund). The ManCo provides investment advisory and management services to the Fund pursuant to the terms of the Investment Management Agreement entered into at the time of the Fund\'s formation.

The parallel ownership structure described above --- in which each principal holds identical percentage interests in both the GP and the ManCo --- was established at the time of the Fund\'s formation for simplicity and to align the principals\' economic and governance interests across both entities. However, as discussed in Section II.B above, this structure has proven cumbersome in the context of personnel changes and does not provide an efficient mechanism for the admission of new carry-bearing professionals.

**[B. Proposed Structure (Post-Restructuring)]{.underline}**

Following the restructuring, the organizational framework will be as follows:

> **Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\")** --- a newly formed Delaware limited liability company --- will serve as the parent holding company for the Ardent platform. HoldCo will be the sole member of both the ManCo (directly) and GP Intermediate (directly). The Certificate of Formation for HoldCo was filed with the Delaware Secretary of State on March 1, 2024 (DE File No. 7948231).
>
> The members of HoldCo and their respective membership interests will be as follows:
>
> • Marcus Aldridge: 42%
>
> • Priya Narayanan: 36%
>
> • Robert Hsiao: 14%
>
> • Elena Marchetti: 4%
>
> • Samuel Okonkwo: 4%
>
> **Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\")** --- a newly formed Delaware limited liability company --- will serve as an intermediate entity between HoldCo and the General Partner. GP Intermediate will be the sole member of Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the General Partner). The Certificate of Formation for GP Intermediate was filed with the Delaware Secretary of State on March 1, 2024 (DE File No. 7948237).
>
> **Ardent Capital GP III LLC** (the General Partner) will remain in existence as a Delaware limited liability company and will continue to serve as the sole general partner of the Fund. The only change is that its sole member will be GP Intermediate (replacing the five individual principals). The LLC agreement of the General Partner will be amended and restated (Second Amended and Restated LLC Agreement) to reflect this change in membership.
>
> **Ardent Capital Management LLC** (the ManCo) will remain in existence as a Delaware limited liability company and will continue to serve as the Fund\'s SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD #298417). Its sole member will be HoldCo (replacing the five individual principals). The LLC agreement of the ManCo will be amended and restated (Second Amended and Restated LLC Agreement) to reflect this change in membership. Form ADV will be amended to reflect the new ownership structure.
>
> **Ardent Capital Partners III LP** (the Fund) will remain in existence as a Delaware limited partnership. Ardent Capital GP III LLC will continue to serve as its sole general partner. The Fund\'s LPA will be amended (Amendment No. 1 to the LPA) to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner\'s ownership.

The key structural features of the proposed framework are summarized below:

> • HoldCo is formed as a Delaware limited liability company. Its Certificate of Formation has been filed with the Delaware Secretary of State (filed March 1, 2024, DE File No. 7948231).
>
> • GP Intermediate is formed as a Delaware limited liability company. Its Certificate of Formation has been filed with the Delaware Secretary of State (filed March 1, 2024, DE File No. 7948237).
>
> • The registered agent for both HoldCo and GP Intermediate is Prestige Registered Agents LLC, 850 New Burton Road, Suite 201, Dover, DE 19904.
>
> • HoldCo has been assigned EIN 93-1847225 by the Internal Revenue Service. GP Intermediate has been assigned EIN 93-1847231.
>
> • The ManCo will remain an SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD #298417). An amended Form ADV Part 1 will be filed with the SEC to reflect the new ownership structure, including the identification of HoldCo as the ManCo\'s sole member and the updated Schedule A and Schedule B information. The amendment is targeted for filing on or about March 10, 2024.
>
> • The Managing Members of HoldCo will be Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan, who will have authority over the day-to-day operations of HoldCo and, by extension, the ManCo and the General Partner.
>
> • The departing principals (David Kellner and Joanna Trask) will withdraw as members of both the General Partner and the ManCo. Ardent GP Intermediate LLC will be substituted as the sole member of the General Partner, and HoldCo will be substituted as the sole member of the ManCo.

Organizational charts depicting the current structure (pre-restructuring) and the proposed structure (post-restructuring) are attached hereto as Appendix A and Appendix B, respectively.

**[C. Governance Provisions of HoldCo]{.underline}**

The HoldCo LLC Agreement, which will govern the internal affairs of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC, includes the following key governance provisions:

**Managing Members.** Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan will serve as the Managing Members of HoldCo, with authority over the day-to-day management and operations of HoldCo, the ManCo, and the General Partner. The Managing Members will have the power to act on behalf of HoldCo in all matters arising in the ordinary course of business, including the execution of contracts, the hiring and termination of personnel, the management of portfolio company investments, and the conduct of investor relations.

**Supermajority Consent Provisions.** Certain material actions will require the affirmative consent of members holding at least 75% of the total membership interests in HoldCo (a \"Supermajority Consent\"). Actions requiring Supermajority Consent include, among others:

> \(a\) the transfer, assignment, pledge, or encumbrance of any membership interest in HoldCo;
>
> \(b\) the admission of any new member to HoldCo;
>
> \(c\) any amendment to the carried interest allocation percentages set forth in the Carried Interest Allocation Agreement;
>
> \(d\) the incurrence of any indebtedness by HoldCo, the ManCo, or the General Partner in excess of \$500,000 in the aggregate;
>
> \(e\) the entry into any transaction with an affiliate of HoldCo or any member thereof;
>
> \(f\) the dissolution, liquidation, or winding up of HoldCo, the ManCo, or the General Partner; and
>
> \(g\) any amendment to the HoldCo LLC Agreement.

**Transfer Restrictions.** The HoldCo LLC Agreement contains customary restrictions on the transfer of membership interests. No member may transfer, assign, pledge, or otherwise dispose of any membership interest without the prior written consent of the Managing Members and, in the case of transfers to third parties, a Supermajority Consent. Permitted transfers to immediate family members and estate planning vehicles are subject to the prior written consent of the Managing Members and compliance with applicable securities laws.

**Buy-Sell Provisions.** The HoldCo LLC Agreement includes buy-sell provisions that are triggered upon the occurrence of certain events, including the death, disability, or termination of a member. Upon the occurrence of a triggering event, the remaining members (or HoldCo itself, at the election of the Managing Members) will have the right to purchase the departing member\'s interest at a price determined by a formula-based valuation methodology set forth in the LLC Agreement.

**Tag-Along and Drag-Along Rights.** The HoldCo LLC Agreement includes customary tag-along and drag-along provisions. If the Managing Members propose to transfer more than 50% of their combined membership interests in HoldCo to a third party, each non-Managing Member will have the right to participate in such transfer on a pro rata basis and on the same terms and conditions (tag-along). Conversely, if the Managing Members receive a bona fide offer to acquire 100% of the membership interests in HoldCo, they will have the right to require all other members to participate in such transfer on the same terms and conditions (drag-along).

**Vesting Schedules for Next-Generation Principals.** The membership interests of Elena Marchetti and Samuel Okonkwo in HoldCo will be subject to vesting schedules set forth in the HoldCo LLC Agreement. The specific vesting terms are under negotiation and are expected to include a four-year vesting period with a one-year cliff, subject to continued employment with the ManCo and satisfaction of applicable performance conditions. Unvested interests will be subject to forfeiture upon termination of employment, except in cases of death, disability, or termination without cause.

**[IV. Economics Realignment]{.underline}**

The restructuring necessitates a comprehensive realignment of the Fund\'s economic arrangements, including carried interest allocations, management company profit share distributions, and GP commitment obligations. This section describes the pre-restructuring and post-restructuring economics in detail.

**[A. Pre-Restructuring Carry Allocation]{.underline}**

Under the current carried interest allocation framework, the Fund\'s 20% carried interest (subject to the 8% preferred return and full catch-up mechanism described in Articles VI and VII of the LPA) is allocated among the five senior principals in the following percentages:

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**           **Current Carry %**     **Accrued Carry (Based on \$87.6M Total)**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- --------------------------------------------
  Marcus Aldridge         35%                     \$30,660,000

  Priya Narayanan         30%                     \$26,280,000

  David Kellner           15%                     \$13,140,000

  Joanna Trask            12%                     \$10,512,000

  Robert Hsiao            8%                      \$7,008,000

  **Total**               **100%**                **\$87,600,000**
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The carried interest rate is 20% of net profits generated by the Fund, calculated on a whole-fund basis, subject to an 8% per annum compounded preferred return to the limited partners and a full (100%) catch-up to the General Partner until the 20/80 split is achieved, all as set forth in Article VII of the LPA. The clawback obligation under the LPA is joint and several among all members of the General Partner, with each individual principal maintaining an escrow account equal to 30% of aggregate carried interest distributions received.

**[B. Post-Restructuring Carry Allocation]{.underline}**

Following the restructuring, the carried interest allocations will be realigned as follows:

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**           **New Carry %**         **Change from Current**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -------------------------
  Marcus Aldridge         42%                     +7 percentage points

  Priya Narayanan         36%                     +6 percentage points

  Robert Hsiao            14%                     +6 percentage points

  Elena Marchetti         4%                      New allocation

  Samuel Okonkwo          4%                      New allocation

  **Total**               **100%**                ---
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------

The aggregate 27 percentage points of carried interest freed up by the departures of David Kellner (15%) and Joanna Trask (12%) are redistributed among the remaining and next-generation principals as set forth above. The redistribution reflects the General Partner\'s assessment of each principal\'s relative contribution to the Fund\'s investment activities, leadership responsibilities, and long-term commitment to the Ardent platform.

For illustrative purposes, the following table sets forth the notional shares of the \$87.6 million of accrued carried interest (as of September 30, 2023) under the post-restructuring allocation percentages:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**                       **Post-Restructuring Notional Accrued Carry**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------
  Marcus Aldridge                     \$36,792,000

  Priya Narayanan                     \$31,536,000

  Robert Hsiao                        \$12,264,000

  Elena Marchetti                     \$3,504,000

  Samuel Okonkwo                      \$3,504,000

  **Total**                           **\$87,600,000**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

It is important to note, however, that the accrued carried interest attributable to the vested interests of David Kellner and Joanna Trask will be carved out and addressed separately pursuant to their respective separation agreements, as described in Section V below. The redistribution of carry percentages described in this Section IV.B applies to go-forward carried interest on future appreciation of the Fund\'s portfolio and on future realizations. The Amended and Restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement will contain detailed provisions governing the allocation of carried interest between the departing principals\' retained vested interests and the post-restructuring allocations.

The carried interest rate (20%), preferred return (8%), catch-up mechanism, and clawback mechanics are unchanged. There is no modification to any economic term of the LPA that affects the limited partners\' rights, including the preferred return, the distribution waterfall, or the clawback.

**[C. Management Fee Allocation]{.underline}**

The Fund\'s annual management fee during the investment period is 1.75% of total committed capital, yielding annual management fee revenue of approximately \$49 million (\$2.8 billion × 1.75%). Following the expiration of the investment period on June 30, 2025, the management fee will step down to 1.50% of invested capital (net of write-offs and write-downs), as provided in Section 4.1 of the LPA.

The ManCo\'s operating expenses --- including compensation and benefits for sixty-two (62) non-principal employees, office lease payments (590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor, New York, NY 10022), technology infrastructure and systems, compliance and regulatory costs, professional liability insurance, and other general and administrative expenses --- total approximately \$31.85 million per annum, representing approximately 65% of the annual management fee revenue.

The ManCo Profit Share --- the residual management fee revenue after payment of operating expenses --- is approximately \$17.15 million per annum (approximately 35% of the \$49 million annual management fee). This profit share is distributed to the principals in accordance with their respective ownership interests in the ManCo (and, following the restructuring, through their membership interests in HoldCo).

**Pre-Restructuring Profit Share Allocation:**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**           **Share %**             **Annual Amount**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  Marcus Aldridge         35%                     \$6,002,500

  Priya Narayanan         30%                     \$5,145,000

  David Kellner           15%                     \$2,572,500

  Joanna Trask            12%                     \$2,058,000

  Robert Hsiao            8%                      \$1,372,000

  **Total**               **100%**                **\$17,150,000**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Post-Restructuring Profit Share Allocation (through HoldCo):**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**           **Share %**             **Annual Amount**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  Marcus Aldridge         42%                     \$7,203,000

  Priya Narayanan         36%                     \$6,174,000

  Robert Hsiao            14%                     \$2,401,000

  Elena Marchetti         4%                      \$686,000

  Samuel Okonkwo          4%                      \$686,000

  **Total**               **100%**                **\$17,150,000**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

There is no change to the management fee rate charged to the Fund, the total management fee amount payable by the limited partners, or the ManCo\'s operating expense budget. The redistribution of the ManCo profit share is an internal economic matter among the principals and does not affect the Fund or its limited partners. The management fee payable by the limited partners under Section 4.1 of the LPA remains \$49 million per annum during the investment period (subject to adjustments for new closings and defaulting limited partners as provided therein).

**[D. GP Commitment Reallocation]{.underline}**

The General Partner\'s aggregate commitment to the Fund is \$42 million, representing 1.5% of the Fund\'s \$2.8 billion in total commitments, as required by Section 3.2 of the LPA. This commitment is funded pro rata by the individual principals in proportion to their membership interests in the General Partner.

The departing principals\' GP commitment obligations are summarized as follows:

> **David Kellner:**
>
> • Total GP commitment: \$6,300,000 (15% × \$42,000,000)
>
> • Funded amount (70%): \$4,410,000
>
> • Unfunded balance: \$1,890,000
>
> **Joanna Trask:**
>
> • Total GP commitment: \$5,040,000 (12% × \$42,000,000)
>
> • Funded amount (70%): \$3,528,000
>
> • Unfunded balance: \$1,512,000
>
> **Combined unfunded departing commitment:** \$3,402,000 (\$1,890,000 + \$1,512,000)

The unfunded balance of the departing principals\' GP commitments (\$3,402,000 in the aggregate) will be assumed by the remaining HoldCo members on a pro rata basis in accordance with their post-restructuring membership percentages:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**           **HoldCo %**            **Assumed Unfunded Commitment**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- ---------------------------------
  Marcus Aldridge         42%                     \$1,428,840

**[VII. Key-Person Analysis]{.underline}**

**[A. LPA Key-Person Provisions (Section 5.2)]{.underline}**

Section 5.2 of the LPA designates Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan as the \"Key Persons\" of the Fund. Under Section 5.2, a \"Key Person Event\" is triggered if:

> \(a\) both Key Persons cease to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund; or
>
> \(b\) one Key Person ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund and is not replaced by a substitute approved by the LPAC within one hundred twenty (120) days of such cessation.

Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event, the Fund\'s investment period is automatically suspended, and the General Partner may not make new investments (other than follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies and investments for which binding commitments have been entered into prior to the Key Person Event) until either (i) the LPAC approves a substitute Key Person, or (ii) the LPAC waives the Key Person Event by affirmative vote.

Neither David Kellner nor Joanna Trask is a designated Key Person under Section 5.2 of the LPA. Their departures do not, individually or in combination, constitute a Key Person Event under the LPA.

**Conclusion:** No Key Person Event is triggered by the departures of David Kellner and Joanna Trask. Both designated Key Persons --- Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan --- continue in their full-time roles as Managing Partners of the Ardent platform and will continue to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund.

**[B. Expanded Key-Person Provisions in Side Letters]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding the absence of a Key Person Event under the LPA, certain side letters contain \"expanded key person\" provisions that extend the scope of the key person framework beyond the two designated Key Persons.

Six (6) of the Fund\'s fourteen (14) side letters contain expanded key person provisions that designate David Kellner as a \"Contributing Person.\" Under these side letter provisions, the departure of a Contributing Person triggers the following requirements:

> \(a\) **Notification Requirement:** The General Partner is required to provide written notification to the affected limited partner within fifteen (15) business days of the Contributing Person\'s departure or announcement of departure.
>
> \(b\) **Investment Period Suspension Right:** Three (3) of the six side letters containing expanded key person provisions grant the affected limited partner the right to request a suspension of the Fund\'s investment period for a period of ninety (90) days, during which time the LPAC will review the circumstances of the departure and determine whether any further action is warranted.

The General Partner has taken the following steps to comply with these side letter provisions:

> • Notification letters will be sent to each of the six affected limited partners within fifteen (15) business days of the announcement of Mr. Kellner\'s retirement, in compliance with the notification requirements of their respective side letters.
>
> • With respect to the three side letters that grant an investment period suspension right, the General Partner believes that the LPAC\'s consent to the restructuring, the orderly and planned nature of Mr. Kellner\'s retirement, his continued involvement with the platform as a Senior Advisor for a period of two years, and the promotion of Ms. Marchetti and Mr. Okonkwo to carry-bearing roles should address any concerns and obviate the need for any suspension of the investment period. The General Partner intends to engage proactively with the affected limited partners to discuss these matters and to respond to any questions or concerns.

The General Partner notes that Joanna Trask is not designated as a Contributing Person in any side letter, and accordingly her departure does not trigger any expanded key person provisions.

**[VIII. Side-Letter Compliance Summary]{.underline}**

**[A. Overview]{.underline}**

The Fund has fourteen (14) side letters currently in effect, covering a subset of the Fund\'s forty-seven (47) limited partners. Calderwood & Harkness LLP, in coordination with Pemberton Hale LLP (as the Fund\'s formation counsel), has conducted a comprehensive review of all fourteen side letters to identify any provisions that are implicated by the proposed restructuring.

**[B. Category-by-Category Analysis]{.underline}**

The following is a summary of the side letter provisions reviewed, organized by category, together with an assessment of the impact of the restructuring on each:

**1. Most Favored Nation (\"MFN\") Provisions (11 side letters):**

Eleven of the fourteen side letters contain MFN provisions entitling the applicable limited partner to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner (subject to customary carve-outs for terms related to tax, regulatory, or legal requirements specific to a particular investor). Calderwood & Harkness has reviewed the restructuring and has determined that no new \"most favored\" terms are being created by the restructuring that would trigger MFN obligations. The restructuring is an internal organizational matter among the principals and the General Partner and does not modify, amend, or supplement any term of any side letter or the LPA in a manner that would give rise to an MFN claim. No issues have been identified with respect to MFN compliance.

**2. Expanded Key-Person Provisions (6 side letters, naming Kellner as Contributing Person):**

As discussed in detail in Section VII.B above, six side letters contain expanded key person provisions designating David Kellner as a Contributing Person. Written notification to the affected limited partners is required within fifteen (15) business days of Mr. Kellner\'s departure, and three of the six side letters grant a ninety (90)-day investment period suspension right. The General Partner is taking all required actions to comply with these provisions.

**3. Fee discount or Rebate Provisions (8 side letters):**

Eight side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner a discount on management fees or a rebate of a portion of management fees (in each case, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the applicable side letter). The restructuring does not affect the management fee rate, the total management fee amount, or the calculation methodology for any fee discount or rebate. Accordingly, no fee discount or rebate provision is implicated by the restructuring, and no issues have been identified.

**4. Transfer/Restructuring Consent Requirements (4 side letters):**

Four side letters --- those entered into with the following limited partners --- contain provisions requiring prior written notice and, in certain cases, affirmative consent for any \"material change in the management structure\" of the Fund:

> \(a\) Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System
>
> \(b\) Pinnacle Insurance Group
>

>

The General Partner believes that the LPAC\'s consent to the restructuring, together with the direct notifications provided to each of the four limited partners, satisfies the consent and notification requirements of their respective side letters. In the event that any of the four limited partners raises an objection or requests additional information, the General Partner will engage with such limited partner to address its concerns promptly and in good faith.

**5. Co-Investment Priority Rights (9 side letters):**

Nine side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner priority rights or preferential access to co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund. The restructuring necessitates an update to the Fund\'s Co-Investment Allocation Policy to reflect the removal of David Kellner and Joanna Trask from co-investment eligibility (as they will no longer be principals of the platform) and the updated allocation percentages for the remaining and next-generation principals. The co-investment priority rights of the nine affected limited partners are not diminished or otherwise adversely affected by the restructuring, and no issues have been identified.

The proposed restructuring has been designed and structured to comply with all fourteen (14) side letters currently in effect. Required notifications are being sent within the timeframes prescribed by the applicable side letter provisions. No side-letter provision is anticipated to block or materially impede the restructuring. Calderwood & Harkness LLP will continue to monitor compliance with side-letter obligations throughout the implementation process and will work with Pemberton Hale LLP to ensure that all required actions are completed in a timely manner.

A summary matrix of the fourteen side letters, organized by provision category, is attached hereto as Appendix E.

Section 9.4 of the LPA requires the prior consent of the LPAC for certain material actions by the General Partner, including, without limitation, any material change in the management structure of the Fund. **[Section AA.5 --- Section 1061 Compliance]{.underline}**

This Section AA.5 is a new provision added by Calderwood & Harkness LLP.

\(a\) **Acknowledgment.** The General Partner acknowledges that the Carried Interest (both the Legacy Carry Tranche and the New Carry Tranche) constitutes an \"Applicable Partnership Interest\" within the meaning of Section 1061(c)(1) of the Code, and that the provisions of Section 1061 apply to the General Partner (and its individual members, to the extent they hold Applicable Partnership Interests) with respect to long-term capital gain allocated to, or recognized upon the disposition of, the Carried Interest.

\(b\) **Separate Tracking.** The General Partner shall maintain records sufficient to separately track the holding period of the Legacy Carry Tranche (commencing on or about December 2019; three-year holding period satisfied as of approximately December 2022) and the New Carry Tranche (commencing on the Final Closing Date, target October 31, 2025; three-year holding period to be satisfied on October 31, 2028), as required by Treasury Regulation Section 1.1061-4 and any successor guidance.

\(c\) **Recharacterization Reporting.** Any long-term capital gain allocated to the General Partner (or its individual members) with respect to the New Carry Tranche that is recognized prior to October 31, 2028 shall be reported on the Partnership\'s Schedule K-1 (and on the individual Schedule K-1s of the General Partner\'s members, as applicable) as subject to recharacterization as short-term capital gain under Section 1061(a), unless an exception to Section 1061 applies (such as the capital interest exception under Section 1061(c)(4) or the exception for gain from assets not held for portfolio investment purposes).

\(d\) **Required Disclosures.** The General Partner shall cause the Partnership to furnish to each holder of an Applicable Partnership Interest (and to the Internal Revenue Service) the information required by Section 1061(d) of the Code and Treasury Regulation Section 1.1061-6 (or any successor regulation), including, without limitation:

> \(i\) the \"API 1-Year Distributive Share Amount\" (within the meaning of Treasury Regulation Section 1.1061-3(c)(1)), being the amount of net long-term capital gain allocated to the holder that would be recharacterized as short-term capital gain if a one-year holding period were applied in lieu of the three-year holding period;
>
> \(ii\) the \"API 3-Year Distributive Share Amount\" (within the meaning of Treasury Regulation Section 1.1061-3(c)(2)), being the amount of net long-term capital gain allocated to the holder that would be recharacterized as short-term capital gain under Section 1061(a) because the three-year holding period has not been satisfied; and
>
> \(iii\) such other information as the Internal Revenue Service may require by form, instruction, or other guidance.

\(e\) **Capital Interest Exception for GP Co-Invest.** The GP Co-Invest of \$14,000,000 shall not be treated as an Applicable Partnership Interest to the extent it represents a capital interest in the Partnership that was acquired in exchange for a capital contribution of money (and not in connection with the performance of services), and to the extent such capital interest qualifies for the exception set forth in Section 1061(c)(4) of the Code. The General Partner shall maintain records demonstrating (i) the amount of the GP Co-Invest capital contribution, (ii) the Partnership Interest received in exchange therefor, and (iii) that allocations and distributions with respect to such Partnership Interest are made in the same manner as allocations and distributions with respect to other non-service partnership interests of a similar class. The GP Co-Invest interest shall be clearly identified as a capital interest (and not an Applicable Partnership Interest) on the Partnership\'s books and records and on the applicable Schedule K-1s.

**[Section AA.6 --- Withholding and Indemnification]{.underline}**

**Section AA.6(a) --- Section 1446 Withholding (ECI Withholding on Non-U.S. Partners)**

\(i\) The Partnership is authorized and required to withhold and remit to the Internal Revenue Service such amounts as are required to be withheld under Section 1446 of the Code (and the Treasury Regulations thereunder) with respect to any Non-U.S. Partner\'s allocable share of the Partnership\'s income that is, or is treated as, Effectively Connected Income (ECI). The applicable withholding rate under Section 1446 is the highest rate of tax specified in Section 1 of the Code (for individual Non-U.S. Partners) or Section 11 of the Code (for corporate Non-U.S. Partners), applied to the Non-U.S. Partner\'s allocable share of ECI.

\(ii\) Any amount withheld pursuant to this Section AA.6(a) shall be treated as a distribution to the affected Non-U.S. Partner for purposes of this Agreement and shall reduce subsequent distributions otherwise payable to such Non-U.S. Partner under the distribution waterfall in Section Z.1.

\(iii\) Each Non-U.S. Partner shall furnish to the Partnership a properly completed and executed Form W-8BEN, Form W-8BEN-E, or other applicable Form W-8, as appropriate, on or before the date such Non-U.S. Partner is admitted to the Partnership, and shall update such form as required by applicable law (generally, every three years or upon a change in circumstances). A Non-U.S. Partner\'s failure to timely provide an accurate Form W-8 shall entitle the Partnership to withhold at the maximum applicable rate, without regard to any reduced rate that might otherwise be available under an applicable income tax treaty.

\*\*\[C&H Comment: The Offshore blocker (PCV International Holdings Ltd.) is specifically designed to block ECI from flowing through to Non-U.S. Partners, including Sovereign Capital Partners (Cayman) Ltd. (commitment of \$75,000,000). If the Offshore blocker is properly interposed and functioning as intended, the Offshore blocker (as a foreign corporation) will be the \"partner\" for purposes of Section 1446, and the Offshore blocker itself will be subject to U.S. federal income tax on any ECI allocated to it (filing Form 1120-F). Non-U.S. Partners investing through the Offshore blocker should not themselves be treated as receiving ECI allocations, and Section 1446 withholding should not apply at the investor level. **[Section AA.7 --- Section 707 Disguised Sale Protections]{.underline}**

This Section AA.7 is a new provision added by Calderwood & Harkness LLP.

\(a\) **Intent.** It is the intent of the parties that the contribution of the Contributed Assets by the Rolling LPs (through and together with Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP) to the Partnership in exchange for Partnership Interests, and the concurrent admission of the Secondary Investors (including Garrison Secondaries Fund IV LP) to the Partnership in exchange for cash capital contributions, shall be treated as a tax-free contribution under Section 721 of the Code and shall *not* be treated as a \"disguised sale\" of the Contributed Assets by the Rolling LPs to the Partnership (or to the Secondary Investors) under Section 707(a)(2)(B) of the Code and the Treasury Regulations promulgated thereunder (Treasury Regulation Sections 1.707-3 through 1.707-9).

\(b\) **Liability Allocations.** The General Partner shall allocate partnership liabilities under Section 752 of the Code and the Treasury Regulations thereunder (including Treasury Regulation Sections 1.752-1 through 1.752-7) to the Rolling LPs in an amount sufficient to support the non-recognition treatment of the contribution and, to the extent any liabilities encumber the Contributed Assets or are assumed by the Partnership in connection with the contribution, to establish that the \"qualified liability\" exception under Treasury Regulation Section 1.707-5(a)(6) applies to such liabilities.

\(c\) **Two-Year Presumption.** No distribution, payment, or other transfer of money or property shall be made to a Rolling LP within two (2) years of the date of the contribution of the Contributed Assets to the Partnership (the \"Two-Year Period\") if such distribution, payment, or transfer would, together with other facts and circumstances, create a presumption of a disguised sale under Treasury Regulation Section 1.707-3(c) (which provides that a transfer made within two years of a contribution is presumed to be a sale unless the facts and circumstances clearly establish otherwise), *except* to the extent that: (i) such distribution constitutes a Tax Distribution under Section Z.4; (ii) such distribution is a return of the Rolling LP\'s Capital Contribution in connection with the winding up of the Partnership; or (iii) the General Partner, based on advice from nationally recognized tax counsel (which may include Calderwood & Harkness LLP), determines in good faith that the distribution would not be treated as part of a disguised sale under the facts-and-circumstances analysis of Treasury Regulation Section 1.707-3(b).

\(d\) **Tax Protection Agreement.** The protections set forth in this Section AA.7 are in addition to, and are not intended to limit, the protections set forth in the Tax Protection Agreement among the Partnership, the General Partner, and the Rolling LPs (a separate document to be executed concurrently with this Agreement), which provides for, among other things, minimum holding periods for the Contributed Assets, liability allocation commitments, and indemnification of the Rolling LPs in the event of gain recognition resulting from the Partnership\'s actions.

**[Section AA.8 --- Section 752 Liability Allocations]{.underline}**

\(a\) All liabilities of the Partnership (including recourse liabilities, nonrecourse liabilities, and partner nonrecourse liabilities, as such terms are defined in Treasury Regulation Section 1.752-1) shall be allocated among the Partners in accordance with Sections 752 and 704 of the Code and the Treasury Regulations promulgated thereunder.

\(b\) To the extent the Partnership incurs any debt during the term of the Partnership (including, without limitation, borrowings under any subscription credit facility, bridge financing, or follow-on investment borrowing from the \$100,000,000 follow-on investment reserve), the General Partner shall allocate such debt among the Partners in a manner that is: (i) consistent with the disguised sale protections set forth in Section AA.7 and the tax protection commitments to the Rolling LPs set forth in the Tax Protection Agreement; (ii) consistent with the economic risk of loss (for recourse liabilities) or profit-sharing ratios (for nonrecourse liabilities) of the Partners, as determined in accordance with the Treasury Regulations; and (iii) calculated to minimize, to the extent reasonably practicable, the risk of any constructive distribution to the Rolling LPs under Section 752(b) of the Code that could trigger gain recognition under Section 731(a).

\(c\) The General Partner shall provide each Partner with a schedule setting forth such Partner\'s share of the Partnership\'s liabilities (for purposes of Section 752 of the Code) within sixty (60) days following the close of each fiscal year, or within thirty (30) days following any material change in the Partnership\'s liabilities.

**[Section BB.1 --- Domestic blocker (PCV Domestic blocker Inc.)]{.underline}**

This Article BB is a new provision added by Calderwood & Harkness LLP. The Hawthorne Reid draft contained a brief reference to the possible use of blocker entities, but did not include detailed provisions governing their formation, capitalization, or operation. Given the significance of the blocker structures to the tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors in the Partnership, comprehensive provisions are warranted.

\(a\) **Formation.** PCV Domestic blocker Inc. (the \"Domestic blocker\") shall be formed as a C-corporation under the laws of the State of Delaware on or before September 30, 2025. The General Partner shall cause the Domestic blocker to be formed and to obtain an employer identification number (EIN) from the Internal Revenue Service prior to the Initial Closing Date.

\(b\) **Purpose.** The Domestic blocker is interposed between the Partnership and the Tax-Exempt Partners for the purpose of blocking unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") under Section 512 of the Code (including debt-financed income under Section 514 of the Code) that would otherwise flow through to such Tax-Exempt Partners from income allocated by the Partnership. The Tax-Exempt Partners that will invest through the Domestic blocker are:

> \(i\) Meridian Public Employees\' Retirement System, with a capital commitment of \$125,000,000; and
>
> \(ii\) Ashford University Endowment, with a capital commitment of \$50,000,000;
>
> representing an aggregate capital commitment of \$175,000,000 to be channeled through the Domestic blocker.

\(c\) **Capitalization.** The Domestic blocker shall be capitalized with capital contributions from the Tax-Exempt Partners in exchange for shares of common stock (or such other class of equity securities as the General Partner determines is appropriate) of the Domestic blocker. The Domestic blocker shall in turn use such capital contributions to acquire a limited partnership interest in the Partnership in an amount equal to the aggregate capital contributed by the Tax-Exempt Partners.

\(d\) **Tax Treatment.** The Domestic blocker, as a C-corporation, shall be subject to corporate-level U.S. federal income tax on its allocable share of Partnership income at the applicable corporate tax rate (currently twenty-one percent (21%)). Distributions from the Domestic blocker to the Tax-Exempt Partners shall be treated as dividends to the extent of the Domestic blocker\'s current and accumulated earnings and profits (E&P), and as a return of capital to the extent of the Tax-Exempt Partner\'s basis in its shares of the Domestic blocker, and as capital gain thereafter. Dividend distributions received by a Tax-Exempt Partner from the Domestic blocker should not constitute UBTI (provided that the Tax-Exempt Partner\'s stock in the Domestic blocker is not \"debt-financed property\" within the meaning of Section 514 of the Code), and therefore the Domestic blocker should effectively \[DELETED: block\] \[ADDED: block\] UBTI from reaching the Tax-Exempt Partners.

\(e\) **Corporate-Level Tax Leakage.** The parties acknowledge and agree that the use of the Domestic blocker results in a layer of corporate-level income tax on Partnership income that is allocable to the Domestic blocker, which represents \"tax leakage\" that reduces the after-tax return to the Tax-Exempt Partners. Specifically, income allocated to the Domestic blocker will be taxed at the corporate level (21%), and distributions from the Domestic blocker to the Tax-Exempt Partners may be further subject to state-level taxes, resulting in an aggregate tax burden that the Tax-Exempt Partners would not bear if they invested directly (absent UBTI concerns). The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize such tax leakage through tax-efficient structuring of dispositions of Portfolio Company investments (including, without limitation, installment sales, like-kind exchanges to the extent available under the Code, and timing of gain recognition events to align with the Domestic blocker\'s overall tax position), but does not guarantee any particular level of tax efficiency.

\(f\) **Governance.** The Domestic blocker shall be managed by a board of directors consisting of one or more individuals designated by the General Partner. The board of directors of the Domestic blocker shall have such authority as is necessary to manage the affairs of the Domestic blocker, including the authority to cause the Domestic blocker to make capital contributions to the Partnership, to receive distributions from the Partnership, and to make distributions to the Domestic blocker\'s stockholders (the Tax-Exempt Partners). The Domestic blocker shall not engage in any business or activity other than holding its limited partnership interest in the Partnership and ancillary activities related thereto.
