**[LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE CHARTER AND TERMS OF REFERENCE]{.underline}**

**HARROWGATE PRIVATE EQUITY FUND V LP** a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Fund\")

**General Partner:** Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"General Partner\"), whose sole member is Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"Sponsor\")

**Effective as of the date of the First Close** (Target: August 15, 2025)

This Limited Partner Advisory Committee Charter and Terms of Reference (this \"Charter\") is adopted by the General Partner of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership, pursuant to Section 11.1 of the Agreement of Limited Partnership of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, dated as of August 15, 2025 (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"Partnership Agreement\" or \"LPA\").

Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings given to them in the Partnership Agreement. This Charter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflicts of law principles.

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**[ARTICLE I --- PURPOSE AND ESTABLISHMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1 --- Establishment of the LPAC**

The General Partner hereby establishes a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\" or the \"Committee\") for Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP. The LPAC is established to serve in a consultative and advisory capacity to the General Partner on certain matters as set forth herein and in the Partnership Agreement, and to foster transparency and constructive dialogue between the General Partner and the Fund\'s Limited Partners regarding Fund governance, potential conflicts of interest, and other matters of significance to the Fund\'s investor base.

The LPAC is not a governing body of the Fund and does not have the authority to manage, control, or direct the business and affairs of the Fund, which authority is vested exclusively in the General Partner pursuant to the Partnership Agreement and applicable Delaware law, including the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 *et seq.*). The establishment of the LPAC shall not alter or diminish the powers and authority of the General Partner as set forth in the Partnership Agreement or give rise to any inference that the LPAC exercises control over, or participates in the control of, the Fund\'s business.

**Section 1.2 --- Purpose**

The LPAC is established for the following purposes:

> \(a\) To review and, where required by the Partnership Agreement, approve or consent to certain transactions and matters involving actual or potential conflicts of interest between the General Partner (or its affiliates, principals, or related persons) and the Fund or the Limited Partners;
>
> \(b\) To consult on valuation matters referred to it by the General Partner, including the review of valuation methodologies and conclusions presented by the General Partner on at least an annual basis;
>
> \(c\) To approve or consent to certain waivers of investment restrictions and guidelines as set forth in the Partnership Agreement, upon the request of the General Partner;
>
> \(d\) To approve or consent to extensions of the Fund Term beyond those that the General Partner is entitled to effect at its sole discretion under the Partnership Agreement;
>
> \(e\) To serve as a forum for communication and consultation between the General Partner and the Limited Partners on matters of Fund governance, operations, fees and expenses, and such other matters as the General Partner may, in its discretion, bring before the LPAC; and
>
> \(f\) To perform such other advisory functions as are contemplated by the Partnership Agreement or this Charter.

For the avoidance of doubt, the LPAC\'s role is advisory and consultative in nature, except where the Partnership Agreement expressly requires the LPAC\'s approval or consent as a condition to the General Partner taking or refraining from taking a specified action. Fiduciary duties do not attach to LPAC Members in their capacity as such, and LPAC Members shall not be deemed to be agents, trustees, or fiduciaries of the Fund, the General Partner, or any other Limited Partner by reason of their service on the LPAC.

**[ARTICLE II --- COMPOSITION AND MEMBERSHIP]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Number of Members**

The LPAC shall consist of five (5) members (each, a \"Member\" and, collectively, the \"Members\"). Three (3) Members shall be designated at the First Close of the Fund. The remaining two (2) Members shall be designated by the General Partner, in consultation with the existing Members, at subsequent closings or as vacancies arise, but in any event no later than the Final Close Deadline (February 15, 2027). In the period between the First Close and the designation of the fourth and fifth Members, the LPAC shall function with three (3) Members, and all quorum and voting thresholds shall be adjusted accordingly as set forth in Article III.

**Section 2.2 --- Initial Members**

The following Limited Partners (or their designated representatives) are anticipated to be designated as the initial three (3) Members of the LPAC at the First Close:

> \(a\) **Northmoor State Pension System** (anticipated capital commitment: \$200,000,000) --- designated representative: Helen T. Barrows, Director of Private Markets;
>
> \(b\) **Edgecombe Insurance Group Ltd.** (anticipated capital commitment: \$150,000,000) --- designated representative: Alastair G. Dunmore, Head of Alternative Investments; and
>
> \(c\) **The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund** (anticipated capital commitment: \$100,000,000) --- designated representative: Dr. Philip W. Sheng, Chief Investment Officer.

Each initial Member\'s appointment to the LPAC is subject to confirmation upon such Member\'s execution and delivery of its respective Subscription Agreement and any applicable Side Letter to the General Partner. In the event that any anticipated initial Member does not execute a Subscription Agreement at or prior to the First Close, the General Partner shall designate a replacement Member from among the Limited Partners admitted at the First Close.

**Section 2.3 --- Selection Criteria**

Members shall be selected from among Limited Partners with meaningful capital commitments to the Fund. In selecting Members, the General Partner shall endeavor to maintain a diverse and representative LPAC that reflects the breadth and composition of the Fund\'s investor base, including, as applicable, representation from among pension plans, endowments and foundations, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, funds of funds, family offices, and other institutional investors.

LPAC membership is available to investors in the Main Fund (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP), the Parallel Fund (Harrowgate Fund V Parallel LP), and the Offshore Feeder (Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP), as each such vehicle invests alongside the Main Fund on a pro rata basis and participates in the same investment program. A Limited Partner\'s membership in the LPAC shall not be conditioned upon its investment through any particular vehicle within the fund complex.

**Section 2.4 --- Observer Status**

The General Partner may, in its sole discretion, grant observer status to one or more Limited Partners, permitting such Limited Partners (through their designated representatives) to attend LPAC meetings in a non-voting, advisory capacity. Observers shall not be counted for purposes of determining a quorum and shall not have the right to vote on any matter presented to the LPAC, but may participate in discussions at the invitation of the General Partner or the Members. Observers shall be bound by the same confidentiality obligations applicable to Members as set forth in Article VII of this Charter.

The General Partner acknowledges that certain Side Letters may provide for LPAC observer rights. By way of example, the Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority has been granted LPAC observer rights pursuant to its negotiated Side Letter, and such rights shall be honored in accordance with the terms thereof, subject to the confidentiality and other provisions of this Charter.

**Section 2.5 --- Designated Representatives**

Each Member shall designate one (1) individual to serve as its representative on the LPAC (the \"Designated Representative\") and one (1) alternate representative (the \"Alternate Representative\"). The Designated Representative shall be the primary attendee at LPAC meetings and shall have full authority to act and vote on behalf of such Member. In the absence or unavailability of the Designated Representative, the Alternate Representative shall be entitled to attend and participate in meetings and to cast votes on behalf of such Member with the same authority as the Designated Representative.

All designations and changes of Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives shall be communicated in writing (including by email) to the General Partner, to the attention of Rachel M. Overton, Partner, Head of Investor Relations, Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, and shall be effective upon receipt by the General Partner. The General Partner shall maintain a current register of Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives.

**Section 2.6 --- Term of Membership**

Each Member shall serve on the LPAC for the duration of the Fund Term (including any extension thereof), unless such Member earlier resigns, is removed, or ceases to be a Limited Partner in the Fund (including by reason of a full transfer of its limited partnership interest in the Fund). A Member that transfers all of its limited partnership interest in the Fund (whether pursuant to a secondary sale or otherwise) shall automatically cease to be a Member of the LPAC effective as of the date of such transfer, without the necessity of any further action by the General Partner or the LPAC.

A Member that transfers a portion, but not all, of its limited partnership interest in the Fund shall retain its LPAC membership, provided that such Member continues to hold a limited partnership interest in the Fund following such partial transfer.

**Section 2.7 --- Resignation and Removal**

> \(a\) **Resignation.** A Member may resign from the LPAC at any time by delivering written notice of resignation to the General Partner. Such resignation shall be effective upon receipt by the General Partner or such later date as may be specified in the notice.
>
> \(b\) **Removal.** The General Partner may replace a Member upon the occurrence of any of the following events:
>
> \(i\) such Member ceases to hold any limited partnership interest in the Fund (including by reason of a full transfer of its interest);
>
> \(ii\) such Member becomes subject to a Bankruptcy Event (as defined in the Partnership Agreement);
>
> \(iii\) such Member (or its Designated Representative or Alternate Representative) fails to attend three (3) consecutive regularly scheduled meetings of the LPAC without designating an alternate or otherwise providing prior notice of non-attendance to the General Partner; or
>
> \(iv\) such Member materially breaches its confidentiality obligations under Article VII of this Charter and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days following written notice from the General Partner specifying the nature of such breach.
>
> \(c\) **Process.** Replacement Members shall be selected by the General Partner in consultation with the remaining LPAC Members. The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that the composition of the LPAC continues to satisfy the diversity and representativeness objectives set forth in Section 2.3.

**Section 2.8 --- Vacancies**

Vacancies on the LPAC arising from resignation, removal, or any other cause shall be filled by the General Partner after consultation with the existing Members. The General Partner shall endeavor to fill any vacancy within sixty (60) days of the date on which such vacancy arises. During any period in which a vacancy exists and the remaining number of Members is fewer than five (5), the LPAC shall continue to function, and quorum and voting thresholds shall be determined by reference to the number of Members then serving.

**[ARTICLE III --- MEETINGS]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Frequency**

The LPAC shall meet at least two (2) times per calendar year at such times as the General Partner shall determine. Additional meetings may be called by the General Partner at any time, or upon the written request of at least two (2) Members specifying the purpose of the requested meeting. The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to schedule meetings at times that accommodate the schedules of the Members. The General Partner\'s principal contact for LPAC coordination and scheduling shall be Rachel M. Overton, Partner, Head of Investor Relations, Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC (email: r.overton@harrowgatecapital.com; telephone: (302) 555-1200).

**Section 3.2 --- Notice**

The General Partner shall provide not less than fifteen (15) business days\' prior written notice of each regularly scheduled meeting and not less than five (5) business days\' prior written notice of each special meeting. Each notice of meeting shall include a proposed agenda, the date, time, and location (or videoconference/teleconference dial-in information) of the meeting, and any materials to be considered at the meeting. Notice may be delivered by email to each Member\'s Designated Representative (and Alternate Representative) at the email address on file with the General Partner.

In the event of exigent circumstances requiring urgent LPAC action (for example, a time-sensitive conflict-of-interest transaction), the General Partner may provide shorter notice, provided that the General Partner uses commercially reasonable efforts to provide as much advance notice as is practicable under the circumstances and that no fewer than two (2) business days\' notice is given.

**Section 3.3 --- Format**

Meetings of the LPAC may be held in person at the offices of Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC at 1200 Concord Pike, Suite 600, Wilmington, Delaware 19803, or at such other location as designated by the General Partner, or by teleconference or videoconference, or any combination thereof. Members may participate in any meeting by means of conference telephone, video conferencing platform (e.g., Calderon Software, Northgate Data Systems), or similar communications equipment that allows all participants to hear each other at the same time, and such participation shall constitute presence in person at such meeting for all purposes under this Charter.

The General Partner shall make reasonable accommodations for Members located in different time zones, including, without limitation, by rotating meeting times or scheduling meetings during business hours that are reasonably convenient for Members in multiple jurisdictions.

**Section 3.4 --- Quorum**

A quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the Members then serving. By way of illustration, when all five (5) seats on the LPAC are filled, a quorum shall consist of three (3) Members; when only three (3) seats are filled (as may be the case between the First Close and the designation of the fourth and fifth Members), a quorum shall consist of two (2) Members. For purposes of determining a quorum, a Member shall be deemed present if the Member\'s Designated Representative or Alternate Representative is in attendance (whether in person, by teleconference, or by videoconference). Observers shall not be counted for purposes of determining a quorum.

No action may be taken at a meeting at which a quorum is not present, except to adjourn the meeting to a later date. In the event a quorum is not present, the Members present may adjourn the meeting to a date not more than fifteen (15) business days later, and the General Partner shall provide notice of such adjourned meeting to all Members not in attendance.

**Section 3.5 --- Voting and Action**

Each Member shall have one (1) vote on each matter submitted to the LPAC for a vote, regardless of the size of such Member\'s capital commitment to the Fund. Except as otherwise expressly provided herein or in the Partnership Agreement, actions of the LPAC shall require the affirmative vote of a majority of the Members present at a meeting at which a quorum is constituted.

Action may be taken by the LPAC without a meeting by unanimous written consent, circulated by the General Partner and executed (including by electronic signature or email confirmation) by all Members then serving. Any action so taken shall have the same force and effect as if taken at a duly convened meeting of the LPAC. The General Partner shall retain the original or electronic copies of all written consents in the Fund\'s records.

In the event of a tie vote (which may occur if the LPAC has an even number of Members then serving due to a vacancy), the matter in question shall be deemed not approved, and the General Partner may request that the matter be reconsidered at a subsequent meeting or by written consent.

**Section 3.6 --- Agenda and Materials**

The General Partner shall prepare and circulate the agenda for each meeting of the LPAC together with the notice of such meeting. Any Member may request that items be added to the agenda by written notice to the General Partner delivered at least five (5) business days before the meeting. The General Partner shall use reasonable efforts to accommodate such requests but reserves the right to defer items to a subsequent meeting if, in the General Partner\'s reasonable judgment, the requested item is not time-sensitive or if adequate materials cannot be prepared in advance.

The General Partner shall provide Members with relevant materials in advance of the meeting, including, as applicable, conflict-of-interest descriptions and analyses, valuation reports and summaries, supporting documentation for any matter requiring LPAC approval or consent, portfolio summaries, fee and expense reports, and such other information as the General Partner deems appropriate or as any Member may reasonably request. To the extent practicable, materials shall be provided at least five (5) business days in advance of the meeting to afford Members adequate time for review.

**Section 3.7 --- Minutes**

The General Partner (or its designee) shall prepare minutes of each meeting of the LPAC. Minutes shall include a summary of the matters discussed, the text of any resolutions adopted, the vote of each Member on each matter submitted to a vote, and a record of attendance. Draft minutes shall be circulated to all Members who attended the meeting for review within twenty (20) business days following the meeting. Members shall have ten (10) business days from receipt of draft minutes to submit comments or corrections. Minutes shall be finalized upon the approval of a majority of the Members who attended the meeting to which the minutes relate. Finalized minutes shall be maintained by the General Partner as part of the Fund\'s books and records.

**Section 3.8 --- Attendance by General Partner and Advisors**

Representatives of the General Partner and the Sponsor, including Marcus J. Harrowgate (Managing Partner), Diana R. Castellano (Partner, Co-Head of Investments), Jonathan P. Birch (Partner), and Catherine E. Loomis (General Counsel & Chief Compliance Officer), may attend all meetings of the LPAC in a non-voting capacity and shall be available to respond to questions and present information to the Members.

The General Partner may invite Fund counsel (Calderwood & Harkness LLP), the Fund auditor (Caldwell, Fitch & Hartley LLP), the fund administrator (Pinnacle Fund Services LLC), or other advisors to attend meetings or portions thereof as reasonably necessary in connection with matters on the agenda. The General Partner shall inform the Members in advance of the identities of any non-Member attendees expected at a meeting.

The LPAC may request that certain portions of a meeting be held without representatives of the General Partner present (an \"Executive Session\"). In such event, the General Partner and its representatives shall withdraw from the meeting for the duration of the Executive Session. The Members present during the Executive Session may request that notes of any matters discussed or actions taken during the Executive Session be included (or excluded, as applicable) in the formal minutes. The General Partner shall cooperate in good faith with any reasonable request for an Executive Session.

**[ARTICLE IV --- SCOPE OF AUTHORITY AND RESPONSIBILITIES]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Conflict of Interest Approvals**

The LPAC shall review and, where required by the Partnership Agreement, approve or consent to transactions involving actual or potential conflicts of interest between the General Partner (or its affiliates, principals, or related persons) and the Fund or the Limited Partners. Such conflicts of interest transactions include, but are not limited to, the following:

> \(a\) **Co-Investment by the General Partner or Affiliates.** Co-investment transactions in which the General Partner, the Sponsor, any principal thereof, or any affiliate invests alongside the Fund on  by the General Partner. Members seeking reimbursement shall submit documentation of such expenses to the General Partner in accordance with the Fund\'s expense reimbursement policies.

Any engagement of independent advisors by the LPAC, including independent valuation firms, legal counsel, or other professionals, shall require the prior written consent of the General Partner (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), and the costs thereof shall be borne by the Fund as a Fund expense. The General Partner shall cooperate with the LPAC in the selection and engagement of any such independent advisors.

**[ARTICLE VII --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Confidentiality Obligations**

Each Member (and each observer) shall maintain the confidentiality of all non-public information received in connection with its service on the LPAC (\"Confidential Information\"), including, but not limited to:

> \(a\) portfolio company financial information, operating data, and business plans;
>
> \(b\) valuation data, methodologies, models, and conclusions;
>
> \(c\) co-investment opportunities, deal pipeline information, and term sheets;
>
> \(d\) conflict-of-interest disclosures and the substance of any LPAC deliberations related thereto;
>
> \(e\) Fund financial statements, performance data, IRRs, multiples, and capital account information;
>
> \(f\) information relating to the identity, capital commitments, or investment terms of other Limited Partners; and
>
> \(g\) any other proprietary, trade secret, or confidential information of the Fund, the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any portfolio company.

Each Member shall use Confidential Information solely for purposes of fulfilling its responsibilities as a Member of the LPAC and shall not disclose Confidential Information to any third party except as permitted under Section 7.2. Each Member shall take reasonable precautions to protect the confidentiality of Confidential Information, using at least the same degree of care that such Member uses to protect its own confidential information of similar importance.

**Section 7.2 --- Exceptions**

The confidentiality obligations set forth in Section 7.1 shall not apply to information:

> \(a\) that is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Charter or any other confidentiality obligation owed to the Fund or the General Partner;
>
> \(b\) that was known to the Member prior to its receipt from the Fund or the General Partner, as demonstrated by the Member\'s written records, without breach of any other confidentiality obligation;
>
> \(c\) that is independently developed by the Member without use of or reference to Confidential Information;
>
> \(d\) that is required to be disclosed by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, or by a governmental or regulatory authority having jurisdiction over the Member, including, without limitation, disclosures required under state or federal public records laws, freedom of information acts, or similar statutes applicable to governmental plan investors (such as Northmoor State Pension System) or sovereign investors (such as Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority), *provided* that the Member shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide the General Partner with prompt prior written notice of such required disclosure so that the General Partner may seek an appropriate protective order or other remedy;
>
> \(e\) that is disclosed to the Member\'s professional advisors, auditors, internal and external legal counsel, consultants, or other agents on a need-to-know basis and subject to confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth herein; or
>
> \(f\) that is disclosed pursuant to the terms of a Side Letter entered into between the General Partner and the applicable Member or the applicable Member\'s governing body or oversight agency.

**Section 7.3 --- Duration**

The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article VII shall survive the termination and winding up of the Fund for a period of two (2) years following the date of final liquidating distributions to the Limited Partners.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- LIABILITY AND INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- No Fiduciary Duty**

LPAC Members do not owe fiduciary duties to the Fund, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner by reason of their service on the LPAC. LPAC Members act solely in their capacity as representatives of their respective Limited Partners, and their service on the LPAC shall not create or be deemed to create a relationship of principal and agent, trustee and beneficiary, or any other fiduciary relationship between such Members and the Fund, the General Partner, any other Limited Partner, or any portfolio company. This Section 8.1 is consistent with and supplements the elimination and modification of fiduciary duties set forth in the Partnership Agreement to the fullest extent permitted by the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act.

**Section 8.2 --- Limitation of Liability**

No Member shall be liable to the Fund, the General Partner, any Limited Partner, or any other person for any act or omission taken or suffered in good faith in connection with its service on the LPAC, including any approval, consent, waiver, recommendation, vote, or abstention given, withheld, or made, except in the case of such Member\'s fraud, willful misconduct, or bad faith. No Member shall be liable for any action or inaction of the General Partner, for the investment decisions of the Fund, or for the performance of any portfolio investment, whether or not such action, inaction, or decision was the subject of LPAC review or approval.

The foregoing limitation of liability shall apply to the fullest extent permitted by applicable Delaware law and shall be in addition to (and not in limitation of) any limitation of liability afforded to the Member in its capacity as a Limited Partner under the Partnership Agreement or applicable law.

**Section 8.3 --- Indemnification**

The Fund shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless each Member and its Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives (collectively, \"Indemnified LPAC Persons\") against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, judgments, fines, penalties, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses of investigation) arising out of or relating to such Indemnified LPAC Person\'s service on the LPAC, to the fullest extent permitted by the Partnership Agreement and applicable Delaware law, except to the extent that such losses, claims, damages, liabilities, or expenses result from the Indemnified LPAC Person\'s fraud, willful misconduct, or bad faith.

Indemnification obligations under this Section 8.3 are obligations of the Fund (and, accordingly, are borne indirectly by the Limited Partners as Fund expenses) and not of the General Partner individually, except as may otherwise be provided in the Partnership Agreement. The procedures for asserting and processing indemnification claims shall be as set forth in the Partnership Agreement.

**Section 8.4 --- Insurance**

The General Partner may, in its discretion, cause the Fund to obtain directors\' and officers\' liability insurance or similar liability insurance covering LPAC Members and their Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives in connection with their service on the LPAC, the cost of which shall be borne as a Fund expense. The General Partner shall inform the LPAC of the existence, scope, and material terms of any such insurance policy upon request.

**[ARTICLE IX --- AMENDMENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Amendment Procedure**

This Charter may be amended, modified, or supplemented by the General Partner with the prior approval of a majority of the LPAC Members then serving. All amendments shall be in writing and shall be effective upon execution by the General Partner and delivery of written notice to all Members (and observers, if applicable). No amendment to this Charter shall diminish the rights of any Member under this Charter without such Member\'s prior written consent, unless such diminution applies equally to all Members.

For the avoidance of doubt, amendments to the Partnership Agreement that affect the authority, composition, or responsibilities of the LPAC shall be governed by the amendment provisions of the Partnership Agreement, and any resulting changes to this Charter shall be adopted in accordance with this Section 9.1.

**[ARTICLE X --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Governing Law**

This Charter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflicts of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

**Section 10.2 --- Dispute Resolution**

Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising under, out of, or in connection with this Charter, including any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination, shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware lacks subject matter jurisdiction, the Superior Court of the State of Delaware, New Castle County), consistent with the dispute resolution provisions of the Partnership Agreement. Each Member, by accepting appointment to the LPAC, consents to the personal jurisdiction of such courts and waives any objection to venue therein.

**Section 10.3 --- Relationship to Partnership Agreement**

This Charter is supplemental to and subject to the Partnership Agreement in all respects. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the provisions of this Charter and the provisions of the Partnership Agreement, the Partnership Agreement shall control and govern. References herein to sections of the Partnership Agreement are to the corresponding sections of the Agreement of Limited Partnership of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time.

**Section 10.4 --- Notices**

All notices, requests, demands, consents, and other communications under this Charter shall be delivered in writing to the addresses (including email addresses) set forth in each Member\'s Subscription Agreement or as subsequently updated in writing by the applicable Member to the General Partner. Notices shall be deemed delivered upon receipt (or, in the case of email, upon transmission without receipt of an automated delivery failure notification).

Notices to the General Partner shall be delivered to:

**[ARTICLE XII --- REPORTING AND INFORMATION RIGHTS]{.underline}**

**[Section 12.1 --- Financial Statements]{.underline}**

\(a\) **Annual Financial Statements.** The General Partner shall cause to be prepared and delivered to each Partner annual financial statements of the Partnership, prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (\"U.S. GAAP\"), audited by Whitfield & Pratt LLP (or such other nationally recognized independent public accounting firm as the General Partner may select). Such annual audited financial statements shall be delivered to each Partner within one hundred twenty (120) days following the end of each fiscal year. The annual financial statements shall include a balance sheet, a statement of operations, a statement of changes in partners\' capital, a statement of cash flows, and the notes thereto.

\(b\) **Quarterly Financial Statements.** The General Partner shall cause to be prepared and delivered to each Partner quarterly unaudited financial statements of the Partnership, including a summary net asset value (\"NAV\") report, within sixty (60) days following the end of each calendar quarter. Quarterly financial statements shall be prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP on a basis consistent with the annual financial statements.

\(c\) **Fund Administration.** Fund administration, accounting, and NAV calculations shall be performed by Halcyon Fund Services, Inc. or such other fund administrator as the General Partner may engage from time to time.

**[Section 12.2 --- Tax Reporting]{.underline}**

\(a\) The General Partner shall cause to be prepared and delivered to each Partner a Schedule K-1 (or equivalent) reflecting such Partner\'s allocable share of the Partnership\'s items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit for each fiscal year, within ninety (90) days following the end of such fiscal year (target delivery: March 31 of the following year).

\(b\) Tax preparation and advisory services for the Partnership shall be coordinated by Greystone Tax Advisors LLC or such other tax advisor as the General Partner may engage from time to time.

\(c\) The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide each Partner with such additional tax information as may be reasonably requested by such Partner or as may be required for such Partner to prepare its own tax returns.

**[Section 12.3 --- Investor Reports]{.underline}**

\(a\) **Quarterly Portfolio Reports.** The General Partner shall cause to be prepared and delivered to each Partner a quarterly portfolio report within sixty (60) days following the end of each calendar quarter. Each quarterly portfolio report shall include (i) a summary of investment activity during the quarter (including new investments, follow-on investments, and realizations), (ii) portfolio valuations (at fair value in accordance with ASC 820), (iii) Capital Account balances for each Partner, and (iv) a summary of fees and expenses charged to the Partnership during the quarter.

\(b\) **Annual Meeting or Report.** The General Partner shall hold an annual meeting of the Limited Partners (in person, by video conference, or by teleconference) or, in lieu thereof, shall provide an annual written report to the Limited Partners, summarizing the Partnership\'s investment activities, performance, and outlook.

\(c\) **Capital Call and Distribution Notices.** Capital call notices and distribution notices shall be delivered to each Partner in the forms attached hereto as Exhibit B and Exhibit C, respectively, in accordance with the applicable notice periods set forth in this Agreement.

**[Section 12.4 --- Confidentiality of Information]{.underline}**

All information regarding the Partnership, its Partners, its Portfolio Investments, and its operations shall be treated as confidential by each Partner and shall not be disclosed to any Person other than such Partner\'s directors, officers, employees, legal counsel, accountants, and other professional advisors who have a need to know such information and who are bound by appropriate confidentiality obligations. The foregoing restriction shall be subject to exceptions for (a) disclosures required by applicable law, regulation, or governmental order, (b) disclosures required by the Freedom of Information Act or similar state or local laws applicable to governmental or quasi-governmental entities, (c) disclosures to regulatory authorities having jurisdiction over such Partner, and (d) such other exceptions as may be set forth in the applicable side letter between the General Partner and such Partner.

**[ARTICLE XIII --- EXCUSE AND EXCLUSION]{.underline}**

**[Section 13.1 --- Excuse Rights]{.underline}**

\(a\) A Limited Partner may request to be excused from participation in a particular Portfolio Investment if such participation would (i) violate any applicable law, regulation, order, or decree to which such Limited Partner is subject, (ii) cause a material adverse legal, tax, or regulatory consequence to such Limited Partner (including, without limitation, adverse consequences under ERISA, the Unrelated Business Income Tax provisions of the Code, or applicable foreign tax laws), or (iii) conflict with such Limited Partner\'s organizational documents, investment policies, or investment guidelines.

\(b\) **Procedure.** An excuse request must be made in writing by the requesting Limited Partner to the General Partner within ten (10) Business Days following receipt of the applicable capital call notice. The excuse request shall set forth in reasonable detail the basis for the requested excuse and shall be accompanied by such supporting documentation as the General Partner may reasonably request.

\(c\) **Determination.** The General Partner shall determine in good faith whether the requested excuse is warranted. In the event of a dispute regarding the propriety of an excuse request, the General Partner shall consult with the LPAC before making a final determination. The General Partner\'s determination shall be final and binding on the requesting Limited Partner.

**[Section 13.2 --- Exclusion]{.underline}**

\(a\) The General Partner may, in its sole discretion, exclude a Limited Partner from participation in a particular Portfolio Investment if the General Partner determines in good faith that such Limited Partner\'s participation would (i) cause a material adverse effect on the Partnership, the applicable Portfolio Company, or the other Partners, (ii) violate any applicable law, regulation, order, or decree, or (iii) jeopardize the Partnership\'s tax status, including the Partnership\'s qualification as a VCOC under Article XVII.

\(b\) An excluded Limited Partner\'s unfunded Capital Commitment shall not be reduced by the amount of the exclusion and shall remain available for future capital calls.

**[Section 13.3 --- Allocations for Excused/Excluded Limited Partners]{.underline}**

\(a\) Any Limited Partner that is excused or excluded from participation in a particular Portfolio Investment pursuant to this Article XIII shall not bear any share of the costs associated with, and shall not share in any profits or losses arising from, such Portfolio Investment.

\(b\) The pro rata share of the excused or excluded Limited Partner shall be reallocated among the remaining Partners (including the General Partner) on a pro rata basis based on their respective Capital Commitments (adjusted for any other excused or excluded Limited Partners).

**[ARTICLE XIV --- LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE (LPAC)]{.underline}**

**[Section 14.1 --- Establishment and Composition]{.underline}**

\(a\) **Establishment.** The General Partner shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\") promptly following the First Close. The LPAC shall consist of a minimum of three (3) and a maximum of seven (7) members.

\(b\) **Appointment.** Members of the LPAC shall be appointed by the General Partner from among the largest Limited Partners (measured by Capital Commitment). The General Partner shall endeavor to include at least one representative of a non-U.S. Limited Partner on the LPAC if non-U.S. Capital Commitments aggregate \$50,000,000 or more.

\(c\) **Initial LPAC.** The General Partner anticipates inviting representatives of the following entities to serve as initial LPAC members (subject to their admission as Limited Partners at the First Close): Ironwood PERS, Northgate Endowment Management LLC, and Pinnacle Insurance Group, Inc. Additional LPAC members may be appointed following the Final Close in accordance with this Section 14.1. The initial composition of the LPAC is set forth in Schedule E attached hereto.

\(d\) **Term and Removal.** Each LPAC member shall serve until the earlier of (i) such member\'s resignation from the LPAC, (ii) such member ceasing to hold a Partnership Interest, or (iii) removal by the General Partner for reasonable cause. The General Partner may appoint replacement LPAC members from time to time.

**[Section 14.2 --- Role and Authority]{.underline}**

\(a\) **Advisory Capacity.** The LPAC shall act in an advisory (non-fiduciary) capacity and shall not have the authority to act on behalf of the Partnership or to bind the Partnership or any Partner to any agreement or obligation. LPAC members shall not, by virtue of their service on the LPAC, be deemed to be general partners or to owe fiduciary duties to the Partnership or any Partner.

\(b\) **Matters Requiring LPAC Consent or Consultation.** The following matters shall require the prior consent or consultation of the LPAC, as applicable:

> \(i\) Approval of conflicts of interest and related-party transactions involving the General Partner, its Affiliates, or the Key Persons;
>
> \(ii\) Approval of valuations in connection with the removal of the General Partner, Key Person Events, and Carried Interest calculations;
>
> \(iii\) Consent to distributions in kind;
>
> \(iv\) Consent to the second Extension Period (extending the Fund Term from May 15, 2038 to May 15, 2039);
>
> \(v\) Consent to investments that exceed the Concentration Limit;
>
> \(vi\) Consent to acceptance of Aggregate Commitments in excess of the Hard Cap;
>
> \(vii\) Review of the General Partner\'s allocation of expenses between the Partnership and its Affiliates;
>
> \(viii\) Approval of follow-on investments after the expiration of the Investment Period (in circumstances where such investments were not committed during the Investment Period);
>
> \(ix\) Approval of replacement Key Persons pursuant to Section 10.4; and
>
> \(x\) Such other matters as may be referred to the LPAC by the General Partner from time to time.

**[Section 14.3 --- Meetings]{.underline}**

\(a\) The LPAC shall meet at least semi-annually (in person, by video conference, or by teleconference) and at any other time upon the request of the General Partner or any two (2) LPAC members.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide meeting materials (including agendas and relevant supporting documentation) to LPAC members at least five (5) Business Days in advance of each scheduled meeting.

\(c\) A quorum for purposes of LPAC meetings shall consist of a majority of the then-serving LPAC members. Actions may be taken by the LPAC at a duly convened meeting at which a quorum is present or by written consent of the requisite number of LPAC members.

**[Section 14.4 --- Voting]{.underline}**

\(a\) Each LPAC member shall have one (1) vote on all matters submitted to the LPAC for approval or consent.

\(b\) Unless otherwise specified in this Agreement, decisions of the LPAC shall be made by a simple majority of the votes cast by LPAC members present (in person or by proxy) at a duly convened meeting or acting by written consent.

\(c\) A supermajority vote (two-thirds of the then-serving LPAC members) shall be required for (i) consent to investments exceeding the Concentration Limit and (ii) consent to acceptance of Aggregate Commitments in excess of the Hard Cap.

**[Section 14.5 --- Indemnification of LPAC Members]{.underline}**

Each LPAC member shall be indemnified by the Partnership to the same extent as the General Partner and other Covered Persons are indemnified under Article XVI. For purposes of Article XVI, LPAC members shall be deemed \"Covered Persons.\"

**[ARTICLE XV --- BOOKS, RECORDS, AND BANK ACCOUNTS]{.underline}**

**[Section 15.1 --- Books and Records]{.underline}**

\(a\) The General Partner shall maintain, or cause to be maintained, complete and accurate books and records of the Partnership\'s business and affairs at the principal office of the Partnership (3400 Sand Hill Road, Suite 220, Menlo Park, California 94025) or at such other location as the General Partner may designate.

\(b\) The books and records of the Partnership shall be available for inspection and copying by any Limited Partner or its duly authorized representatives during normal business hours upon reasonable advance written notice to the General Partner. The cost of any such inspection or copying shall be borne by the requesting Limited Partner.

\(c\) The books and records shall include, without limitation, a copy of this Agreement (as amended from time to time), the Certificate of Limited Partnership, all financial statements, tax returns, the Schedule of Partners, and such other records as are required to be maintained under the DRULPA or applicable law.

**[Section 15.2 --- Bank Accounts]{.underline}**

\(a\) All cash of the Partnership shall be held in one or more bank accounts at Ridgeway National Bank, N.A. (Steven Cho, Vice President --- Fund Banking, 383 Madison Avenue, New York, New York 10179), or at such other financial institution as the General Partner may select from time to time.

\(b\) The General Partner is hereby authorized to open, maintain, and close bank accounts in the name of the Partnership, and to designate signatories with authority to draw on such accounts.

\(c\) Cash held in Partnership bank accounts may be temporarily invested in short-term, investment-grade instruments pending deployment in Portfolio Investments or distribution to Partners.

**[Section 15.3 --- Valuation]{.underline}**

\(a\) Portfolio Investments shall be valued at fair value in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification Topic 820 --- Fair Value Measurement (\"ASC 820\"), as determined by the General Partner in good faith.

\(b\) The General Partner shall establish and maintain a written valuation policy, which shall set forth the methodologies, assumptions, and procedures to be used in determining the fair value of Portfolio Investments. Common valuation methodologies may include comparable company analysis, precedent transaction analysis, discounted cash flow analysis, and market-based approaches, as appropriate for the nature and stage of each Portfolio Investment.

\(c\) Annual valuations of Portfolio Investments shall be subject to review by the Partnership\'s independent auditor (Whitfield & Pratt LLP) in connection with the annual audit.

\(d\) The LPAC shall be consulted on the valuation methodology applied by the General Partner and on any significant valuation disputes or adjustments.

**[ARTICLE XVI --- INDEMNIFICATION AND EXCULPATION]{.underline}**

**[Section 16.1 --- Indemnification]{.underline}**

\(a\) The Partnership shall indemnify and hold harmless the General Partner, its members, managers, officers, and employees, the Management Company, the LPAC members, and the Affiliates, agents, and representatives of each of the foregoing (collectively, \"Covered Persons\"), from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses, judgments, fines, settlements, and other amounts) (collectively, \"Losses\") arising out of, relating to, or in connection with any act or omission of such Covered Person in connection with the business or affairs of the Partnership; *provided*, *however*, that no Covered Person shall be entitled to indemnification under this Section 16.1 to the extent that such Losses result from the willful misconduct, gross negligence, fraud, or bad faith of such Covered Person.

\(b\) The right to indemnification under this Section 16.1 shall be in addition to any other rights to which a Covered Person may be entitled under applicable law, any other agreement, or otherwise.

\(c\) Indemnification amounts shall be paid from Partnership assets. If Partnership assets are insufficient to satisfy indemnification obligations, the General Partner may issue capital calls to fund such obligations from unfunded Capital Commitments in accordance with Section 4.1.

**[Section 16.2 --- Exculpation]{.underline}**

\(a\) No Covered Person shall be liable to the Partnership or to any Partner for any Losses arising out of, relating to, or in connection with any act or omission of such Covered Person in connection with the business or affairs of the Partnership, except to the extent that such Losses result from the willful misconduct, gross negligence, fraud, or bad faith of such Covered Person.

\(b\) The General Partner, in performing its duties and exercising its powers under this Agreement, may rely in good faith upon the opinions, reports, advice, and other information provided by legal counsel, accountants, auditors, appraisers, investment bankers, consultants, and other professional advisors, and shall not be liable for any action taken or omitted in reliance upon such opinions, reports, advice, or other information if the General Partner\'s reliance thereon was reasonable.

**[Section 16.3 --- Insurance]{.underline}**

The General Partner may cause the Partnership to purchase and maintain directors\' and officers\' liability insurance (\"D&O insurance\") and errors and omissions insurance (\"E&O insurance\") covering Covered Persons, at the Partnership\'s expense, in such amounts and with such coverage as the General Partner deems appropriate. Such insurance shall be placed through Vantage Risk Advisors, Inc. (contact: Laura Benton) or such other insurance broker as the General Partner may select from time to time.

**[Section 16.4 --- Advancement of Expenses]{.underline}**

The Partnership shall advance to any Covered Person entitled to indemnification under Section 16.1 the reasonable costs and expenses (including attorneys\' fees) incurred by such Covered Person in defending any action, suit, or proceeding to which such Covered Person is a party by reason of its status as a Covered Person, upon receipt by the Partnership of a written undertaking by or on behalf of such Covered Person to repay such amounts if it is ultimately determined that such Covered Person is not entitled to indemnification under this Article XVI.

**[ARTICLE XVII --- ERISA AND REGULATORY MATTERS]{.underline}**

**[Section 17.1 --- VCOC Election]{.underline}**

\(a\) If \"benefit plan investors\" (as defined in Department of Labor Regulation § 2510.3-101(f)(2)) hold, at any time, twenty-five percent (25%) or more of any class of equity interests in the Partnership (calculated in accordance with DOL Regulation § 2510.3-101(f)), the General Partner shall cause the Partnership to qualify and maintain its qualification as a \"venture capital operating company\" (VCOC) within the meaning of DOL Regulation § 2510.3-101(d).

\(b\) VCOC qualification requires that, on the initial \"valuation date\" and at least one day during each subsequent annual \"valuation period,\" at least fifty percent (50%) of the assets of the Partnership (other than short-term investments), valued at cost, consist of \"venture capital investments\" --- that is, equity investments in Portfolio Companies in which the Partnership has obtained and exercises contractual management rights (including the right to participate in the management or conduct of the business of the Portfolio Company, such as board seats, board observation rights, or equivalent governance provisions).

\(c\) The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain VCOC status throughout the Fund Term, including by obtaining and exercising management rights in a sufficient number of Portfolio Companies to satisfy the VCOC test.

\(d\) If the General Partner determines that VCOC status cannot be maintained, the General Partner shall promptly notify all benefit plan investor Limited Partners and shall take such actions as are reasonably necessary to comply with ERISA, including offering such Limited Partners the opportunity to transfer their Partnership Interests or making structural modifications to the Partnership.

**[Section 17.2 --- ERISA Representations]{.underline}**

Each Limited Partner that is a \"benefit plan investor\" (as defined under ERISA and DOL Regulation § 2510.3-101) or that is otherwise subject to ERISA or Section 4975 of the Code shall so represent in its Subscription Agreement and shall promptly notify the General Partner of any change in its status as a benefit plan investor. The General Partner shall monitor the percentage of benefit plan investor participation at each Closing and on an ongoing basis in connection with any Transfers of Partnership Interests.

**[Section 17.3 --- Investment Company Act]{.underline}**

The Partnership shall be operated so as to be exempt from registration as an investment company under the Investment Company Act. The Partnership shall rely on the exclusion from the definition of \"investment company\" set forth in Section 3(c)(7) of the Investment Company Act, which provides an exclusion for issuers whose outstanding securities are owned exclusively by \"qualified purchasers\" (as defined in Section 2(a)(51) of the Investment Company Act). Each Limited Partner shall represent in its Subscription Agreement that it is a qualified purchaser, and the General Partner shall not admit any Person as a Limited Partner unless such Person is a qualified purchaser.

**[Section 17.4 --- Advisers Act]{.underline}**

\(a\) Cobalt Ventures LP is currently registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission as an Exempt Reporting Adviser (\"ERA\") pursuant to Section 203(m) of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended (the \"Advisers Act\") (SEC File No. 802-11934).

\(b\) If the formation of the Partnership and the acceptance of Capital Commitments hereunder would cause the aggregate assets under management (\"AUM\") of Cobalt Ventures LP and its relying advisers to exceed the ERA threshold, the General Partner shall coordinate with regulatory counsel (Fielding & O\'Hara PLLC, contact: Brian Liddell) to evaluate whether registration as a registered investment adviser under the Advisers Act is required, and, if so, to effect such registration and to amend Form ADV accordingly.

\(c\) The General Partner shall comply with all applicable requirements of the Advisers Act and the rules and regulations thereunder, including Form ADV filing and updating requirements, recordkeeping requirements, and the anti-fraud provisions of Section 206 of the Advisers Act.

**[Section 17.5 --- Anti-Money Laundering / OFAC]{.underline}**

\(a\) Anti-money laundering (\"AML\") and know-your-customer (\"KYC\") screening of all prospective investors shall be conducted by Halcyon Fund Services, Inc. in accordance with the Bank Secrecy Act, the USA PATRIOT Act, and applicable regulations promulgated by the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (\"FinCEN\").

\(b\) No Person shall be admitted as a Limited Partner if such Person (or any beneficial owner of such Person) appears on the list of Specially Designated Nationals and blocked Persons maintained by the U.S. Department of the Treasury\'s Office of Foreign Assets Control (\"OFAC\") or is otherwise a prohibited person under applicable anti-money laundering laws and sanctions programs.

\(c\) Each Limited Partner shall represent in its Subscription Agreement that it is not a prohibited person and shall promptly notify the General Partner if any change in its status occurs.

**[Section 17.6 --- Securities Law Compliance]{.underline}**

\(a\) Partnership Interests are being offered and sold in reliance on the exemption from registration under the Securities Act provided by Regulation D promulgated thereunder.

\(b\) The General Partner shall cause to be filed a Form D with the SEC and shall make such state \"blue sky\"orities having jurisdiction over such Partner, (iv) to prospective transferees of such Partner\'s Partnership Interest (subject to such transferees entering into appropriate confidentiality agreements), or (v) as otherwise permitted by the applicable Side Letter between the General Partner and such Partner.

\(c\) The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Section 21.9 shall survive the termination or dissolution of the Partnership and the withdrawal or removal of any Partner for a period of three (3) years.

**[Section 21.10 --- Power of Attorney]{.underline}**

Each Limited Partner hereby irrevocably constitutes and appoints the General Partner (and any successor general partner), with full power of substitution, as its true and lawful attorney-in-fact, with full power and authority in its name, place, and stead, to execute, acknowledge, deliver, swear to, record, file, and publish on behalf of such Limited Partner:

> \(a\) any amendment to this Agreement or the Certificate of Limited Partnership;
>
> \(b\) any certificates, instruments, documents, or filings that may be required to be filed by the Partnership or any Partner under the laws of the State of Delaware or any other jurisdiction in which the Partnership conducts business;
>
> \(c\) any instruments necessary or appropriate to reflect the admission, withdrawal, or substitution of Partners, or the dissolution and winding up of the Partnership; and
>
> \(d\) any other instruments, documents, or certificates that the General Partner deems necessary or appropriate to carry out the provisions of this Agreement or to comply with applicable law.

The power of attorney granted herein is coupled with an interest and shall survive the death, disability, incapacity, dissolution, bankruptcy, insolvency, or termination of any Limited Partner and shall extend to such Limited Partner\'s heirs, successors, assigns, and personal representatives.

**[Section 21.11 --- No Third-Party Beneficiaries]{.underline}**

Except as expressly set forth in Article XVI with respect to Covered Persons, nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any Person other than the Partners and their respective successors and permitted assigns any legal or equitable right, benefit, or remedy of any nature under or by reason of this Agreement.

**[Section 21.12 --- Partnership Tax Matters Representative]{.underline}**

\(a\) The General Partner (or its designee) shall serve as the \"partnership representative\" of the Partnership within the meaning of Section 6223(a) of the Code (as amended by the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2015 and subsequent legislation). The partnership representative shall have sole authority to act on behalf of the Partnership in connection with any administrative or judicial proceeding with the Internal Revenue Service or any other taxing authority, and the partnership representative\'s determinations in such proceedings shall be binding on the Partnership and all Partners.

\(b\) The partnership representative may, in its discretion, make a \"push-out\" election under Section 6226 of the Code (or any comparable provision of state or local tax law) in lieu of the Partnership paying any imputed underpayment resulting from a partnership-level audit adjustment.

\(c\) The General Partner shall promptly notify the Limited Partners of the commencement of any material tax audit or proceeding and shall keep the Limited Partners reasonably informed of the progress of any such audit or proceeding.

\(d\) The Partnership shall indemnify and hold harmless the partnership representative from and against any Losses arising out of its service as partnership representative, to the same extent as Covered Persons are indemnified under Article XVI.

This AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED AGREEMENT OF LIMITED PARTNERSHIP OF ARDENT CAPITAL PARTNERS III LP (this \"Amendment\") is entered into and made effective as of February 28, 2024 (the \"Amendment Effective Date\"), by Ardent Capital GP III LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"General Partner\"), acting in its capacity as the sole general partner of, and on behalf of, Ardent Capital Partners III LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Partnership\" or the \"Fund\").

**WHEREAS**, in connection with the Restructuring, David Kellner, a Senior Partner of the General Partner and the Management Company, is retiring from his positions with the General Partner and the Management Company effective March 31, 2024, and Joanna Trask, a Partner of the General Partner and the Management Company, is departing from her positions with the General Partner and the Management Company effective April 15, 2024, and each of David Kellner and Joanna Trask has withdrawn, or has agreed to withdraw, as a member of the General Partner and the Management Company in connection with the Restructuring;

**WHEREAS**, Section 9.4 of the Partnership Agreement provides that the consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\") shall be required for certain amendments to the Partnership Agreement and for material changes to the management structure of the Fund, including changes in the ownership or control of the General Partner;

**WHEREAS**, the LPAC, currently consisting of duly appointed representatives of Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System, Crestwood Endowment Partners, Pinnacle Insurance Group, and Graystone Family Office LLC, has been duly notified of the Restructuring and the proposed amendments to the Partnership Agreement contemplated by this Amendment, and has provided its written consent to this Amendment and the Restructuring at a duly convened meeting of the LPAC held on February 14, 2024, in compliance with the requirements of Section 9.4 of the Partnership Agreement;

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner desires to amend the Partnership Agreement to (a) reflect the Restructuring, including the interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate in the ownership chain of the General Partner and the Management Company, (b) update certain defined terms to reflect the new organizational structure and the departure of David Kellner and Joanna Trask, (c) amend the GP Commitment provisions to reflect the assumption of departing principals\' unfunded commitments by the remaining and newly admitted principals, and (d) make conforming changes to Section 5.2 (Key Person), Section 8.3 (Transfer of GP Interest), Section 9.4 (LPAC Consent), and related provisions of the Partnership Agreement;

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner is authorized to execute this Amendment on behalf of the Partnership pursuant to the terms of Section 9.4 of the Partnership Agreement and has obtained all requisite consents and approvals, including the consent of the LPAC and the written consent of all members of the General Partner prior to the Restructuring;
> \"**HoldCo Members**\" means the members of HoldCo from time to time. As of the Amendment Effective Date, the HoldCo Members and their respective membership interests in HoldCo are as follows:

For the avoidance of doubt, David Kellner and Joanna Trask are hereby removed from the definition of \"Principals\" effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, reflecting their respective departures from the General Partner and the Management Company in connection with the Restructuring.

> \(b\) A \"Key Person Event\" under Section 5.2 of the Partnership Agreement shall be triggered if either (i) both Key Persons cease to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund during the Investment Period, or (ii) one Key Person ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund during the Investment Period and such Key Person is not replaced by a substitute individual approved by the LPAC within one hundred twenty (120) days following such cessation.

The General Partner confirms that it has provided, or will provide within fifteen (15) business days following the effective date of David Kellner\'s departure (March 31, 2024), all notifications required to be delivered to the applicable limited partners under such side letters, in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in the applicable side letter provisions. The General Partner further confirms that it will provide similar notifications to any limited partners holding side letters containing analogous provisions with respect to the departure of Joanna Trask, within fifteen (15) business days following the effective date of her departure (April 15, 2024).

The General Partner acknowledges that three (3) side letters entered into in connection with the Fund\'s closings grant the applicable limited partners a right to request a suspension of the Investment Period for a period of up to ninety (90) days pending LPAC review and consultation upon the departure of a Contributing Person, as defined in such side letters. The General Partner hereby confirms the following facts with respect to such suspension rights:

> \(a\) The General Partner notified the LPAC of the Restructuring and the planned departures of David Kellner and Joanna Trask by formal letter dated February 5, 2024, delivered by email and by overnight courier to each LPAC member.

> \(b\) The LPAC convened a duly noticed meeting on February 14, 2024, at which all four (4) LPAC representatives were present (either in person or by telephone), and the LPAC discussed the Restructuring, the departures of David Kellner and Joanna Trask, and the proposed amendments to the Partnership Agreement.

> \(c\) At the February 14, 2024 meeting, the LPAC granted its consent to the Restructuring and the amendments contemplated by this Amendment, and no LPAC member raised an objection or requested a suspension of the Investment Period.

> \(a\) The transfer of the membership interests in the General Partner from the five (5) individual principals (Marcus Aldridge, Priya Narayanan, David Kellner, Joanna Trask, and Robert Hsiao) to Ardent GP Intermediate LLC, as the sole member of the General Partner, in connection with the Restructuring constitutes a \"Permitted Transfer\" under Section 8.3 of the Partnership Agreement and does not require the consent of the limited partners of the Partnership, other than the consent of the LPAC, which has been duly obtained as set forth in Article IV of this Amendment.

> \(b\) The interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate in the ownership chain of the General Partner in connection with the Restructuring does not constitute a \"Transfer\" (as defined in Section 8.3 of the Partnership Agreement) of the General Partner\'s interest in the Partnership. Ardent Capital GP III LLC\'s general partner interest in the Partnership has not been transferred, assigned, pledged, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of in any manner. Ardent Capital GP III LLC continues to hold the same general partner interest in the Partnership that it held immediately prior to the Restructuring, and no assignment or conveyance of such interest has occurred.

Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.1 above, any future transfer, assignment, pledge, encumbrance, hypothecation, or other disposition (whether voluntary or involuntary, by operation of law or otherwise) of the general partner interest in the Partnership held by Ardent Capital GP III LLC, or any change in control of the General Partner, HoldCo, or GP Intermediate, shall continue to be subject to the transfer restrictions set forth in Section 8.3 of the Partnership Agreement, as amended by this Amendment, and shall require the prior written consent of the LPAC under Section 9.4 of the Partnership Agreement, as amended by this Amendment.
> \(e\) All instruments, agreements, and filings necessary to effect the Restructuring have been duly executed, delivered, and, where applicable, filed with the appropriate governmental authorities.
**[ARTICLE IV --- AMENDMENTS TO SECTION 9.4 (LPAC CONSENT)]{.underline}**
**Section 4.1 --- LPAC Consent for Restructuring**
Section 9.4 of the Partnership Agreement is hereby amended and restated to confirm that the consent of the LPAC shall be required for any of the following actions:
> \(d\) Any other action or matter for which LPAC consent is required under the Partnership Agreement or any side letter.

The General Partner hereby confirms that the LPAC has been duly consulted with respect to all of the amendments set forth in this Amendment and with respect to the Restructuring, and that the LPAC has granted its consent to all such amendments and to the Restructuring, at a duly convened meeting of the LPAC held on February 14, 2024, in compliance with all applicable requirements of Section 9.4 of the Partnership Agreement.
**Section 4.2 --- LPAC Composition**
The LPAC as of the Amendment Effective Date consists of duly appointed representatives of the following limited partners:

The LPAC members collectively represent aggregate capital commitments of Six Hundred Million Dollars (\$600,000,000), representing approximately 21.4% of the total capital commitments of the Fund. The composition, appointment, and removal of LPAC members continues to be governed by Section 9.4 of the Partnership Agreement, as amended hereby.
**Section 4.3 --- Future LPAC Consent Provisions**

> \(a\) Any future change in the identity or composition of the HoldCo Members that would result in a \"change in control\" of HoldCo (as defined in Section 3.2 of this Amendment) shall require the prior written consent of the LPAC, which consent may be granted or withheld in the LPAC\'s sole discretion.

> \(b\) The General Partner shall provide the LPAC with not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any proposed change in the composition of the HoldCo Members, including any proposed admission, withdrawal, or substitution of any HoldCo Member and any proposed transfer, assignment, or encumbrance of any HoldCo membership interest. Such notice shall describe in reasonable detail the proposed change, the identity of any new or departing HoldCo Member, the resulting ownership percentages of the HoldCo Members following such change, and any other information reasonably requested by the LPAC to evaluate the proposed change.

> \(c\) For the avoidance of doubt, changes in the relative ownership percentages among existing HoldCo Members that do not result in a change in control of HoldCo shall not require LPAC consent, provided that the General Partner shall provide the LPAC with written notice of any such change within fifteen (15) business days following the effectiveness thereof.

As of the Amendment Effective Date, Twenty-Nine Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$29,400,000) of the GP Commitment has been funded, representing 70% of the total GP Commitment. This funding percentage is consistent with the overall capital called by the Partnership, which as of the Amendment Effective Date has called One Billion Nine Hundred Sixty Million Dollars (\$1,960,000,000) of total commitments, representing 70% of total commitments of \$2,800,000,000. The General Partner has funded its GP Commitment pro rata with the limited partners\' capital contributions in accordance with the terms of the Partnership Agreement.

The remaining unfunded GP Commitment as of the Amendment Effective Date is Twelve Million Six Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$12,600,000), which the General Partner is obligated to fund pro rata with future capital calls to the limited partners in accordance with the terms of the Partnership Agreement.

> \(b\) Any removal of the General Partner pursuant to Section 9.7 shall also result in the automatic cessation of the Management Company\'s role as investment adviser and manager of the Fund, effective upon the effective date of such removal, unless the successor general partner otherwise determines, in its sole discretion, to retain the Management Company in such capacity pursuant to a new or amended investment management agreement.

> \(c\) For the avoidance of doubt, the removal of the General Partner pursuant to Section 9.7 shall not affect the rights of the departing General Partner or the HoldCo Members (or their successors or assigns) with respect to any accrued but unpaid carried interest, management fees, or other compensation earned prior to the effective date of such removal, subject to the clawback and escrow provisions of the Partnership Agreement.

The term of the Fund, as set forth in Section 10.1 of the Partnership Agreement, is not modified by this Amendment. The Fund term expires on December 31, 2029, subject to two (2) successive one-year extensions at the sole discretion of the General Partner, which would extend the Fund term to December 31, 2030 and December 31, 2031, respectively. The General Partner confirms that it has not exercised, and does not presently intend to exercise, either extension right as of the Amendment Effective Date.
The General Partner hereby represents and warrants to the Partnership and the limited partners as follows, as of the Amendment Effective Date:

The execution and delivery of this Amendment by the General Partner, and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby (including the Restructuring), have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate, limited liability company, and partnership action on the part of the General Partner, including the written consent of all of its members as constituted immediately prior to the Restructuring (namely, Marcus Aldridge, Priya Narayanan, David Kellner, Joanna Trask, and Robert Hsiao), which written consent was executed and delivered as of February 28, 2024. The General Partner has full power, authority, and legal capacity to execute and deliver this Amendment and to perform its obligations hereunder and under the Partnership Agreement, as amended hereby. This Amendment constitutes the valid and binding obligation of the General Partner, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity.
**Section 7.2 --- LPAC Consent**

The General Partner represents and warrants that the LPAC was duly notified of the Restructuring and the proposed amendments to the Partnership Agreement by formal letter dated February 5, 2024, delivered by email and by overnight courier to each LPAC representative at the address set forth in the Partnership records. The LPAC convened a duly noticed meeting on February 14, 2024, at which all four (4) LPAC representatives participated, and the LPAC granted its consent to this Amendment and to the Restructuring at such meeting, in compliance with all applicable requirements of Section 9.4 of the Partnership Agreement. The General Partner has received and retains in its records written confirmation of the LPAC\'s consent, and a copy of the LPAC Written Consent dated February 14, 2024 has been provided to the Partnership\'s counsel.

> \(a\) Four (4) side letters (entered into with Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System, Pinnacle Insurance Group, Crestwood Endowment Partners, and Haverford Capital Partners) contain provisions requiring prior written notice and/or affirmative consent from the applicable limited partner for any material change in the management structure of the Fund. The General Partner has provided the required prior written notice to each such limited partner and has obtained the required consents, or will obtain such consents prior to the effective date of the applicable changes.

> \(c\) The General Partner has complied, and will continue to comply, with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations in connection with the Restructuring and the execution and implementation of this Amendment.

Except as expressly amended, modified, or supplemented by this Amendment, the Partnership Agreement shall remain in full force and effect and is hereby ratified and confirmed in all respects. All references in the Partnership Agreement to \"this Agreement,\" \"hereof,\" \"herein,\" \"hereunder,\" or words of similar import shall, from and after the Amendment Effective Date, be deemed to refer to the Partnership Agreement as amended by this Amendment. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the terms and provisions of this Amendment and the terms and provisions of the Partnership Agreement (as in effect immediately prior to this Amendment), the terms and provisions of this Amendment shall govern and control.

This Amendment may be executed in one or more counterparts, including by facsimile or portable document format (.pdf) transmission, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page of this Amendment by facsimile or by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.
**\[SIGNATURE PAGE FOLLOWS\]**
**SIGNATURE PAGE TO AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED AGREEMENT OF LIMITED PARTNERSHIP OF ARDENT CAPITAL PARTNERS III LP**
**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the General Partner has executed this Amendment as of the date first written above.
**Acknowledged and consented to by the Limited Partner Advisory Committee:**
Reference is hereby made to the LPAC Written Consent dated February 14, 2024, executed by the duly authorized representatives of each of the following LPAC members:
A copy of the LPAC Written Consent is on file with the General Partner and is incorporated herein by reference.

The following sets forth the organizational and ownership structure of the Fund and its affiliated entities following the completion of the Restructuring, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date. This chart is provided for informational and illustrative purposes and is subject to the terms and conditions of this Amendment and the Partnership Agreement.

*Note: Funded amounts reflect 70% of each principal\'s total commitment, consistent with the overall 70% capital call rate of the Partnership (\$1,960,000,000 called out of \$2,800,000,000 total commitments) as of the Amendment Effective Date.*
