\*\*\"Effectively Connected Income\" or \"ECI\"\*\* means income that is effectively connected with the conduct of a trade or business within the United States within the meaning of Section 864 of the Code, including income treated as ECI under Section 897 of the Code (relating to dispositions of U.S. real property interests).

\(b\) **After-Tax Basis.** The Clawback Amount shall be calculated on an after-tax basis, taking into account the U.S. federal, state, and local income taxes actually paid (or deemed paid) by the General Partner (or its individual members, as applicable) with respect to the Carried Interest distributions subject to clawback. The assumed combined marginal tax rate to be used for this after-tax calculation shall be agreed upon by the General Partner and the LP Advisory Committee prior to the Final Closing Date.

\(d\) \*\*Offshore blocker Entity Classification Election.\*\* The General Partner shall cause the Offshore blocker (PCV International Holdings Ltd.) to file a Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) with the Internal Revenue Service, electing to be classified as a corporation (rather than a partnership or disregarded entity) for U.S. federal income tax purposes, effective as of the date of formation of the Offshore blocker (target: September 30, 2025). The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that such Form 8832 is filed no later than seventy-five (75) days after the date of formation of the Offshore blocker, in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 301.7701-3(c)(1)(i).

**\[C&H Comment: The Hawthorne Reid draft references the pre-BBA \"tax matters partner\" regime under former Section 6231(a)(7) of the Code, which was repealed by the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2015 effective for partnership tax years beginning after December 31, 2017. The Partnership is subject to the centralized partnership audit regime under Sections 6221 through 6241 of the Code (the \"BBA Audit Rules\"), which requires the designation of a \"partnership representative\" (not a \"tax matters partner\"). We have proposed a complete rewrite of this section.\]**

\(c\) **Authority.** The Partnership Representative shall have the sole authority to act on behalf of the Partnership in connection with any federal income tax audit, examination, or judicial proceeding under the BBA Audit Rules, including (without limitation) the authority to: (i) receive notices from the Internal Revenue Service; (ii) bind the Partnership and the Partners with respect to matters arising under the BBA Audit Rules; (iii) extend the statute of limitations with respect to any Partnership item; (iv) file amended returns on behalf of the Partnership; and (v) negotiate, settle, or contest any proposed adjustment. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Partnership Representative shall keep the Limited Partners and the LP Advisory Committee reasonably informed of the status and progress of any audit, examination, or proceeding, and shall not agree to any settlement or adjustment (whether by entering into a closing agreement, accepting a notice of final partnership adjustment, or otherwise) without first consulting with the LP Advisory Committee and providing the LP Advisory Committee with a reasonable opportunity to review and comment on the proposed settlement or adjustment.

**\[C&H Comment: The push-out election under Section 6226 is strongly recommended. Without a push-out election, the Partnership would be liable for an \"imputed underpayment\" calculated at the highest individual tax rate (currently 37% for ordinary income, plus any applicable state tax rates), without regard to the individual tax characteristics of the Partners. This calculation would be particularly unfavorable to (i) Tax-Exempt Partners (such as Meridian Public Employees\' Retirement System and Ashford University Endowment), which are generally exempt from federal income tax and would effectively be subsidizing the tax liabilities of other Partners; (ii) Non-U.S. Partners (such as Sovereign Capital Partners (Cayman) Ltd.), which may not be subject to U.S. tax on certain items of income; and (iii) Partners that are subject to lower rates (e.g., long-term capital gain rates) or that have offsetting losses or credits. The push-out election ensures that each Partner bears the tax consequences of any audit adjustment in accordance with its own tax position.\]**

> \(iv\) Not dispose of (or cause the Partnership to dispose of) the shares of Vectral Cloud Inc. prior to March 2026 (being the date on which the five-year holding period under Section 1202(a)(1) is expected to be satisfied), absent (A) a Qualifying IPO or other liquidity event approved by the General Partner and the LP Advisory Committee, or (B) the prior written consent of Partners holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the Partnership Interests then outstanding, in each case in order to preserve the ability of eligible Partners to tack the five-year holding period under Section 1202(h).

\(i\) The Partnership is authorized and required to withhold and remit to the Internal Revenue Service such amounts as are required to be withheld under Section 1446 of the Code (and the Treasury Regulations thereunder) with respect to any Non-U.S. Partner\'s allocable share of the Partnership\'s income that is, or is treated as, Effectively Connected Income (ECI). The applicable withholding rate under Section 1446 is the highest rate of tax specified in Section 1 of the Code (for individual Non-U.S. Partners) or Section 11 of the Code (for corporate Non-U.S. Partners), applied to the Non-U.S. Partner\'s allocable share of ECI.

\(iii\) Each Non-U.S. Partner shall furnish to the Partnership a properly completed and executed Form W-8BEN, Form W-8BEN-E, or other applicable Form W-8, as appropriate, on or before the date such Non-U.S. Partner is admitted to the Partnership, and shall update such form as required by applicable law (generally, every three years or upon a change in circumstances). A Non-U.S. Partner\'s failure to timely provide an accurate Form W-8 shall entitle the Partnership to withhold at the maximum applicable rate, without regard to any reduced rate that might otherwise be available under an applicable income tax treaty.

\*\*\[C&H Comment: The Offshore blocker (PCV International Holdings Ltd.) is specifically designed to block ECI from flowing through to Non-U.S. Partners, including Sovereign Capital Partners (Cayman) Ltd. (commitment of \$75,000,000). If the Offshore blocker is properly interposed and functioning as intended, the Offshore blocker (as a foreign corporation) will be the \"partner\" for purposes of Section 1446, and the Offshore blocker itself will be subject to U.S. federal income tax on any ECI allocated to it (filing Form 1120-F). Non-U.S. Partners investing through the Offshore blocker should not themselves be treated as receiving ECI allocations, and Section 1446 withholding should not apply at the investor level. However, this withholding provision must remain in the LPA to address any Non-U.S. Partner that elects to invest directly in the Partnership (rather than through the Offshore blocker), or in the event the Offshore blocker structure is for any reason not effective in blocking ECI.\]\*\*

\(d\) **Tax Protection Agreement.** The protections set forth in this Section AA.7 are in addition to, and are not intended to limit, the protections set forth in the Tax Protection Agreement among the Partnership, the General Partner, and the Rolling LPs (a separate document to be executed concurrently with this Agreement), which provides for, among other things, minimum holding periods for the Contributed Assets, liability allocation commitments, and indemnification of the Rolling LPs in the event of gain recognition resulting from the Partnership\'s actions.

\(d\) **Tax Treatment.** The Domestic blocker, as a C-corporation, shall be subject to corporate-level U.S. federal income tax on its allocable share of Partnership income at the applicable corporate tax rate (currently twenty-one percent (21%)). Distributions from the Domestic blocker to the Tax-Exempt Partners shall be treated as dividends to the extent of the Domestic blocker\'s current and accumulated earnings and profits (E&P), and as a return of capital to the extent of the Tax-Exempt Partner\'s basis in its shares of the Domestic blocker, and as capital gain thereafter. Dividend distributions received by a Tax-Exempt Partner from the Domestic blocker should not constitute UBTI (provided that the Tax-Exempt Partner\'s stock in the Domestic blocker is not \"debt-financed property\" within the meaning of Section 514 of the Code), and therefore the Domestic blocker should effectively \[DELETED: block\] \[ADDED: block\] UBTI from reaching the Tax-Exempt Partners.

\(b\) **Purpose.** The Offshore blocker is interposed between the Partnership and the Non-U.S. Partners for the purpose of blocking Effectively Connected Income (ECI) from flowing through to Non-U.S. Partners (thereby avoiding the obligation of Non-U.S. Partners to file U.S. federal income tax returns and pay U.S. tax on ECI) and blocking the application of FIRPTA withholding under Sections 897 and 1446 of the Code with respect to dispositions of Partnership assets that may constitute U.S. real property interests. The Non-U.S. Partner that will invest through the Offshore blocker is:

\(c\) **Check-the-box Election.** As set forth in Section AA.1(d), the General Partner shall cause the Offshore blocker to file a Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) with the Internal Revenue Service, electing to be classified as a corporation (rather than as a partnership or disregarded entity) for U.S. federal income tax purposes, effective as of the date of formation of the Offshore blocker (target: September 30, 2025). Classification as a corporation is essential to the Offshore blocker\'s function as a blocker entity; if the Offshore blocker were classified as a partnership or disregarded entity, the income of the Offshore blocker (including ECI) would flow through directly to the Non-U.S. Partners, thereby defeating the purpose of the structure.

\(c\) The General Partner shall provide the Limited Partners with a written summary of all Transaction Fees received and offsets applied on at least an annual basis, and upon request by the LPAC.
\(g\) Costs associated with LPAC meetings, including travel, venue, and related expenses;

\(c\) Distributions shall generally be made in cash. In-kind distributions of securities or other property shall be permitted only with the prior consent of the LPAC (or, in the case of distributions made in connection with the liquidation and winding up of the Partnership, without LPAC consent), subject to Section 8.5.
\(b\) In-kind Distributions shall require the prior consent of the LPAC, except in connection with the liquidation and winding up of the Partnership pursuant to Article XIII.

\(a\) The Clawback obligation set forth in Section 9.1 shall be guaranteed by the following principals of Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, each of whom shall execute a personal guarantee in form and substance reasonably acceptable to the LPAC: (i) Marcus J. Harrowgate; (ii) Diana R. Castellano; and (iii) Jonathan P. Birch (each, a **\"Clawback Guarantor\"** and, collectively, the **\"Clawback Guarantors\"**), as set forth in Schedule C.

\(b\) The results of each interim clawback test shall be provided to the LPAC within ninety (90) days following the end of the applicable Fiscal Year, together with a report from the Independent Auditor setting forth the methodology and assumptions used in such test.

\(c\) If an interim clawback test reveals that the General Partner has received excess Carried Interest, the General Partner and the LPAC shall consult in good faith regarding the appropriate treatment of such excess, which may include (i) the establishment of an escrow or holdback from future Carried Interest Distributions, (ii) the voluntary return of all or a portion of the excess by the General Partner, or (iii) such other arrangement as the General Partner and the LPAC may agree.
\(a\) The Investment Period shall be automatically suspended, effective as of the date of the Key Person Event;
**[ARTICLE XI --- LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE (LPAC)]{.underline}**

\(a\) The General Partner shall establish and maintain a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the **\"LPAC\"**) composed of five (5) members, each of whom shall be a representative designated by a Limited Partner or a group of Limited Partners.

\(b\) Three (3) LPAC members shall be designated at or promptly following the First Close. The General Partner anticipates that the initial LPAC members will be representatives designated by the following Limited Partners: (i) Northmoor State Pension System, (ii) Edgecombe Insurance Group Ltd., and (iii) The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund. The remaining two (2) LPAC members shall be designated at or following the Final Close.

\(c\) The General Partner shall designate LPAC members from among the Limited Partners, taking into consideration the diversity of the Limited Partner base (including investor type, geographic location, and commitment size), the size of each Limited Partner\'s Capital Commitment, and the willingness and ability of such Limited Partner to serve on the LPAC. The General Partner shall consult with the Limited Partners in good faith regarding LPAC composition.

\(d\) LPAC members shall serve for the duration of the Fund Term (including any extension period), unless a member resigns, is removed by the General Partner in consultation with the other LPAC members, or ceases to be a Partner. The General Partner shall designate a replacement LPAC member to fill any vacancy on the LPAC.

\(a\) The LPAC shall hold at least two (2) meetings during each Fiscal Year. Meetings may be held in person, by video conference, or by telephone conference, as determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC members.

\(b\) Special meetings of the LPAC may be convened by the General Partner at any time, or upon the written request of a majority of the LPAC members. The General Partner shall provide at least ten (10) Business Days\' advance written notice of each LPAC meeting (or such shorter notice as the circumstances may require), together with an agenda and relevant supporting materials.

\(c\) The General Partner\'s personnel, including the Key Persons, shall attend LPAC meetings and shall be available to respond to questions from LPAC members regarding the Fund\'s investments, operations, and performance.
\(d\) The General Partner shall prepare and distribute written minutes of each LPAC meeting to the LPAC members within thirty (30) days following such meeting.

\(a\) The LPAC shall act in an advisory and consent capacity only. The LPAC shall not have any management authority over the affairs of the Partnership and shall not participate in the control of the Partnership\'s business within the meaning of Section 17-303 of the Act.
\(b\) The following matters shall require the prior approval or consent of the LPAC:
> \(iii\) Extension of the Fund Term beyond the second GP discretionary extension (i.e., the third one-year extension described in Section 2.5(c) shall require LPAC approval);
> \(ix\) Such other matters as may be submitted to the LPAC by the General Partner from time to time.
\(c\) The LPAC\'s approval or consent shall not be required for any matter not expressly set forth in Section 11.3(b) or elsewhere in this Agreement.
\(a\) A quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., three (3) out of five (5) members).
\(b\) All actions of the LPAC shall be taken by the affirmative vote of a majority of the LPAC members present and constituting a quorum.
\(c\) The LPAC may act by written consent in lieu of a meeting if a majority of LPAC members execute a written consent approving the action to be taken.

\(a\) LPAC members shall act solely in an advisory capacity and shall not owe fiduciary duties to any other Limited Partner, the Partnership, or the General Partner by virtue of their service on the LPAC. No LPAC member shall be liable to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any other Partner for any act or omission taken in connection with LPAC service, except to the extent caused by such LPAC member\'s fraud, bad faith, or willful misconduct.

\(b\) The Partnership shall indemnify and hold harmless each LPAC member (and such LPAC member\'s employer, Affiliates, officers, directors, and employees) against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or in connection with such LPAC member\'s service on the LPAC, except to the extent such losses are the result of fraud, bad faith, or willful misconduct by such LPAC member.

\(a\) Each LPAC member shall be bound by the confidentiality obligations set forth in Section 15.4 of this Agreement with respect to all information received in connection with LPAC service, including information regarding the Fund\'s investments, Portfolio Companies, other Limited Partners, and the General Partner\'s proprietary investment processes.

\(b\) Notwithstanding the foregoing, LPAC members that are governmental plan investors or other public entities may disclose confidential information to the extent required by applicable public records laws, freedom of information acts, or other mandatory disclosure obligations, *provided* that such LPAC member shall provide advance written notice to the General Partner (to the extent practicable and permitted by law) of any such required disclosure and shall cooperate with the General Partner in seeking to minimize the scope of such disclosure or to obtain confidential treatment.

\(b\) No Limited Partner shall participate in the management or control of the Partnership\'s business, transact any business on behalf of the Partnership, or have any power to sign for or bind the Partnership. No Limited Partner shall be deemed to be participating in the control of the Partnership\'s business within the meaning of Section 17-303 of the Act by virtue of exercising any right or power granted to Limited Partners under this Agreement (including voting rights, consent rights, and rights to participate on the LPAC).

The General Partner and its Associates shall be entitled to rely, and shall be fully protected in relying, upon information, opinions, reports, or statements (including financial statements and information, and opinions, reports, or statements as to the value or amount of assets, liabilities, profits, or losses of the Partnership or any facts pertinent to the existence and amount of assets from which distributions might properly be paid) of the following Persons or groups: (a) one or more officers or employees of the General Partner or the Sponsor whom the General Partner reasonably believes to be reliable and competent in the matters presented; (b) any attorney, independent accountant, appraiser, or other expert or advisor (including Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Caldwell, Fitch & Hartley LLP) whom the General Partner reasonably believes to be qualified in the matters presented; and (c) any committee of the LPAC acting within the scope of its authority.

\(c\) The Sponsor shall not raise or commence fundraising for a successor private equity fund during the Investment Period until at least \[seventy-five percent (75%)\] of the Fund\'s Aggregate Commitments have been invested or committed to Portfolio Investments. \[*Note: The successor fund restriction percentage is bracketed and remains subject to further discussion.*\] For purposes of this provision, \"committed\" shall include amounts that are subject to binding commitments (including signed letters of intent or purchase agreements) but that have not yet been funded.

\(d\) In the event of a conflict between the interests of the Partnership and the interests of any other fund, account, or vehicle managed by the Sponsor or its Affiliates, the General Partner shall resolve such conflict in a manner that it reasonably determines to be fair and equitable to the Partnership, subject to the LPAC\'s authority to review and approve conflicts of interest and related-party transactions as set forth in Section 11.3(b)(i).

> \(ii\) The Limited Partners shall have the right to appoint a successor general partner within one hundred eighty (180) days of the effective date of removal, and the removed General Partner shall cooperate in the orderly transition of management responsibilities to such successor;

> \(iii\) The removed General Partner shall be entitled to receive Carried Interest on Portfolio Investments made prior to the effective date of removal, subject to such modifications (including potential reduction of the Carried Interest percentage) as may be negotiated among the removed General Partner, the successor general partner, and the Limited Partners;
> \(iv\) The Management Fee shall cease to accrue as of the effective date of removal; and
> \(v\) The removed General Partner shall be entitled to receive any accrued and unpaid Management Fee through the effective date of removal.
> \(iii\) The Management Fee shall cease to accrue as of the effective date of removal;

> \(i\) The Limited Partners initiating the removal vote shall deliver written notice to the General Partner and all other Limited Partners specifying the basis for removal (in the case of a For-Cause Removal) and the proposed effective date of removal;

> \(iv\) The effective date of removal shall be not less than ninety (90) days following the date on which the requisite vote is obtained (unless the General Partner agrees to an earlier effective date).
\(c\) The removal of the General Partner pursuant to Section 12.6, if no successor general partner is appointed within one hundred eighty (180) days of the effective date of removal;
No Transfer of a Partnership Interest shall be effective unless all of the following conditions are satisfied:

\(a\) The proposed transferee shall have executed an assignment and assumption agreement in the form attached hereto as Exhibit C (or in such other form as the General Partner may prescribe), pursuant to which the transferee assumes all obligations of the transferor with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest;

A transferee of all or any portion of a Partnership Interest shall be admitted as a substitute Limited Partner of the Partnership (a **\"Substitute Limited Partner\"**) only upon (a) the General Partner\'s consent to the Transfer (to the extent required under Section 14.1), (b) the satisfaction of all conditions set forth in Section 14.2, and (c) the execution by the transferee of a joinder or counterpart to this Agreement and such other documents as the General Partner may reasonably require. \(a\) The Partnership shall, to the fullest extent permitted by the Act and applicable law, indemnify and hold harmless the General Partner, its members, managers, officers, directors, employees, and agents (including Associates, Key Persons, and LPAC members) (collectively, **\"Indemnified Persons\"**) against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees, judgments, fines, settlement amounts, and other expenses incurred in connection with the investigation, preparation, defense, or settlement of any pending or threatened claim, action, suit, or proceeding, whether civil, criminal, administrative, or investigative) arising out of or in connection with the activities of the Partnership, the General Partner\'s management of the Partnership, or any act or omission of an Indemnified Person in connection with the affairs of the Partnership, *except* to the extent that such losses are determined by a final, non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction to have been caused by such Indemnified Person\'s fraud, gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material breach of this Agreement.

\(b\) Notices shall be effective (i) when delivered by hand, (ii) one (1) Business Day after being sent by overnight courier, (iii) three (3) Business Days after being sent by registered or certified mail, or (iv) when sent by email (provided that confirmation of receipt is obtained by the sender).

This Agreement (together with the Subscription Agreements executed by each Limited Partner, the Side Letters entered into between the General Partner and the respective Limited Partners, and the Schedules and Exhibits attached hereto) constitutes the entire agreement among the Partners with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements, understandings, representations, and warranties (whether oral or written) among the Partners with respect to such subject matter. No Partner has relied on any representation or warranty not set forth in this Agreement or in the applicable Subscription Agreement.
**[Section 15.11 --- Counterparts; Electronic Signatures]{.underline}**

This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page to this Agreement by facsimile transmission, email (including .pdf format), or other electronic means shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart. Electronic signatures (including signatures compliant with the U.S. Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act (E-SIGN) and the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (UETA)) shall be valid and binding for all purposes of this Agreement.
\(a\) No waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless made in a writing signed by the Partner or Partners against whom such waiver is sought to be enforced.

\(d\) The General Partner shall administer the MFN election process in good faith and shall promptly notify each electing Limited Partner of the outcome of its election. Elected Side Letter provisions shall be deemed to supplement this Agreement with respect to the electing Limited Partner, effective as of the date of the Final Close.
**\[SIGNATURE PAGES FOLLOW\]**
**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the undersigned have executed this Agreement of Limited Partnership as of the date of the First Close.

Each Limited Partner has executed a Subscription Agreement containing a signature page and joinder to this Agreement, which Subscription Agreements are incorporated herein by this reference. The signature of each Limited Partner on its respective Subscription Agreement shall constitute such Limited Partner\'s execution of, and agreement to be bound by, this Agreement of Limited Partnership.

Note: The proportionate share of Carried Interest attributable to each Clawback Guarantor will be determined in accordance with the internal Carried Interest allocation arrangements of Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, as disclosed to the LPAC. Each Clawback Guarantor\'s personal guarantee is limited to the after-tax amount of Carried Interest actually received (and not previously returned) by such Clawback Guarantor.

**Geographic Focus**                                       Primarily North American (United States and Canada); non-North American investments not to exceed \[20%\] of Aggregate Commitments without LPAC consent
**Hostile Acquisitions**                                   Not permitted without LPAC consent
**Affiliate Transactions**                                 Not permitted without LPAC consent and majority LP consent

*The form of Transfer Agreement to be executed by transferors and transferees of Partnership Interests pursuant to Article XIV of this Agreement is set forth in a separate document and is incorporated herein by reference. A copy of the form of Transfer Agreement will be made available to each Limited Partner upon request to the General Partner.*

*The form of Subscription Agreement (including the investor questionnaire, representations and warranties, and joinder to the Agreement of Limited Partnership) to be executed by each Limited Partner in connection with its admission to the Partnership pursuant to Article III of this Agreement is set forth in a separate document and is incorporated herein by reference. A copy of the form of Subscription Agreement will be provided to each prospective Limited Partner in connection with the offering and sale of Partnership Interests.*

matches.line: **[LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE CHARTER AND TERMS OF REFERENCE]{.underline}**
**Effective as of the date of the First Close** (Target: August 15, 2025)

This Limited Partner Advisory Committee Charter and Terms of Reference (this \"Charter\") is adopted by the General Partner of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership, pursuant to Section 11.1 of the Agreement of Limited Partnership of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, dated as of August 15, 2025 (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"Partnership Agreement\" or \"LPA\").
**Section 1.1 --- Establishment of the LPAC**

The General Partner hereby establishes a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\" or the \"Committee\") for Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP. The LPAC is established to serve in a consultative and advisory capacity to the General Partner on certain matters as set forth herein and in the Partnership Agreement, and to foster transparency and constructive dialogue between the General Partner and the Fund\'s Limited Partners regarding Fund governance, potential conflicts of interest, and other matters of significance to the Fund\'s investor base.

The LPAC is not a governing body of the Fund and does not have the authority to manage, control, or direct the business and affairs of the Fund, which authority is vested exclusively in the General Partner pursuant to the Partnership Agreement and applicable Delaware law, including the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 *et seq.*). The establishment of the LPAC shall not alter or diminish the powers and authority of the General Partner as set forth in the Partnership Agreement or give rise to any inference that the LPAC exercises control over, or participates in the control of, the Fund\'s business.
The LPAC is established for the following purposes:

> \(e\) To serve as a forum for communication and consultation between the General Partner and the Limited Partners on matters of Fund governance, operations, fees and expenses, and such other matters as the General Partner may, in its discretion, bring before the LPAC; and

For the avoidance of doubt, the LPAC\'s role is advisory and consultative in nature, except where the Partnership Agreement expressly requires the LPAC\'s approval or consent as a condition to the General Partner taking or refraining from taking a specified action. Fiduciary duties do not attach to LPAC Members in their capacity as such, and LPAC Members shall not be deemed to be agents, trustees, or fiduciaries of the Fund, the General Partner, or any other Limited Partner by reason of their service on the LPAC.

The LPAC shall consist of five (5) members (each, a \"Member\" and, collectively, the \"Members\"). Three (3) Members shall be designated at the First Close of the Fund. The remaining two (2) Members shall be designated by the General Partner, in consultation with the existing Members, at subsequent closings or as vacancies arise, but in any event no later than the Final Close Deadline (February 15, 2027). In the period between the First Close and the designation of the fourth and fifth Members, the LPAC shall function with three (3) Members, and all quorum and voting thresholds shall be adjusted accordingly as set forth in Article III.
The following Limited Partners (or their designated representatives) are anticipated to be designated as the initial three (3) Members of the LPAC at the First Close:

Each initial Member\'s appointment to the LPAC is subject to confirmation upon such Member\'s execution and delivery of its respective Subscription Agreement and any applicable Side Letter to the General Partner. In the event that any anticipated initial Member does not execute a Subscription Agreement at or prior to the First Close, the General Partner shall designate a replacement Member from among the Limited Partners admitted at the First Close.

Members shall be selected from among Limited Partners with meaningful capital commitments to the Fund. In selecting Members, the General Partner shall endeavor to maintain a diverse and representative LPAC that reflects the breadth and composition of the Fund\'s investor base, including, as applicable, representation from among pension plans, endowments and foundations, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, funds of funds, family offices, and other institutional investors.

LPAC membership is available to investors in the Main Fund (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP), the Parallel Fund (Harrowgate Fund V Parallel LP), and the Offshore Feeder (Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP), as each such vehicle invests alongside the Main Fund on a pro rata basis and participates in the same investment program. A Limited Partner\'s membership in the LPAC shall not be conditioned upon its investment through any particular vehicle within the fund complex.

The General Partner may, in its sole discretion, grant observer status to one or more Limited Partners, permitting such Limited Partners (through their designated representatives) to attend LPAC meetings in a non-voting, advisory capacity. Observers shall not be counted for purposes of determining a quorum and shall not have the right to vote on any matter presented to the LPAC, but may participate in discussions at the invitation of the General Partner or the Members. Observers shall be bound by the same confidentiality obligations applicable to Members as set forth in Article VII of this Charter.

The General Partner acknowledges that certain Side Letters may provide for LPAC observer rights. By way of example, the Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority has been granted LPAC observer rights pursuant to its negotiated Side Letter, and such rights shall be honored in accordance with the terms thereof, subject to the confidentiality and other provisions of this Charter.

Each Member shall designate one (1) individual to serve as its representative on the LPAC (the \"Designated Representative\") and one (1) alternate representative (the \"Alternate Representative\"). The Designated Representative shall be the primary attendee at LPAC meetings and shall have full authority to act and vote on behalf of such Member. In the absence or unavailability of the Designated Representative, the Alternate Representative shall be entitled to attend and participate in meetings and to cast votes on behalf of such Member with the same authority as the Designated Representative.

All designations and changes of Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives shall be communicated in writing (including by email) to the General Partner, to the attention of Rachel M. Overton, Partner, Head of Investor Relations, Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, and shall be effective upon receipt by the General Partner. The General Partner shall maintain a current register of Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives.

Each Member shall serve on the LPAC for the duration of the Fund Term (including any extension thereof), unless such Member earlier resigns, is removed, or ceases to be a Limited Partner in the Fund (including by reason of a full transfer of its limited partnership interest in the Fund). A Member that transfers all of its limited partnership interest in the Fund (whether pursuant to a secondary sale or otherwise) shall automatically cease to be a Member of the LPAC effective as of the date of such transfer, without the necessity of any further action by the General Partner or the LPAC.

A Member that transfers a portion, but not all, of its limited partnership interest in the Fund shall retain its LPAC membership, provided that such Member continues to hold a limited partnership interest in the Fund following such partial transfer.

> \(a\) **Resignation.** A Member may resign from the LPAC at any time by delivering written notice of resignation to the General Partner. Such resignation shall be effective upon receipt by the General Partner or such later date as may be specified in the notice.

> \(iii\) such Member (or its Designated Representative or Alternate Representative) fails to attend three (3) consecutive regularly scheduled meetings of the LPAC without designating an alternate or otherwise providing prior notice of non-attendance to the General Partner; or

> \(c\) **Process.** Replacement Members shall be selected by the General Partner in consultation with the remaining LPAC Members. The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that the composition of the LPAC continues to satisfy the diversity and representativeness objectives set forth in Section 2.3.

Vacancies on the LPAC arising from resignation, removal, or any other cause shall be filled by the General Partner after consultation with the existing Members. The General Partner shall endeavor to fill any vacancy within sixty (60) days of the date on which such vacancy arises. During any period in which a vacancy exists and the remaining number of Members is fewer than five (5), the LPAC shall continue to function, and quorum and voting thresholds shall be determined by reference to the number of Members then serving.

The LPAC shall meet at least two (2) times per calendar year at such times as the General Partner shall determine. Additional meetings may be called by the General Partner at any time, or upon the written request of at least two (2) Members specifying the purpose of the requested meeting. The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to schedule meetings at times that accommodate the schedules of the Members. The General Partner\'s principal contact for LPAC coordination and scheduling shall be Rachel M. Overton, Partner, Head of Investor Relations, Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC (email: r.overton@harrowgatecapital.com; telephone: (302) 555-1200).

In the event of exigent circumstances requiring urgent LPAC action (for example, a time-sensitive conflict-of-interest transaction), the General Partner may provide shorter notice, provided that the General Partner uses commercially reasonable efforts to provide as much advance notice as is practicable under the circumstances and that no fewer than two (2) business days\' notice is given.

Meetings of the LPAC may be held in person at the offices of Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC at 1200 Concord Pike, Suite 600, Wilmington, Delaware 19803, or at such other location as designated by the General Partner, or by teleconference or videoconference, or any combination thereof. Members may participate in any meeting by means of conference telephone, video conferencing platform (e.g., Calderon Software, Northgate Data Systems), or similar communications equipment that allows all participants to hear each other at the same time, and such participation shall constitute presence in person at such meeting for all purposes under this Charter.

A quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the Members then serving. By way of illustration, when all five (5) seats on the LPAC are filled, a quorum shall consist of three (3) Members; when only three (3) seats are filled (as may be the case between the First Close and the designation of the fourth and fifth Members), a quorum shall consist of two (2) Members. For purposes of determining a quorum, a Member shall be deemed present if the Member\'s Designated Representative or Alternate Representative is in attendance (whether in person, by teleconference, or by videoconference). Observers shall not be counted for purposes of determining a quorum.

Each Member shall have one (1) vote on each matter submitted to the LPAC for a vote, regardless of the size of such Member\'s capital commitment to the Fund. Except as otherwise expressly provided herein or in the Partnership Agreement, actions of the LPAC shall require the affirmative vote of a majority of the Members present at a meeting at which a quorum is constituted.

Action may be taken by the LPAC without a meeting by unanimous written consent, circulated by the General Partner and executed (including by electronic signature or email confirmation) by all Members then serving. Any action so taken shall have the same force and effect as if taken at a duly convened meeting of the LPAC. The General Partner shall retain the original or electronic copies of all written consents in the Fund\'s records.

In the event of a tie vote (which may occur if the LPAC has an even number of Members then serving due to a vacancy), the matter in question shall be deemed not approved, and the General Partner may request that the matter be reconsidered at a subsequent meeting or by written consent.

The General Partner shall prepare and circulate the agenda for each meeting of the LPAC together with the notice of such meeting. Any Member may request that items be added to the agenda by written notice to the General Partner delivered at least five (5) business days before the meeting. The General Partner shall use reasonable efforts to accommodate such requests but reserves the right to defer items to a subsequent meeting if, in the General Partner\'s reasonable judgment, the requested item is not time-sensitive or if adequate materials cannot be prepared in advance.

The General Partner shall provide Members with relevant materials in advance of the meeting, including, as applicable, conflict-of-interest descriptions and analyses, valuation reports and summaries, supporting documentation for any matter requiring LPAC approval or consent, portfolio summaries, fee and expense reports, and such other information as the General Partner deems appropriate or as any Member may reasonably request. To the extent practicable, materials shall be provided at least five (5) business days in advance of the meeting to afford Members adequate time for review.

The General Partner (or its designee) shall prepare minutes of each meeting of the LPAC. Minutes shall include a summary of the matters discussed, the text of any resolutions adopted, the vote of each Member on each matter submitted to a vote, and a record of attendance. Draft minutes shall be circulated to all Members who attended the meeting for review within twenty (20) business days following the meeting. Members shall have ten (10) business days from receipt of draft minutes to submit comments or corrections. Minutes shall be finalized upon the approval of a majority of the Members who attended the meeting to which the minutes relate. Finalized minutes shall be maintained by the General Partner as part of the Fund\'s books and records.

Representatives of the General Partner and the Sponsor, including Marcus J. Harrowgate (Managing Partner), Diana R. Castellano (Partner, Co-Head of Investments), Jonathan P. Birch (Partner), and Catherine E. Loomis (General Counsel & Chief Compliance Officer), may attend all meetings of the LPAC in a non-voting capacity and shall be available to respond to questions and present information to the Members.

The LPAC may request that certain portions of a meeting be held without representatives of the General Partner present (an \"Executive Session\"). In such event, the General Partner and its representatives shall withdraw from the meeting for the duration of the Executive Session. The Members present during the Executive Session may request that notes of any matters discussed or actions taken during the Executive Session be included (or excluded, as applicable) in the formal minutes. The General Partner shall cooperate in good faith with any reasonable request for an Executive Session.

The LPAC shall review and, where required by the Partnership Agreement, approve or consent to transactions involving actual or potential conflicts of interest between the General Partner (or its affiliates, principals, or related persons) and the Fund or the Limited Partners. Such conflicts of interest transactions include, but are not limited to, the following:

In connection with any conflict-of-interest matter presented to the LPAC, the General Partner shall provide the LPAC with a written description of the transaction, the nature and extent of the conflict, the terms of the proposed transaction, and the General Partner\'s assessment of whether the transaction is fair and reasonable to the Fund and its Limited Partners. The LPAC\'s approval of a conflict-of-interest transaction shall constitute the approval contemplated by the applicable provisions of the Partnership Agreement and shall be documented in the minutes of the meeting at which such approval is granted (or, if by written consent, in the written consent).

The General Partner shall present to the LPAC, at least annually (and more frequently at the General Partner\'s discretion), the methodologies and conclusions of the Fund\'s portfolio valuation, as determined by the General Partner in its reasonable discretion and in accordance with the valuation policies set forth in the Partnership Agreement. The presentation shall include a summary of the fair value of each material portfolio investment, the valuation methodology applied (including comparable company analysis, discounted cash flow analysis, precedent transaction analysis, and any other methodology employed), and any material changes in methodology from the prior valuation period.

The LPAC may review and comment on valuation methodologies and may engage, at the Fund\'s expense and with the prior consent of the General Partner (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld), an independent valuation firm to review specific portfolio company valuations or the General Partner\'s overall valuation methodology. Any such engagement shall be conducted in accordance with the confidentiality and expense provisions of this Charter.

The Fund\'s independent auditor, Caldwell, Fitch & Hartley LLP (Audit Partner: Robert A. Fonseca), shall provide the annual audited financial statements of the Fund, which the LPAC may review and discuss with the auditor at any LPAC meeting. The General Partner shall facilitate the auditor\'s availability for such discussions at the LPAC\'s reasonable request.

Valuation review by the LPAC is consultative in nature. The General Partner retains final authority over all valuations of the Fund\'s portfolio investments, subject to the terms and conditions of the Partnership Agreement and the audit of the Fund\'s financial statements by the Fund\'s independent auditor.

The term of the Fund (the \"Fund Term\") is ten (10) years from the Final Close, subject to extension as set forth in the Partnership Agreement. The General Partner is entitled, at its sole discretion, to extend the Fund Term for up to two (2) successive one-year periods (the \"Discretionary Extensions\"). Following the expiration of the Discretionary Extensions, one (1) additional one-year extension of the Fund Term (the \"Third Extension\") requires the prior approval of the LPAC.

The LPAC\'s approval of the Third Extension shall require the affirmative vote of a majority of the Members then serving (whether at a meeting at which a quorum is present or by unanimous written consent). The General Partner shall provide at least ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the LPAC before requesting approval of the Third Extension, together with a written explanation of the reasons for the requested extension, a summary of the Fund\'s remaining portfolio investments and anticipated disposition timeline, and any other information that the General Partner deems relevant to the LPAC\'s consideration.
The LPAC may, upon the request of the General Partner, waive or modify certain investment restrictions set forth in the Partnership Agreement, including, but not limited to, the following:

Any waiver or modification of an investment restriction shall require the affirmative vote of a majority of the Members then serving and shall be documented in writing (whether in the minutes of the meeting at which such waiver is approved or in a separate written consent). The General Partner shall provide the LPAC with a detailed written request for any such waiver, including a description of the proposed investment or transaction, the specific restriction to be waived, the rationale for the waiver, and the General Partner\'s assessment of the risks and benefits to the Fund.

The General Partner shall promptly notify the LPAC of any Key Person Event as defined in the Partnership Agreement. A \"Key Person Event\" occurs if either Marcus J. Harrowgate or Diana R. Castellano ceases to devote substantially all of his or her professional time and effort to the investment activities of the Fund, including by reason of death, disability, departure from the Sponsor, or any other circumstance specified in the Partnership Agreement.

Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event, the LPAC may consult with the General Partner regarding the cure or remediation of such event, including the identification of replacement investment professionals, the modification of investment strategy, or any other measures that the General Partner may propose to address the Key Person Event. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the ultimate determination of whether a Key Person Event has been cured or waived rests with a majority-in-interest of the Limited Partners as provided in the Partnership Agreement, and the LPAC does not have independent authority to waive or cure a Key Person Event on behalf of the Limited Partners.

The LPAC may serve as a consultative body in connection with any proposal for the removal of the General Partner, whether on a no-fault basis (requiring the affirmative vote of seventy-five percent (75%) in interest of the Limited Partners, excluding commitments held by the General Partner or its affiliates) or for cause (requiring the affirmative vote of a majority in interest of the Limited Partners upon a determination of fraud, willful misconduct, material breach of the Partnership Agreement, or a Bankruptcy Event of the General Partner).

The LPAC does not independently exercise removal authority over the General Partner; such authority is reserved exclusively to the Limited Partners as provided in the Partnership Agreement. The LPAC may, however, facilitate communication among the Limited Partners and the General Partner in connection with any removal proceeding and may provide its views and recommendations to the Limited Partners on a consultative basis.
The General Partner shall present to the LPAC, at least annually, a comprehensive report on fees and expenses of the Fund, including the following:

The LPAC may inquire into any fee or expense matter and may request supporting documentation, invoices, or further detail from the General Partner. The General Partner shall respond to such inquiries in a timely manner, subject to applicable confidentiality obligations and privileges.
The LPAC may review the application of the Fund\'s distribution waterfall, which is structured on a European-style (whole-fund) basis, including the following elements:

The LPAC\'s role in waterfall matters is consultative and informational. The General Partner shall provide the LPAC with periodic updates on the status of the distribution waterfall, including cumulative contributions, distributions, unrealized value, and the General Partner\'s current carried interest entitlement.

The General Partner may, in its sole discretion, consult the LPAC on any other matter relating to the Fund\'s operations, governance, investment strategy, portfolio management, ESG (environmental, social, and governance) policies, or any other subject that the General Partner deems appropriate for LPAC discussion. The LPAC may, through its Members, raise any governance or operational matter for discussion with the General Partner, and the General Partner shall consider such matters in good faith.

Nothing in this Charter shall be construed to grant the LPAC managerial authority over the Fund or to impose upon the General Partner any obligation to follow, adopt, or implement any recommendation or advice of the LPAC, except where the Partnership Agreement expressly conditions the General Partner\'s actions upon the prior approval or consent of the LPAC.

The LPAC\'s authority and advisory role extend to matters affecting Harrowgate Fund V Parallel LP (the \"Parallel Fund\") and Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP (the \"Offshore Feeder\"), each of which invests alongside the Main Fund on a pro rata basis and participates in the same investment program, to the extent that such matters arise under or in connection with the Partnership Agreement or the constituent documents of the Parallel Fund or the Offshore Feeder. The LPAC is intended to serve as a single advisory committee for the entire fund complex, and separate advisory committees are not anticipated for the Parallel Fund or the Offshore Feeder.

Investors in the Parallel Fund or the Offshore Feeder that are LPAC Members or observers shall exercise such capacity with respect to decisions affecting the overall fund complex, and their rights and obligations as Members or observers shall be coextensive with those of Members or observers investing through the Main Fund.

Matters relating to HGF V blocker Corp. (the \"Blocker\"), a Delaware C corporation established for certain tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors to mitigate unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") exposure, that involve conflicts of interest or are otherwise within the LPAC\'s scope of authority and advisory responsibility under Article IV of this Charter, shall be reported to the LPAC. The LPAC shall have the same consultative and approval rights with respect to such matters as it has with respect to the Main Fund, to the extent applicable.

LPAC Members shall receive no compensation from the Fund, the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any affiliate thereof for their service on the LPAC. Membership on the LPAC is undertaken on a voluntary basis as part of the Fund\'s governance framework.

Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by LPAC Members in connection with attendance at LPAC meetings, including travel, lodging, and meals, shall be reimbursable by the Fund as a Fund expense, to the extent approved by the General Partner. Members seeking reimbursement shall submit documentation of such expenses to the General Partner in accordance with the Fund\'s expense reimbursement policies.

Any engagement of independent advisors by the LPAC, including independent valuation firms, legal counsel, or other professionals, shall require the prior written consent of the General Partner (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), and the costs thereof shall be borne by the Fund as a Fund expense. The General Partner shall cooperate with the LPAC in the selection and engagement of any such independent advisors.

Each Member (and each observer) shall maintain the confidentiality of all non-public information received in connection with its service on the LPAC (\"Confidential Information\"), including, but not limited to:
> \(d\) conflict-of-interest disclosures and the substance of any LPAC deliberations related thereto;

Each Member shall use Confidential Information solely for purposes of fulfilling its responsibilities as a Member of the LPAC and shall not disclose Confidential Information to any third party except as permitted under Section 7.2. Each Member shall take reasonable precautions to protect the confidentiality of Confidential Information, using at least the same degree of care that such Member uses to protect its own confidential information of similar importance.

LPAC Members do not owe fiduciary duties to the Fund, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner by reason of their service on the LPAC. LPAC Members act solely in their capacity as representatives of their respective Limited Partners, and their service on the LPAC shall not create or be deemed to create a relationship of principal and agent, trustee and beneficiary, or any other fiduciary relationship between such Members and the Fund, the General Partner, any other Limited Partner, or any portfolio company. This Section 8.1 is consistent with and supplements the elimination and modification of fiduciary duties set forth in the Partnership Agreement to the fullest extent permitted by the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act.

No Member shall be liable to the Fund, the General Partner, any Limited Partner, or any other person for any act or omission taken or suffered in good faith in connection with its service on the LPAC, including any approval, consent, waiver, recommendation, vote, or abstention given, withheld, or made, except in the case of such Member\'s fraud, willful misconduct, or bad faith. No Member shall be liable for any action or inaction of the General Partner, for the investment decisions of the Fund, or for the performance of any portfolio investment, whether or not such action, inaction, or decision was the subject of LPAC review or approval.

The Fund shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless each Member and its Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives (collectively, \"Indemnified LPAC Persons\") against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, judgments, fines, penalties, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses of investigation) arising out of or relating to such Indemnified LPAC Person\'s service on the LPAC, to the fullest extent permitted by the Partnership Agreement and applicable Delaware law, except to the extent that such losses, claims, damages, liabilities, or expenses result from the Indemnified LPAC Person\'s fraud, willful misconduct, or bad faith.

The General Partner may, in its discretion, cause the Fund to obtain directors\' and officers\' liability insurance or similar liability insurance covering LPAC Members and their Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives in connection with their service on the LPAC, the cost of which shall be borne as a Fund expense. The General Partner shall inform the LPAC of the existence, scope, and material terms of any such insurance policy upon request.

This Charter may be amended, modified, or supplemented by the General Partner with the prior approval of a majority of the LPAC Members then serving. All amendments shall be in writing and shall be effective upon execution by the General Partner and delivery of written notice to all Members (and observers, if applicable). No amendment to this Charter shall diminish the rights of any Member under this Charter without such Member\'s prior written consent, unless such diminution applies equally to all Members.

For the avoidance of doubt, amendments to the Partnership Agreement that affect the authority, composition, or responsibilities of the LPAC shall be governed by the amendment provisions of the Partnership Agreement, and any resulting changes to this Charter shall be adopted in accordance with this Section 9.1.

Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising under, out of, or in connection with this Charter, including any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination, shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware lacks subject matter jurisdiction, the Superior Court of the State of Delaware, New Castle County), consistent with the dispute resolution provisions of the Partnership Agreement. Each Member, by accepting appointment to the LPAC, consents to the personal jurisdiction of such courts and waives any objection to venue therein.

This Charter, together with the Partnership Agreement and any applicable Side Letters, constitutes the entire understanding among the General Partner and the LPAC Members with respect to the establishment, composition, authority, and operation of the LPAC. This Charter supersedes all prior discussions, negotiations, and agreements, whether written or oral, relating to the subject matter hereof.

**AGREEMENT OF LIMITED PARTNERSHIP**
**HARROWGATE PRIVATE EQUITY FUND V LP**

This Agreement of Limited Partnership (this **\"Agreement\"**) of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the **\"Partnership\"** or the **\"Fund\"**), is entered into as of the date of the First Close (as defined below) by and among Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as the general partner (the **\"General Partner\"** or **\"GP\"**), and each Person who is admitted as a limited partner of the Partnership (each, a **\"Limited Partner\"** or **\"LP\"** and, collectively, the **\"Limited Partners\"**), in each case in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth herein. The General Partner and the Limited Partners are sometimes referred to herein individually as a **\"Partner\"** and collectively as the **\"Partners.\"**
**RECITALS**

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner has caused a Certificate of Limited Partnership to be filed (or to be filed on or prior to the date hereof) with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, forming the Partnership as a limited partnership under and pursuant to the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. § 17-101 *et seq.*, as amended from time to time (the **\"Act\"**);

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner desires to establish the Fund as a private equity investment vehicle for the purpose of making equity and equity-related investments, directly or indirectly, primarily in North American mid-market and upper-mid-market companies in the industrials, business services, healthcare services, and technology-enabled services sectors;

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner is the sole general partner of the Partnership and is a Delaware limited liability company, the sole member of which is Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the **\"Sponsor\"**);

**WHEREAS**, the Sponsor has sponsored and managed four predecessor private equity funds (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund I LP through Harrowgate Private Equity Fund IV LP) and manages approximately \$5.8 billion in aggregate assets under management as of the date hereof;

This Certificate is delivered pursuant to, and in accordance with, the authority vested in the General Partner under the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of the Partnership dated as of March 15, 2017 (as defined below, the \"A&R LPA\"), and is based upon the following recitals of fact and the certifications set forth herein.

Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (\"DARF\" or the \"Partnership\") is a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership duly registered under the Exempted Limited Partnership Act (As Revised) of the Cayman Islands, bearing Registration No. ELP-87234, with its registered office located at 4th Floor, Harbour Place, 103 South Church Street, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1104, Cayman Islands. The Partnership was originally formed pursuant to an Agreement of Limited Partnership dated as of November 2, 2015, which was subsequently amended and restated in its entirety by the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement dated as of March 15, 2017 (the \"A&R LPA\"). The A&R LPA is governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware, as provided in Section 15.02 thereof.

As of the date hereof, the Partnership has forty-seven (47) Limited Partners who have been admitted to the Partnership in accordance with the terms and conditions of the A&R LPA and the relevant subscription agreements. The General Partner confirms that no additional Limited Partners have been admitted, and no existing Limited Partners have withdrawn or been removed, since the date of the Key Person Event (as defined below).

Pursuant to Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA, a \"Key Person Event\" is deemed to have occurred if the Key Person \"is unable to devote substantially all of his professional time to the affairs of the Partnership for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days, whether by reason of death, permanent disability, incapacitation, resignation, removal, or any other cause.\" The seven (7) consecutive calendar day period commenced on June 3, 2024 and expired on June 10, 2024. Accordingly, the Key Person Event was deemed triggered on June 10, 2024 (i.e., seven consecutive calendar days following June 3, 2024) (the \"Key Person Event Date\").

Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA provides that: (i) the Investment Period of the Partnership shall be automatically suspended; (ii) the General Partner shall not make any new portfolio investments on behalf of the Partnership, provided that the General Partner may make follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions in an aggregate amount not exceeding \$28.7 million (representing 1.0% of the Partnership\'s assets under management as of the most recent quarterly valuation); and (iii) a 90-calendar-day cure period (the \"Cure Period\") shall commence on the Key Person Event Date, during which the General Partner may propose one or more Successor Key Persons for approval by the Limited Partners. The Cure Period commenced on June 10, 2024 and was set to expire on September 8, 2024.

The General Partner delivered written notice of the Key Person Event (the \"Key Person Event Notice\") to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners of the Partnership on June 14, 2024, which date was within the required five (5) business day notification period. The Key Person Event Notice was delivered by electronic mail transmission to the notice addresses on file for each Limited Partner, with a copy delivered by international courier (Granite Harbor Enterprises) to each Limited Partner\'s physical notice address, in each case as set forth in the records of the Partnership and in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 16.01 of the A&R LPA. The Key Person Event Notice described: (i) the nature of the Key Person Event; (ii) the suspension of the Investment Period; (iii) the restrictions on new portfolio investments; (iv) the commencement and expiration of the Cure Period; and (v) the General Partner\'s intention to propose one or more Successor Key Persons during the Cure Period.

Following extensive consultations with the members of the Investor Advisory Committee (as described in Recital G below), the General Partner proposed Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons for the Partnership. Ms. Sato currently serves as Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding 10% of the membership interests) of DCM. She has been with DCM since its formation in 2015 and has been a senior member of the investment team throughout the life of the Partnership. Mr. Huang currently serves as Head of Credit Strategies of DCM. He joined DCM in 2017 and has served in roles of progressively increasing responsibility within the investment team, most recently overseeing all credit-related investment strategies of the Partnership.

> \(i\) a Successor Key Person Proposal letter, dated July 15, 2024, setting forth the qualifications, experience, and proposed roles of Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons, together with biographical information and investment track records for each proposed Successor Key Person (the \"Successor Proposal\");

> \(iii\) a Form of Written Consent of Limited Partners (the \"Form of Written Consent\"), to be executed and returned by each consenting Limited Partner on or before the LP Consent Deadline (as defined in Recital F below).

> \(c\) *Establishment of Investment Committee.* A new Section 8.05 is added to the A&R LPA, establishing a three-member Investment Committee of the Partnership. The Investment Committee shall consist of: (1) Elaine R. Sato, who shall serve as Chair of the Investment Committee; (2) Jonathan K. Huang; and (3) one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee of the Partnership pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA. All new portfolio investments by the Partnership in excess of \$5.0 million shall require the approval of at least two (2) of the three (3) members of the Investment Committee. The Investment Committee shall meet no less frequently than bi-weekly during the first twelve (12) months following the Amendment Effective Date.

> \(e\) *Designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor.* Marcus J. Whitmore is designated as \"Senior Advisor\" to the Partnership and to the General Partner, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date. In such capacity, Mr. Whitmore shall have no governance authority, no voting rights with respect to any matter requiring the action or consent of the General Partner, and no authority to bind the Partnership or the General Partner. Mr. Whitmore\'s role as Senior Advisor shall be limited to providing non-binding advisory input on investment matters, to the extent his health permits, and shall be subject to the terms and conditions of a separate Senior Advisor Agreement between Mr. Whitmore and DCM.

> Mr. Whitmore\'s carried interest shall vest on a modified schedule as follows: fifty percent (50%) of Mr. Whitmore\'s carried interest allocation shall be deemed vested immediately as of the Key Person Event Date (June 10, 2024); the remaining fifty percent (50%) shall vest ratably on a monthly basis over thirty-six (36) months commencing on June 10, 2024, subject to continued compliance by Mr. Whitmore with the non-competition and non-solicitation covenants set forth in the Operating Agreement of DCM and the Senior Advisor Agreement.
As of the Certification Date, the aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments for purposes of the consent vote (the \"Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments\") are calculated as follows:

The General Partner established August 23, 2024 as the deadline by which all Forms of Written Consent were required to be received by the General Partner (the \"LP Consent Deadline\"). The LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024 represents forty (40) calendar days from the July 15, 2024 circulation date of the Successor Proposal, the First Amendment, and the Form of Written Consent. The forty-day consent period was determined by the General Partner to be reasonable and consistent with the time periods customarily afforded to Limited Partners in similar circumstances, and was within the Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024. The General Partner also delivered reminder notices to all Limited Partners who had not yet returned executed Forms of Written Consent on August 5, 2024 and August 12, 2024, respectively.

The Investor Advisory Committee (the \"IAC\") of the Partnership, established pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA, consists of five (5) members, each of whom is a representative of a Limited Partner of the Partnership. As of the date hereof, the members of the IAC are as follows:

The IAC reviewed the Successor Proposal, the First Amendment, and related materials at a meeting held on July 29, 2024, at the offices of Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, 51 West 52nd Street, 40th Floor, New York, NY 10019. The meeting was attended by all five IAC members (Ms. Cortland, Mr. Oshima, Ms. Mercer, Mr. Ashworth, and Ms. Al-Rashid) and by legal counsel to the IAC, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (Helen M. Calloway, Partner, and David Pineda, Senior Associate). Also in attendance at the invitation of the IAC were Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang, who presented their qualifications, investment philosophy, and proposed governance structure, and responded to questions from the IAC members and their legal counsel. The IAC meeting lasted approximately three hours and forty-five minutes. Following the presentation and discussion, the IAC unanimously confirmed that it did not object to the Successor Proposal or the First Amendment, and that the IAC would recommend to the Limited Partners that they approve the same. The IAC\'s recommendation was communicated to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners by separate letter from Ms. Cortland, as IAC Chair, dated August 1, 2024.

All thirty-eight (38) written consents were received by the General Partner on or before August 19, 2024, which date is four (4) calendar days prior to the LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024. No Forms of Written Consent were received by the General Partner after August 19, 2024 and on or before the LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024. No Forms of Written Consent were received by the General Partner after the LP Consent Deadline.

This Certificate, together with all exhibits and attachments hereto, shall be maintained with the books and records of the Partnership in accordance with Section 11.01 of the A&R LPA.
