This AMENDED AND RESTATED LIMITED PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT (this \"**Agreement**\" or \"**LPA**\") of Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P., a Delaware limited partnership (the \"**Partnership**\" or \"**Co-Invest LP**\"), EIN 93-4817265, is entered into and made effective as of January 30, 2026 (the \"**Effective Date**\"), by and among Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, EIN 93-4817302, as general partner of the Partnership (the \"**General Partner**\" or \"**GP**\"), and the persons listed on Schedule A hereto, each of which is admitted to the Partnership as a limited partner (each, a \"**Limited Partner**\" and collectively, the \"**Limited Partners**\").

\"**Acquisition**\" means the acquisition by AcquisitionCo of 100% of the issued and outstanding equity interests of Clarion Hospitality Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation, pursuant to the terms and conditions of that certain Stock Purchase Agreement, dated as of December 12, 2025, by and among AcquisitionCo, the sellers party thereto, and the other parties named therein.
\"**Closing Date**\" means January 30, 2026.

\"**Distributable Cash**\" means, as of any date of determination, the cash held by the Partnership that the GP determines, in its reasonable discretion, is available for distribution to the Partners after taking into account (a) any reserves that the GP determines in good faith are necessary or appropriate for the payment of Partnership debts, expenses, and obligations (whether actual, contingent, or anticipated), and (b) the working capital needs of the Partnership.

\"**Fiscal Year**\" means the calendar year (January 1 through December 31) or, in the case of the first Fiscal Year, the period commencing on the date of formation of the Partnership and ending on December 31 of the year of formation, and in the case of the last Fiscal Year, the period commencing on January 1 of the year of dissolution and ending on the date of the final liquidating distribution.
\"**LPAC**\" or \"**Limited Partner Advisory Committee**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 9.1.

\(f\) References to any statute or statutory provision include any statute or statutory provision that amends, extends, consolidates, or replaces the same, or that has been amended, extended, consolidated, or replaced by the same, and include any rules, regulations, orders, and other subordinate legislation made under the relevant statute or statutory provision.

\(a\) The General Partner may admit additional Limited Partners to the Partnership prior to the Closing Date, in the General Partner\'s sole discretion, subject to maintaining the Aggregate Capital Commitments at Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000). Any such additional Limited Partner shall execute a joinder to this Agreement substantially in the form of Exhibit A and shall be bound by all terms and conditions hereof.

\(b\) After the Closing Date, additional Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership only in connection with a Transfer of a Partnership Interest that is permitted under and consummated in accordance with Article VIII. Any transferee admitted as a Limited Partner shall execute a joinder to this Agreement and shall succeed to all rights and obligations of the transferring Limited Partner with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest.
\(c\) The General Partner shall promptly update Schedule A to reflect the admission of any additional Limited Partner and shall provide a copy of the updated Schedule A to all Partners.

Each Limited Partner, severally and not jointly, hereby represents and warrants to the Partnership and the General Partner, as of the date of such Limited Partner\'s execution of this Agreement (or its joinder hereto) and as of the Closing Date, as follows:

\(b\) **Authority.** Such Limited Partner has full power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under this Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby. The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by such Limited Partner has been duly authorized by all necessary corporate, partnership, limited liability company, or other organizational action on the part of such Limited Partner.

\(c\) **No Violations.** The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by such Limited Partner does not and will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Limited Partner\'s organizational documents, (ii) violate any law, rule, regulation, order, judgment, or decree applicable to such Limited Partner, or (iii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement or instrument to which such Limited Partner is a party or by which its properties are bound.

**(a) Capital Call Notice.** The General Partner shall issue a written notice to each Limited Partner (each, a \"**Capital Call Notice**\") specifying (i) the aggregate amount of the Capital Contribution being called, (ii) each Limited Partner\'s proportionate share of the Capital Contribution (based on its Partnership Percentage), (iii) the purpose of the capital call, (iv) the payment date (which shall not be less than ten (10) Business Days following the date of delivery of such Capital Call Notice), and (v) wire transfer instructions for payment. Capital Call Notices shall be delivered in accordance with Section 14.1 (Notices). A form of Capital Call Notice is attached hereto as Exhibit B.

**(b) Initial Capital Call.** One hundred percent (100%) of each Limited Partner\'s Capital Commitment shall be called at the Closing. The Initial Capital Contribution of each Limited Partner is due and payable on or before January 30, 2026 (the Closing Date). Without limitation, the Initial Capital Contribution of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), due on or before January 30, 2026. All Initial Capital Contributions shall be funded in immediately available United States dollars by wire transfer to the account designated by the General Partner in the applicable Capital Call Notice. Time shall be of the essence with respect to the payment of Initial Capital Contributions.

**(a) Definition of Default.** A \"**Default**\" shall occur if any Limited Partner fails to fund all or any portion of a Capital Contribution within five (5) Business Days following the payment date specified in the applicable Capital Call Notice (after giving effect to the minimum ten (10) Business Day notice period set forth in Section 4.2(a)).
> \(iii\) **Loss of Governance Rights.** The Defaulting Limited Partner shall immediately forfeit any seat on the LPAC and all governance, consent, and voting rights under this Agreement.

> \(iv\) **Default Interest.** Interest shall accrue on the unpaid Capital Contribution amount at the lesser of (A) eighteen percent (18%) per annum, compounded monthly, or (B) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, from the date such Capital Contribution was due until paid in full.

\(b\) **Partnership Representative.** The General Partner shall serve as the \"tax matters partner\" of the Partnership within the meaning of Section 6231 of the Code (as in effect prior to amendment by the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2015) and as the \"partnership representative\" of the Partnership within the meaning of Section 6223 of the Code (as in effect following such amendment), for all taxable years of the Partnership. The General Partner shall have the authority and obligation to take all actions necessary or appropriate in such capacity, including the authority to make elections, extend statutes of limitation, bind the Partnership and the Partners in tax proceedings, and settle tax audits and controversies. The General Partner shall make reasonable efforts to minimize any adverse tax impact on the Limited Partners arising from its actions as Partnership Representative, and shall consult with the LPAC prior to making any material decisions in connection with any tax audit or proceeding.

**(b) Preferred Return.** Second, one hundred percent (100%) to the Limited Partners, pro rata in proportion to their respective Capital Contributions, until each Limited Partner has received cumulative Distributions under this clause (b) equal to a preferred return of eight percent (8%) per annum on unreturned Capital Contributions, compounded quarterly, calculated from the date of each Capital Contribution through the date of each Distribution (the \"**Preferred Return Amount**\"). For purposes of calculating unreturned Capital Contributions, a Limited Partner\'s Capital Contributions shall be reduced by Distributions received by such Limited Partner under clause (a) above. The compounding of the Preferred Return shall occur on the last day of each calendar quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31) (or, in the case of the first and last quarters, on the applicable portion thereof).

Distributions in kind (i.e., distributions of property other than cash) shall not be made except with the prior written approval of a majority of the LPAC. Any in-kind distributions approved by the LPAC shall be valued at fair market value as determined by the General Partner in good faith, subject to review and approval by the LPAC. For purposes of the Distribution waterfall in Section 6.2, in-kind distributions shall be treated as cash distributions in the amount of their fair market value.

\(b\) Execute, deliver, and perform all contracts, agreements, instruments, and documents on behalf of the Partnership, including the execution of closing documents in connection with the Acquisition;
**Section 7.3 --- Actions Requiring LPAC Approval**

Notwithstanding the broad authority granted to the General Partner under Sections 7.1 and 7.2, the following actions shall require the prior written approval of a majority of the members of the LPAC (i.e., at least two (2) of three (3) LPAC members):

\(b\) Any amendment to this Agreement that adversely affects the economic or governance rights of the Limited Partners, including any amendment to the Distribution waterfall, the Preferred Return, the Carried Interest Percentage, or the LPAC provisions;
**(c) Broken Deal Expenses.** Not applicable. The Investment has closed as of the date hereof, and no broken deal expenses have been incurred.

\(e\) Each Limited Partner hereby agrees to take all actions and execute all documents reasonably requested by the General Partner to consummate a Drag-Along Sale, including execution of purchase agreements, closing certificates, and related instruments.

A permitted transferee of a Partnership Interest shall be admitted to the Partnership as a substitute Limited Partner only upon satisfaction of all conditions set forth in Section 8.2 and execution and delivery of such documentation as the General Partner may reasonably require, including a joinder agreement substantially in the form of Exhibit A. Upon admission as a substitute Limited Partner, the transferee shall succeed to all of the rights and obligations of the transferring Limited Partner with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest, and the transferring Limited Partner shall be released from all obligations hereunder with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest (other than obligations that accrued prior to the effective date of such Transfer). The General Partner shall promptly update Schedule A to reflect any such substitution.
**[ARTICLE IX --- LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE (LPAC)]{.underline}**

The Partnership shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\") consisting of three (3) members. The members of the LPAC shall be appointed by the General Partner from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives; provided, however, that Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be entitled to appoint one (1) member of the LPAC for so long as Pellegrino Capital Group LLC holds a Partnership Interest in the Partnership. LPAC members shall serve in a non-fiduciary, advisory capacity, except where specific approval or consent rights are expressly conferred upon the LPAC by this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, LPAC members shall not owe any fiduciary duties to the Partnership or to any other Partner by virtue of their service on the LPAC.
**Section 9.2 --- LPAC Functions**
The LPAC shall have the following functions and responsibilities:
\(b\) Review and approve (or disapprove) all other matters requiring LPAC consent as set forth in Section 7.3;
**Section 9.3 --- LPAC Meetings**

\(a\) The LPAC shall meet at least once per calendar year, or more frequently as the General Partner or any two (2) LPAC members may request. Meetings may be held in person at the offices of the General Partner, by video conference, or by telephonic conference, as determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC members.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice of each meeting to all LPAC members, together with a written agenda and copies of any relevant materials to be discussed at such meeting.

\(c\) A quorum for any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members). Actions of the LPAC shall be taken by the affirmative vote or written consent of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members).
\(d\) Actions may be taken by the LPAC without a meeting by written consent signed by a majority of the LPAC members, which consent shall be effective as of the date of the last signature.
\(e\) The General Partner shall prepare and distribute to all LPAC members written minutes of each meeting within fifteen (15) Business Days following such meeting.
**Section 9.4 --- Indemnification of LPAC Members**

Each member of the LPAC shall be indemnified by the Partnership on the same basis as Covered Persons under Section 7.9 with respect to any Losses incurred by such member arising out of or in connection with such member\'s service on the LPAC. LPAC members acting in good faith in the performance of their duties as LPAC members shall have no personal liability to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner for any actions taken or omitted to be taken in their advisory capacity as LPAC members.
\(a\) The General Partner may remove any LPAC member for Cause upon written notice to such LPAC member and the Limited Partner that appointed or designated such member.

\(b\) Any Limited Partner that appointed or designated an LPAC member may, at any time, designate a replacement for such LPAC member by written notice to the General Partner, and such replacement shall become effective upon receipt of such notice by the General Partner.

\(c\) In the event of a vacancy on the LPAC (whether by removal, resignation, or otherwise), the General Partner shall appoint a replacement LPAC member from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives within thirty (30) days of such vacancy; provided, however, that any vacancy in the LPAC seat held by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be filled by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC.

> \(iv\) During the ninety (90)-day period referred to in clause (iii) above, the General Partner shall consult with the LPAC regarding a management transition plan, including the identification and evaluation of potential replacement key persons and the impact of the Key Person Event on the Investment.

The General Partner may extend the Term for up to two (2) additional one (1)-year periods (each, a \"**GP Extension**\"), subject to the prior written approval of a majority of the members of the LPAC pursuant to Section 7.3(e). If both GP Extensions are exercised, the maximum Term of the Partnership shall expire on January 30, 2038. The Term of the Partnership is intended to be co-terminous with the term of Fund IV as it relates to the Investment.

Our principal areas of focus are: (i) enhanced tag-along protections, (ii) key person trigger mechanics, (iii) LPAC seat allocation for Pellegrino, (iv) preferred return compounding methodology, (v) GP clawback mechanics at liquidation, (vi) narrowing of excuse/exclusion provisions to protect Pellegrino from involuntary exclusion, and (vii) strengthened default cure periods. We would welcome a call to discuss the markup at the parties\' earliest convenience. Please note that certain Pellegrino-specific protections will be addressed in a separate side letter to be circulated shortly (anticipated December 10, 2025).

This AMENDED AND RESTATED LIMITED PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT (this \"**Agreement**\" or \"**LPA**\") of Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P., a Delaware limited partnership (the \"**Partnership**\" or \"**Co-Invest LP**\"), EIN 93-4817265, is entered into and made effective as of January 30, 2026 (the \"**Effective Date**\"), by and among Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, EIN 93-4817302, as general partner of the Partnership (the \"**General Partner**\" or \"**GP**\"), and the persons listed on Schedule A hereto, each of which is admitted to the Partnership as a limited partner (each, a \"**Limited Partner**\" and collectively, the \"**Limited Partners**\").

\"**Acquisition**\" means the acquisition by AcquisitionCo of 100% of the issued and outstanding equity interests of Clarion Hospitality Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation, pursuant to the terms and conditions of that certain Stock Purchase Agreement, dated as of December 12, 2025, by and among AcquisitionCo, the sellers party thereto, and the other parties named therein.
\"**Closing Date**\" means January 30, 2026.

\"**Distributable Cash**\" means, as of any date of determination, the cash held by the Partnership that the GP determines, in its reasonable discretion, is available for distribution to the Partners after taking into account (a) any reserves that the GP determines in good faith are necessary or appropriate for the payment of Partnership debts, expenses, and obligations (whether actual, contingent, or anticipated), and (b) the working capital needs of the Partnership.

\"**Fiscal Year**\" means the calendar year (January 1 through December 31) or, in the case of the first Fiscal Year, the period commencing on the date of formation of the Partnership and ending on December 31 of the year of formation, and in the case of the last Fiscal Year, the period commencing on January 1 of the year of dissolution and ending on the date of the final liquidating distribution.

\"**LPAC**\" or \"**Limited Partner Advisory Committee**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 9.1. For so long as Pellegrino Capital Group LLC holds a Partnership Interest, Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be entitled to designate one (1) member of the LPAC.

\(f\) References to any statute or statutory provision include any statute or statutory provision that amends, extends, consolidates, or replaces the same, or that has been amended, extended, consolidated, or replaced by the same, and include any rules, regulations, orders, and other subordinate legislation made under the relevant statute or statutory provision.

\(a\) The General Partner may admit additional Limited Partners to the Partnership prior to the Closing Date, in the General Partner\'s sole discretion, subject to maintaining the Aggregate Capital Commitments at Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000). Any such additional Limited Partner shall execute a joinder to this Agreement substantially in the form of Exhibit A and shall be bound by all terms and conditions hereof. The GP shall provide notice to existing Limited Partners of any additional admission that would increase the Aggregate Capital Commitments above Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000) or would reduce any existing Limited Partner\'s Partnership Percentage.

\(b\) After the Closing Date, additional Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership only in connection with a Transfer of a Partnership Interest that is permitted under and consummated in accordance with Article VIII. Any transferee admitted as a Limited Partner shall execute a joinder to this Agreement and shall succeed to all rights and obligations of the transferring Limited Partner with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest.
\(c\) The General Partner shall promptly update Schedule A to reflect the admission of any additional Limited Partner and shall provide a copy of the updated Schedule A to all Partners.

Each Limited Partner, severally and not jointly, hereby represents and warrants to the Partnership and the General Partner, as of the date of such Limited Partner\'s execution of this Agreement (or its joinder hereto) and as of the Closing Date, as follows:

\(b\) **Authority.** Such Limited Partner has full power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under this Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby. The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by such Limited Partner has been duly authorized by all necessary corporate, partnership, limited liability company, or other organizational action on the part of such Limited Partner.

\(c\) **No Violations.** The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by such Limited Partner does not and will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Limited Partner\'s organizational documents, (ii) violate any law, rule, regulation, order, judgment, or decree applicable to such Limited Partner, or (iii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement or instrument to which such Limited Partner is a party or by which its properties are bound.

**(a) Capital Call Notice.** The General Partner shall issue a written notice to each Limited Partner (each, a \"**Capital Call Notice**\") specifying (i) the aggregate amount of the Capital Contribution being called, (ii) each Limited Partner\'s proportionate share of the Capital Contribution (based on its Partnership Percentage), (iii) the purpose of the capital call, (iv) the payment date (which shall not be less than ten (10) Business Days following the date of delivery of such Capital Call Notice), and (v) wire transfer instructions for payment. Each Capital Call Notice shall include reasonable detail regarding the purpose of the call and the application of the called amounts. Capital Call Notices shall be delivered in accordance with Section 14.1 (Notices). A form of Capital Call Notice is attached hereto as Exhibit B.

**(b) Initial Capital Call.** One hundred percent (100%) of each Limited Partner\'s Capital Commitment shall be called at the Closing. The Initial Capital Contribution of each Limited Partner is due and payable on or before January 30, 2026 (the Closing Date). Without limitation, the Initial Capital Contribution of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), due on or before January 30, 2026. All Initial Capital Contributions shall be funded in immediately available United States dollars by wire transfer to the account designated by the General Partner in the applicable Capital Call Notice. Time shall be of the essence with respect to the payment of Initial Capital Contributions.

**(a) Definition of Default.** A \"**Default**\" shall occur if any Limited Partner fails to fund all or any portion of a Capital Contribution within five (5) Business Days following the payment date specified in the applicable Capital Call Notice (after giving effect to the minimum ten (10) Business Day notice period set forth in Section 4.2(a)).
> \(iii\) **Loss of Governance Rights.** The Defaulting Limited Partner shall immediately forfeit any seat on the LPAC and all governance, consent, and voting rights under this Agreement.

> \(iv\) **Default Interest.** Interest shall accrue on the unpaid Capital Contribution amount at the lesser of (A) twelve percent (12%) per annum, compounded monthly, or (B) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, from the date such Capital Contribution was due until paid in full.

\(b\) **Partnership Representative.** The General Partner shall serve as the \"tax matters partner\" of the Partnership within the meaning of Section 6231 of the Code (as in effect prior to amendment by the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2015) and as the \"partnership representative\" of the Partnership within the meaning of Section 6223 of the Code (as in effect following such amendment), for all taxable years of the Partnership. The General Partner shall have the authority and obligation to take all actions necessary or appropriate in such capacity, including the authority to make elections, extend statutes of limitation, bind the Partnership and the Partners in tax proceedings, and settle tax audits and controversies. The General Partner shall make reasonable efforts to minimize any adverse tax impact on the Limited Partners arising from its actions as Partnership Representative, and shall consult with the LPAC prior to making any material decisions in connection with any tax audit or proceeding. The GP, in its capacity as Partnership Representative under Section 6223 of the Code, shall consult with the LPAC prior to making any election under Section 6226 of the Code (the \"push-out\" election) or settling any partnership-level tax audit. The GP shall use commercially reasonable efforts to make a \"push-out\" election under Section 6226 of the Code with respect to any imputed underpayment, so that any tax liability is allocated to the relevant Partners rather than borne at the Partnership level.

**(b) Preferred Return.** Second, one hundred percent (100%) to the Limited Partners, pro rata in proportion to their respective Capital Contributions, until each Limited Partner has received cumulative Distributions under this clause (b) equal to a preferred return of eight percent (8%) per annum on unreturned Capital Contributions, compounded quarterly, calculated from the date of each Capital Contribution through the date of each Distribution (the \"**Preferred Return Amount**\"). For purposes of calculating unreturned Capital Contributions, a Limited Partner\'s Capital Contributions shall be reduced by Distributions received by such Limited Partner under clause (a) above. The compounding of the Preferred Return shall occur on the last day of each calendar quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31) (or, in the case of the first and last quarters, on the applicable portion thereof).

\(b\) The GP shall establish an escrow account with a third-party escrow agent reasonably acceptable to the LPAC, into which the GP shall deposit no less than twenty-five percent (25%) of each Carried Interest distribution received, to be held as security for the GP\'s Clawback obligation under this Section 6.5. Amounts held in escrow shall be released to the GP upon the final determination that no Clawback Amount is owed, or applied toward payment of any Clawback Amount, as applicable.

Distributions in kind (i.e., distributions of property other than cash) shall not be made except with the prior written approval of a majority of the LPAC. Any in-kind distributions approved by the LPAC shall be valued at fair market value as determined by an independent third-party appraiser selected by the General Partner and reasonably acceptable to the LPAC. For purposes of the Distribution waterfall in Section 6.2, in-kind distributions shall be treated as cash distributions in the amount of their fair market value.

\(b\) Execute, deliver, and perform all contracts, agreements, instruments, and documents on behalf of the Partnership, including the execution of closing documents in connection with the Acquisition;
**Section 7.3 --- Actions Requiring LPAC Approval**

Notwithstanding the broad authority granted to the General Partner under Sections 7.1 and 7.2, the following actions shall require the prior written approval of a majority of the members of the LPAC (i.e., at least two (2) of three (3) LPAC members):

\(b\) Any amendment to this Agreement that adversely affects the economic or governance rights of the Limited Partners, including any amendment to the Distribution waterfall, the Preferred Return, the Carried Interest Percentage, or the LPAC provisions;

**(b) Operating Expenses.** The Partnership shall bear its pro rata share (based on relative equity contributions to AcquisitionCo) of any operating expenses of AcquisitionCo or the Investment that are allocable to the Partnership, as determined by the General Partner in its reasonable discretion. In addition, the Partnership shall bear its own ongoing administrative expenses, including accounting, audit, legal, tax preparation, tax filing, custodial, and other administrative fees and expenses incurred in the ordinary course of the Partnership\'s business. The GP shall provide the LPAC with an annual budget of anticipated operating expenses of the Partnership no later than thirty (30) days prior to the commencement of each Fiscal Year.
**(c) Broken Deal Expenses.** Not applicable. The Investment has closed as of the date hereof, and no broken deal expenses have been incurred.

\(e\) Each Limited Partner hereby agrees to take all actions and execute all documents reasonably requested by the General Partner to consummate a Drag-Along Sale, including execution of purchase agreements, closing certificates, and related instruments.

A permitted transferee of a Partnership Interest shall be admitted to the Partnership as a substitute Limited Partner only upon satisfaction of all conditions set forth in Section 8.2 and execution and delivery of such documentation as the General Partner may reasonably require, including a joinder agreement substantially in the form of Exhibit A. Upon admission as a substitute Limited Partner, the transferee shall succeed to all of the rights and obligations of the transferring Limited Partner with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest, and the transferring Limited Partner shall be released from all obligations hereunder with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest (other than obligations that accrued prior to the effective date of such Transfer). The General Partner shall promptly update Schedule A to reflect any such substitution.
**[ARTICLE IX --- LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE (LPAC)]{.underline}**

The Partnership shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\") consisting of three (3) members. The members of the LPAC shall be appointed by the General Partner from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives; provided, however, that Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be entitled to appoint one (1) member of the LPAC for so long as Pellegrino Capital Group LLC holds a Partnership Interest in the Partnership. LPAC members shall serve in a non-fiduciary, advisory capacity, except where specific approval or consent rights are expressly conferred upon the LPAC by this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, LPAC members shall not owe any fiduciary duties to the Partnership or to any other Partner by virtue of their service on the LPAC.
**Section 9.2 --- LPAC Functions**
The LPAC shall have the following functions and responsibilities:
\(b\) Review and approve (or disapprove) all other matters requiring LPAC consent as set forth in Section 7.3;
**Section 9.3 --- LPAC Meetings**

\(a\) The LPAC shall meet at least twice per calendar year, with at least one meeting to be held in person (which may be at the offices of the GP or such other location as the LPAC may agree), or more frequently as the General Partner or any two (2) LPAC members may request. Meetings may be held in person at the offices of the General Partner, by video conference, or by telephonic conference, as determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC members.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice of each meeting to all LPAC members, together with a written agenda and copies of any relevant materials to be discussed at such meeting.

\(c\) A quorum for any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members). Actions of the LPAC shall be taken by the affirmative vote or written consent of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members).
\(d\) Actions may be taken by the LPAC without a meeting by written consent signed by a majority of the LPAC members, which consent shall be effective as of the date of the last signature.
\(e\) The General Partner shall prepare and distribute to all LPAC members written minutes of each meeting within fifteen (15) Business Days following such meeting.
**Section 9.4 --- Indemnification of LPAC Members**

Each member of the LPAC shall be indemnified by the Partnership on the same basis as Covered Persons under Section 7.9 with respect to any Losses incurred by such member arising out of or in connection with such member\'s service on the LPAC. LPAC members acting in good faith in the performance of their duties as LPAC members shall have no personal liability to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner for any actions taken or omitted to be taken in their advisory capacity as LPAC members.
\(a\) The General Partner may remove any LPAC member for Cause upon written notice to such LPAC member and the Limited Partner that appointed or designated such member.

\(b\) Any Limited Partner that appointed or designated an LPAC member may, at any time, designate a replacement for such LPAC member by written notice to the General Partner, and such replacement shall become effective upon receipt of such notice by the General Partner.

\(c\) In the event of a vacancy on the LPAC (whether by removal, resignation, or otherwise), the General Partner shall appoint a replacement LPAC member from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives within thirty (30) days of such vacancy; provided, however, that any vacancy in the LPAC seat held by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be filled by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC.

> \(iv\) During the ninety (90)-day period referred to in clause (iii) above, the General Partner shall consult with the LPAC regarding a management transition plan, including the identification and evaluation of potential replacement key persons and the impact of the Key Person Event on the Investment.

The \"**Term**\" of the Partnership shall commence on the date of the filing of the Certificate of Limited Partnership with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware and shall continue until the tenth (10th) anniversary of the Closing Date (i.e., January 30, 2036), unless earlier dissolved pursuant to Section 11.2. The General Partner may extend the Term for up to two (2) additional one (1)-year periods (each, a \"**GP Extension**\"), subject to the prior written approval of a majority of the members of the LPAC pursuant to Section 7.3(e). Each GP Extension shall require at least one hundred twenty (120) days\' prior written notice to all Limited Partners before the expiration of the then-current Term. If both GP Extensions are exercised, the maximum Term of the Partnership shall expire on January 30, 2038. The Term of the Partnership is intended to be co-terminous with the term of Fund IV as it relates to the Investment.

**(c) Additional Reporting.** The General Partner shall provide such other information as may be reasonably requested by any Limited Partner to satisfy such Limited Partner\'s regulatory, tax, legal, or reporting requirements (including without limitation information required for ERISA compliance, FATCA reporting, Solvency II reporting, and state or municipal pension fund reporting obligations), subject to (i) the General Partner\'s reasonable ability to provide such information, (ii) the requesting Limited Partner\'s execution of any confidentiality or non-disclosure agreement that the General Partner deems reasonably appropriate, and (iii) reimbursement by the requesting Limited Partner of any incremental out-of-pocket costs incurred by the Partnership in connection with providing such information.

**(a) Schedule K-1.** The General Partner shall deliver, or cause to be delivered, to each Limited Partner an IRS Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) (or any successor form or equivalent thereof) on or before March 15 of each year for the immediately preceding Fiscal Year. If the General Partner is unable to deliver final Schedules K-1 by March 15, the General Partner shall deliver estimated Schedules K-1 by such date, followed by final Schedules K-1 as soon as practicable.

**(c) Partnership Representative.** The General Partner shall serve as the Partnership Representative under Section 6223 of the Code for all taxable years of the Partnership. The General Partner shall not settle, compromise, or take any position with respect to any tax audit, examination, or proceeding that would disproportionately adversely affect any Limited Partner without prior consultation with the LPAC. In the event the Partnership is subject to any tax audit adjustment, the General Partner shall, to the extent permitted by applicable law, elect to push out any imputed underpayment to the Partners under Section 6226 of the Code rather than paying the imputed underpayment at the Partnership level.

\(c\) Take all actions reasonably necessary or appropriate in connection with the dissolution, winding up, liquidation, and termination of the Partnership, including the execution and filing of a Certificate of Cancellation; and

All notices, requests, consents, demands, waivers, and other communications required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given and effective (a) when delivered personally, (b) on the next Business Day following deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier service for delivery on the next Business Day, or (c) when sent by electronic mail (with confirmation of receipt by the intended recipient, including by reply email, read receipt, or similar confirmation), in each case addressed as follows:

This Agreement may be amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified only by a written instrument signed by the General Partner and by Limited Partners holding a majority-in-interest of the Aggregate Capital Commitments. No amendment that adversely and disproportionately affects the economic or governance rights of a particular Limited Partner (including such Limited Partner\'s Preferred Return, Carried Interest allocation, Capital Commitment, Partnership Percentage, or LPAC seat) shall be effective without the prior written consent of such affected Limited Partner. Notwithstanding the foregoing, any amendment that would (i) modify the distribution waterfall in Section 6.2, (ii) alter the Preferred Return or Carried Interest Percentage, (iii) extend the Term beyond the GP Extensions contemplated herein, or (iv) modify the GP Clawback in Section 6.5, shall require the prior written consent of each Limited Partner (not merely a majority-in-interest). Notwithstanding the foregoing, the General Partner may amend Schedule A without the consent of the Limited Partners to reflect (i) the admission of additional or substitute Limited Partners, (ii) the withdrawal or removal of Limited Partners, (iii) permitted Transfers of Partnership Interests, and (iv) adjustments to Capital Commitments and Partnership Percentages resulting from any of the foregoing.

No waiver of any term, condition, or provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement of such waiver is sought. No failure or delay by any party in exercising any right, power, or privilege under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any such right, power, or privilege preclude any other or further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right, power, or privilege. The rights and remedies provided herein are cumulative and not exclusive of any rights or remedies provided by law or in equity.

If any term, provision, covenant, or restriction of this Agreement is held by a court of competent jurisdiction or by an arbitrator to be invalid, illegal, void, or unenforceable, the remainder of the terms, provisions, covenants, and restrictions of this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect and shall in no way be affected, impaired, or invalidated. In the event of any such holding, the parties shall negotiate in good faith to substitute for such invalid, illegal, void, or unenforceable provision a valid, legal, and enforceable provision that most closely approximates the economic effect and intent of the invalid, illegal, void, or unenforceable provision.

This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this Agreement by electronic transmission (including by .pdf, DocuSign, or other electronic signature technology) shall constitute valid and effective execution and delivery for all purposes, and electronic signatures shall be deemed original signatures for all purposes under this Agreement.

Except as expressly provided herein with respect to the indemnification of Covered Persons (including LPAC members) under Sections 7.9 and 9.4, nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any Person other than the parties hereto and their permitted successors and assigns any legal or equitable right, benefit, claim, or remedy of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Agreement.

The General Partner may enter into Side Letters with one or more Limited Partners. The terms of any Side Letter shall supplement and, where expressly stated therein, modify or supersede the terms of this Agreement solely as to the Limited Partner that is a party to such Side Letter. Side Letters shall not be deemed to amend this Agreement as to any other Limited Partner unless such other Limited Partner is expressly entitled to the benefits thereof pursuant to a most-favored-nation provision contained in such other Limited Partner\'s Side Letter or this Agreement. The General Partner shall notify the LPAC of the existence of any Side Letters (without being required to disclose the specific terms thereof, unless such disclosure is required by the terms of a Side Letter or a most-favored-nation provision). The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that the terms of any Side Letter do not materially and adversely affect the rights of any Limited Partner that is not a party to such Side Letter. The GP shall, upon request by any Limited Partner, provide a summary of the material economic and governance terms contained in all Side Letters (on a redacted and anonymized basis) to enable such Limited Partner to exercise any most-favored-nation rights.

21: **[I. Executive Summary]{.underline}**
22: 
23: The purpose of this memorandum is to provide Briarwood Family Office LLC (\"BFO\") with a comprehensive review and legal analysis of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. (the \"Fund\" or \"Fund IV\"), dated December 20, 2023 (the \"LPA\"), in connection with BFO\'s evaluation of a proposed limited partnership commitment of Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000) to Fund IV. This memorandum has been prepared at the request of BFO\'s General Counsel, Sandra M. Whitfield, and is intended to assist BFO\'s investment committee in its evaluation and approval process.
24: 
25: Fund IV is organized as a Delaware limited partnership, filed with the Delaware Secretary of State under Certificate Number LP-2023-08841. The Fund is managed by its general partner, Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC (the \"GP\" or the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company whose sole member is Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"MPCA\"). The LPA is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, and the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (\"DRULPA\") applies to the extent not expressly modified by the LPA.
26: 
27: Fund IV\'s stated investment strategy is to pursue value-add and opportunistic investments in North American commercial real estate, real estate operating companies, and asset management platforms. The Fund has established a target fund size of \$1,500,000,000 and a hard cap of \$1,750,000,000. The Fund anticipates holding its first close on or about April 30, 2024, with a final close deadline of October 31, 2024. BFO\'s proposed commitment of \$75,000,000 would represent approximately 5.0% of the target fund size and approximately 4.29% of the hard cap, positioning BFO as a meaningful but not anchor-level investor in the Fund.
28: 
29: MPCA was founded in 2011 by Conrad J. Ellsworth and Priya Narayan, who continue to serve as the firm\'s Co-Founders and Managing Partners. Mr. Ellsworth serves as Chief Executive Officer and Ms. Narayan serves as Chief Investment Officer. Since its founding, MPCA has raised three prior funds --- Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund I, L.P., Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund II, L.P., and Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund III, L.P. (collectively, \"Funds I--III\") --- aggregating approximately \$3.2 billion in committed capital. Fund IV represents a meaningful step-up in target fund size relative to the prior fund vintages, and the GP\'s ability to deploy capital effectively at this increased scale is a consideration that BFO should evaluate as part of its broader investment diligence, which is addressed separately in our concurrent PPM Summary & Risk Assessment Memorandum.
30: 
31: **Overall Assessment.** Following a thorough review of the LPA, it is our view that the agreement is broadly consistent with prevailing market terms for a mid-market real estate private equity fund of this size and strategy. The economic terms --- including a 1.75% management fee on committed capital during the Investment Period, a 20% carried interest above an 8% preferred return, and a European (whole-fund) waterfall --- are within the range we observe across comparable funds in the current market environment. However, several provisions in the LPA warrant attention and, in our recommendation, should be the subject of negotiation through a side letter to the LPA. These provisions relate primarily to (i) the absence of excuse and exclusion rights in the base LPA, (ii) the management fee structure, (iii) co-investment rights, (iv) most favored nation protections, (v) enhanced reporting obligations, (vi) key person provisions, (vii) transfer rights, and (viii) confidentiality carve-outs. Our detailed recommendations on each of these points are summarized at Section XV of this memorandum and discussed in the relevant sections throughout.
32: 
33: This memorandum should be read in conjunction with the separate PPM Summary & Risk Assessment Memorandum prepared by Calderwood & Harkness and delivered concurrently to BFO, which addresses the investment risk factors, market positioning, and track record analysis for Fund IV based on the Private Placement Memorandum dated December 15, 2023.
34: 
35: **[II. Defined Terms and Interpretive Provisions]{.underline}**
36: 
37: Throughout this memorandum, we use capitalized terms as defined in the LPA unless otherwise noted. For the convenience of BFO\'s review, we highlight below the key defined terms in the LPA that are most relevant to BFO\'s evaluation of the proposed commitment and that recur throughout this memorandum:
38: 
39: > • **\"Capital Commitment\"** means the total amount that a Limited Partner has committed to contribute to the Fund as set forth in such Limited Partner\'s Subscription Agreement. BFO\'s proposed Capital Commitment is \$75,000,000.
40: >
41: > • **\"Capital Account\"** means, with respect to each Partner, such Partner\'s capital account as maintained by the Fund in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv) and the applicable provisions of the LPA.
42: >
43: > • **\"Carried Interest\"** means the performance-based allocation payable to the General Partner equal to 20% of the Fund\'s net profits in excess of the Preferred Return, as more fully described in Section V.C below.
44: >
45: > • **\"Commitment Period\"** (synonymous with \"Investment Period\") means the period beginning on the date of the Final Close and ending on the fourth anniversary thereof, during which the General Partner may make new Investments on behalf of the Fund. The Commitment Period is subject to early termination upon a Key Person Event as described in Section VIII.
46: >
47: > • **\"Fund Expenses\"** means the operating expenses of the Fund as described in Section 5.4 of the LPA, including audit fees, legal fees, administration fees, valuation expenses, insurance premiums, taxes, regulatory filing costs, broken-deal costs, and other customary expenses of the Fund. Fund Expenses are discussed in detail in Section V.D of this memorandum.
48: >
49: > • **\"Investment\"** means any investment made by the Fund in a Portfolio Company or other asset in furtherance of the Fund\'s investment strategy, including equity investments, debt investments, mezzanine investments, and joint venture interests.
50: >
51: > • **\"Net Asset Value\" or \"NAV\"** means the fair market value of the Fund\'s assets less the Fund\'s liabilities, as determined by the General Partner in accordance with the valuation provisions of the LPA (Section 9.3 of the LPA).
52: >
53: > • **\"Organizational Expenses\"** means the costs and expenses incurred in connection with the formation and organization of the Fund, including legal fees, regulatory filing fees, and printing costs, which are borne by the Fund subject to the cap described in Section V.D of this memorandum.
54: >
55: > • **\"Preferred Return\"** means the annual compounded preferred return of 8% per annum on contributed capital, as described in the waterfall provisions of the LPA.
56: >
57: > • **\"Subscription Agreement\"** means the subscription agreement entered into between the Fund and each Limited Partner in connection with such Limited Partner\'s admission to the Fund.
58: 
59: The LPA specifies that it is governed by, and to be construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware without regard to conflicts of law principles. The Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (\"DRULPA\"), 6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 et seq., governs the Fund to the extent not expressly modified by the LPA. The LPA contains extensive interpretation clauses stating that, where the provisions of the LPA expressly address a subject also addressed by DRULPA, the LPA provisions are intended to supersede the default DRULPA provisions. This is standard practice in Delaware limited partnership agreements and permits the parties to contract around certain default provisions of DRULPA (as DRULPA expressly permits), including provisions governing distributions, voting, and dissolution.
60: 
61: The LPA makes reference to the Private Placement Memorandum dated December 15, 2023, which sets forth the Fund\'s offering terms, risk factors, and investment strategy in greater detail. Additionally, we note that the GP filed a Form D with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on January 2, 2024, reflecting the Fund\'s reliance on the private placement exemption under Regulation D of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. The PPM and Form D are addressed in our separate PPM Summary & Risk Assessment Memorandum.
62: 
63: **[III. Formation, Term, and Fund Structure]{.underline}**
64: 
65: **A. Formation and Structure**
66: 
67: Fund IV was formed as a Delaware limited partnership pursuant to a Certificate of Limited Partnership filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware under Certificate Number LP-2023-08841. The Fund\'s organizational structure is consistent with the standard structure employed by institutional real estate private equity funds and provides for a single general partner entity and multiple limited partners admitted through a private placement process.
68: 
69: The General Partner of the Fund is Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC, a Delaware limited liability company formed for the sole purpose of serving as the general partner of Fund IV. The sole member of the GP is Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"MPCA\"), the MPCA management company entity through which Messrs. Ellsworth and Narayan and the broader MPCA investment team operate. This single-layer GP structure --- in which the GP is a direct subsidiary of the management company --- is standard for funds of this type and does not raise any structural concerns from BFO\'s perspective. We note, however, that because the GP is a limited liability company with a single member, BFO should be aware that any change in control of MPCA (whether through admission of new members, transfer of membership interests, or otherwise) would effectively constitute a change of control of the GP. The LPA does not contain an express change-of-control provision with respect to MPCA, though the Key Person provisions (discussed in Section VIII below) provide some protection against departure of the principal investment professionals.
70: 
71: The Fund\'s registered agent in the State of Delaware is Beacon Statutory Services LLC, located at 1013 Centre Road, Wilmington, Delaware 19805. The General Partner\'s registered agent is also Beacon Statutory Services LLC at the same address. This is a standard commercial registered agent arrangement.
72: 
73: The GP maintains its principal office at 200 Clarendon Street, 42nd Floor, Boston, Massachusetts 02116, which is the primary business address of MPCA and the location from which Fund IV\'s investment activities are expected to be conducted.
74: 
75: The LPA identifies the following key service providers to the Fund:
76: 
77: > • **Fund Administrator:** Granite Ledger Fund Services LLC, located at 100 Summer Street, Suite 2700, Boston, Massachusetts 02110. The client relationship manager for Fund IV at Granite Ledger is Catherine J. Halloran. The fund administrator will be responsible for maintaining the Fund\'s books and records, processing capital calls and distributions, preparing quarterly financial statements, and coordinating with the Fund\'s auditor on annual audited financial statements. Granite Ledger is a well-established fund services provider with a significant presence in the real estate fund administration space.
78: >
79: > • **Fund Auditor:** Brockton Marsh & Associates LLP, located at 500 Boylston Street, 30th Floor, Boston, Massachusetts 02116. The engagement partner for Fund IV at Brockton Marsh is Neil A. Strickland. Brockton Marsh will be responsible for conducting the annual audit of the Fund\'s financial statements. While Brockton Marsh is a reputable regional audit firm, it is not among the Big Four accounting firms. BFO should assess whether the audit quality and market reputation of Brockton Marsh are consistent with BFO\'s expectations for a fund of this size, though we do not consider this to be a material concern from a legal perspective.

For the convenience of BFO\'s review, we highlight below the key defined terms in the LPA that are most relevant to BFO\'s evaluation of the proposed commitment and that recur throughout this memorandum:

> • **\"Capital Commitment\"** means the total amount that a Limited Partner has committed to contribute to the Fund as set forth in such Limited Partner\'s Subscription Agreement. BFO\'s proposed Capital Commitment is \$75,000,000.

> • **\"Capital Account\"** means, with respect to each Partner, such Partner\'s capital account as maintained by the Fund in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv) and the applicable provisions of the LPA.

> • **\"Carried Interest\"** means the performance-based allocation payable to the General Partner equal to 20% of the Fund\'s net profits in excess of the Preferred Return, as more fully described in Section V.C below.

> • **\"Commitment Period\"** (synonymous with \"Investment Period\") means the period beginning on the date of the Final Close and ending on the fourth anniversary thereof, during which the General Partner may make new Investments on behalf of the Fund. The Commitment Period is subject to early termination upon a Key Person Event as described in Section VIII.

> • **\"Fund Expenses\"** means the operating expenses of the Fund as described in Section 5.4 of the LPA, including audit fees, legal fees, administration fees, valuation expenses, insurance premiums, taxes, regulatory filing costs, broken-deal costs, and other customary expenses of the Fund. Fund Expenses are discussed in detail in Section V.D of this memorandum.

> • **\"Investment\"** means any investment made by the Fund in a Portfolio Company or other asset in furtherance of the Fund\'s investment strategy, including equity investments, debt investments, mezzanine investments, and joint venture interests.

> • **\"Net Asset Value\" or \"NAV\"** means the fair market value of the Fund\'s assets less the Fund\'s liabilities, as determined by the General Partner in accordance with the valuation provisions of the LPA (Section 9.3 of the LPA).

> • **\"Organizational Expenses\"** means the costs and expenses incurred in connection with the formation and organization of the Fund, including legal fees, regulatory filing fees, and printing costs, which are borne by the Fund subject to the cap described in Section V.D of this memorandum.
> • **\"Preferred Return\"** means the annual compounded preferred return of 8% per annum on contributed capital, as described in the waterfall provisions of the LPA.
> • **\"Subscription Agreement\"** means the subscription agreement entered into between the Fund and each Limited Partner in connection with such Limited Partner\'s admission to the Fund.

The LPA specifies that it is governed by, and to be construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware without regard to conflicts of law principles. The Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (\"DRULPA\"), 6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 et seq., governs the Fund to the extent not expressly modified by the LPA. The LPA contains extensive interpretation clauses stating that, where the provisions of the LPA expressly address a subject also addressed by DRULPA, the LPA provisions are intended to supersede the default DRULPA provisions. This is standard practice in Delaware limited partnership agreements and permits the parties to contract around certain default provisions of DRULPA (as DRULPA expressly permits), including provisions governing distributions, voting, and dissolution.

The LPA makes reference to the Private Placement Memorandum dated December 15, 2023, which sets forth the Fund\'s offering terms, risk factors, and investment strategy in greater detail. Additionally, we note that the GP filed a Form D with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on January 2, 2024, reflecting the Fund\'s reliance on the private placement exemption under Regulation D of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. The PPM and Form D are addressed in our separate PPM Summary & Risk Assessment Memorandum.
**[III. Formation, Term, and Fund Structure]{.underline}**
**A. Formation and Structure**

Fund IV was formed as a Delaware limited partnership pursuant to a Certificate of Limited Partnership filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware under Certificate Number LP-2023-08841. The Fund\'s organizational structure is consistent with the standard structure employed by institutional real estate private equity funds and provides for a single general partner entity and multiple limited partners admitted through a private placement process.

The General Partner of the Fund is Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC, a Delaware limited liability company formed for the sole purpose of serving as the general partner of Fund IV. The sole member of the GP is Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"MPCA\"), the MPCA management company entity through which Messrs. Ellsworth and Narayan and the broader MPCA investment team operate. This single-layer GP structure --- in which the GP is a direct subsidiary of the management company --- is standard for funds of this type and does not raise any structural concerns from BFO\'s perspective. We note, however, that because the GP is a limited liability company with a single member, BFO should be aware that any change in control of MPCA (whether through admission of new members, transfer of membership interests, or otherwise) would effectively constitute a change of control of the GP. The LPA does not contain an express change-of-control provision with respect to MPCA, though the Key Person provisions (discussed in Section VIII below) provide some protection against departure of the principal investment professionals.

The Fund\'s registered agent in the State of Delaware is Beacon Statutory Services LLC, located at 1013 Centre Road, Wilmington, Delaware 19805. The General Partner\'s registered agent is also Beacon Statutory Services LLC at the same address. This is a standard commercial registered agent arrangement.

The GP maintains its principal office at 200 Clarendon Street, 42nd Floor, Boston, Massachusetts 02116, which is the primary business address of MPCA and the location from which Fund IV\'s investment activities are expected to be conducted.
The LPA identifies the following key service providers to the Fund:

> • **Fund Administrator:** Granite Ledger Fund Services LLC, located at 100 Summer Street, Suite 2700, Boston, Massachusetts 02110. The client relationship manager for Fund IV at Granite Ledger is Catherine J. Halloran. The fund administrator will be responsible for maintaining the Fund\'s books and records, processing capital calls and distributions, preparing quarterly financial statements, and coordinating with the Fund\'s auditor on annual audited financial statements. Granite Ledger is a well-established fund services provider with a significant presence in the real estate fund administration space.

> • **Fund Auditor:** Brockton Marsh & Associates LLP, located at 500 Boylston Street, 30th Floor, Boston, Massachusetts 02116. The engagement partner for Fund IV at Brockton Marsh is Neil A. Strickland. Brockton Marsh will be responsible for conducting the annual audit of the Fund\'s financial statements. While Brockton Marsh is a reputable regional audit firm, it is not among the Big Four accounting firms. BFO should assess whether the audit quality and market reputation of Brockton Marsh are consistent with BFO\'s expectations for a fund of this size, though we do not consider this to be a material concern from a legal perspective.

Following the expiration of the investment period, the management fee will step down to 2.00% per annum calculated on invested capital, defined as the cost basis of portfolio investments net of write-offs, write-downs, and the return of realized proceeds. This step-down is designed to align the management fee with the actual capital at work in the portfolio and is a standard feature in institutional-quality funds. Management fee reductions granted via side letter---whether through a reduced rate, a cap, or an offset---will be analyzed in the context of their aggregate impact on CLSO Management\'s operating budget and the Principals\' economics.

**Recycling Allowance.** CLSO GP will be permitted to recycle up to 15% of aggregate commitments (\$112,500,000 at Target Size) during the investment period only. Recycled amounts represent realized proceeds from portfolio investments that may be re-called and re-invested, effectively increasing the Fund\'s deployable capital without requiring additional LP commitments. The recycling allowance is subject to the limitation that it may only be exercised during the investment period, and recycled capital counts toward the management fee base during the period in which it is deployed.

**Fund Term.** The Fund\'s term will be 10 years from the final close, with two optional one-year extensions. The first extension may be effected at the sole discretion of CLSO GP. The second extension requires the affirmative consent of the LP Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\"). Based on a target final close of May 15, 2027, the initial term would expire on May 15, 2037, with possible extensions to May 15, 2038 (first extension) and May 15, 2039 (second extension, subject to LPAC consent).

**LP Advisory Committee.** The LPAC will consist of a minimum of three and a maximum of seven members, appointed by CLSO GP. If aggregate non-U.S. commitments reach or exceed \$50,000,000, at least one LPAC member must be a representative of a non-U.S. limited partner. The LPAC\'s functions include consent to conflicts of interest, review of valuation methodology, consent to the second one-year fund extension, and such other matters as may be specified in the LPA.

Each of these investor categories brings different negotiation dynamics and side letter expectations, and the tiered framework recommended in this memorandum is designed to accommodate this diversity while maintaining a manageable level of administrative complexity.

The Placement Agent Agreement between CLSO GP and sagebrush has a target execution date of July 15, 2026, and will set forth the terms of the engagement, including: (a) the 1.50% placement fee on all third-party commitments sourced by sagebrush; (b) the 100% offset of the placement fee against the management fee; (c) a \$150,000 non-refundable retainer payable upon execution; (d) a 24-month tail period during which sagebrush will be entitled to the placement fee on commitments from investors introduced during the engagement term; and (e) sagebrush\'s exclusivity as the Fund\'s global placement agent.

This Section III describes the categories of side letter concessions that we recommend making available on a standardized basis to qualifying investors, subject to the tiered framework discussed in Section VII. These provisions represent the core menu of terms that CLSO GP should be prepared to offer during negotiations, and they are designed to address the most common institutional investor requirements while preserving the Fund\'s economic structure and operational flexibility.

**Mechanics.** Upon the final close of the Fund (target: May 15, 2027), CLSO GP will prepare---with the assistance of Calderwood & Harkness LLP---a redacted compendium of all side letter terms granted to all LPs. The compendium will be redacted to remove investor-identifying information (including the name, commitment size, and contact details of each LP) while preserving the substance of each concession in sufficient detail to permit an informed election. Each MFN-eligible LP will receive a copy of the redacted compendium, together with a notice setting forth the election procedures and the deadline for elections. Each MFN-eligible LP will have 30 calendar days from the date of distribution to elect, in writing, to receive any or all of the disclosed concessions. Elected terms will be incorporated into the electing LP\'s side letter by means of a written amendment executed by the LP and CLSO GP.

**Carve-Outs from MFN.** Certain categories of side letter terms should be excluded from the MFN election process, as they are by their nature investor-specific or relate to the particular legal, regulatory, or tax status of the benefited LP. The recommended carve-out categories are discussed in detail in Section V.C below and summarized in Appendix B. By way of overview, the recommended carve-outs include: (a) ERISA-specific provisions (e.g., the Northgate VCOC carve-out); (b) insurance regulatory provisions (e.g., the Pinnacle compliance suite); (c) FOIA and public records protections (e.g., the Ironwood PERS provisions); (d) blocker entity access (investor-specific tax structuring); (e) LPAC seats (allocated based on commitment size and investor profile); (f) co-investment rights at no fee/no carry, to the extent offered only to investors above a specified commitment threshold (recommended: \$75,000,000); and (g) terms that are personal to the investor, such as notice addresses and contact information.

**Allocation Policy.** Co-investment allocations will be made on a pro rata basis relative to each LP\'s commitment to the Fund, subject to CLSO GP\'s discretion to consider factors including investor suitability for the particular investment, speed of execution and ability to commit capital within the required timeframe, the LP\'s historical participation in co-investment opportunities, and potential conflicts of interest. The allocation policy should be set forth in the LPA and referenced in each side letter that includes co-investment rights.
**I. Advisory Committee (LPAC) Representation**

**LPAC Composition.** As noted in Section II.B, the LPAC will consist of a minimum of three and a maximum of seven members, appointed by CLSO GP. At least one member must be a representative of a non-U.S. LP if aggregate non-U.S. commitments reach \$50,000,000.

**Side Letter Allocation of Seats.** LPAC seats are a governance concession that is typically offered to the largest LPs and to investors whose participation in the LPAC adds value to the Fund\'s governance (e.g., investors with deep sector expertise, investors who represent a particular constituency within the LP base, or investors whose regulatory status makes their input on compliance matters particularly relevant). LPAC seats should be allocated in the side letters of anchor investors. For CLSO Fund I, we recommend guaranteeing one LPAC seat to Ironwood PERS (as the largest anchor investor) in its side letter, and reserving the remaining seats for allocation during the fundraising process based on the composition of the LP base at each closing. Northgate and Pinnacle may request LPAC representation, and CLSO GP should retain flexibility to accommodate such requests if the committee composition allows.

**LPAC Functions.** The LPAC\'s primary functions, as set forth in the LPA, will include: (a) consent to conflicts of interest involving CLSO GP, the Principals, or their affiliates; (b) review of the Fund\'s valuation methodology, including fair value determinations for portfolio investments; (c) consent to the second one-year fund extension (from May 15, 2038 to May 15, 2039, assuming the first extension has been exercised); and (d) such other advisory functions as may be specified in the LPA. The LPAC will operate in an advisory capacity and will not have the power to bind the Fund or CLSO GP, except where specific consent rights are granted.

**MFN Side Letter.** Ironwood PERS will expect full MFN rights, with the broadest possible scope of election. As the largest LP, Ironwood PERS will expect to be the MFN \"benchmark\" investor, meaning that its side letter effectively sets the ceiling of concessions that other investors can elect into (subject to carve-outs for investor-specific regulatory provisions). This is a standard expectation for the largest LP in a fund and is consistent with market practice. We recommend granting full MFN rights to Ironwood PERS, while ensuring that the carve-out categories are clearly delineated to prevent unintended cascade of investor-specific provisions. Specifically, insurance regulatory provisions (applicable to Pinnacle), ERISA/VCOC provisions (applicable to Northgate), and blocker entity access provisions should be carved out of MFN as relating to the specific legal, regulatory, or tax status of the benefited LP.

**Advisory Committee Seat.** Ironwood PERS will expect a guaranteed seat on the LPAC for Helen Tsao or her designee. This is a standard request for the largest LP and is consistent with LPAC governance best practices. Ironwood PERS expects to participate actively in conflict-of-interest reviews, valuation methodology reviews, and extension votes. We recommend granting this concession without qualification, as LPAC participation by the largest LP is both customary and valuable for Fund governance.

From a concessions perspective, the terms sought by Ironwood PERS are well within market norms for anchor investors of this size in life-sciences funds. Co-investment at no fee/no carry is increasingly standard for commitments of \$75,000,000 or more in the life-sciences sector, where deal sizes and concentration limits naturally create co-investment opportunities. The LPAC seat, FOIA protections, and placement agent disclosures are standard governmental plan requirements that impose minimal economic cost on the Fund or other LPs. The annual in-person reporting requirement is a modest operational commitment that builds relationship equity with a key investor.

The MFN process is designed to balance two competing objectives. First, it provides assurance to LPs that they will not be disadvantaged relative to their peers---an assurance that is critical to the fundraising process, as sophisticated investors are reluctant to commit capital without confidence that they will be treated equitably. Second, it preserves CLSO GP\'s ability to offer meaningfully differentiated terms to anchor investors and to investors with unique regulatory requirements, through the carve-out mechanism described below.

The effectiveness of the MFN framework depends on the careful calibration of three parameters: (a) the eligibility threshold, which determines which LPs have MFN rights; (b) the carve-out categories, which determine which side letter terms are excluded from MFN election; and (c) the timing and process, which determine when and how the MFN election occurs.

> 3\. **LPAC Seats.** Provisions guaranteeing or offering LPAC representation. *Justification:* LPAC seats are governance positions that are allocated based on commitment size, investor profile, and the overall composition of the committee. They are inherently limited in number (maximum seven members) and cannot be made available to all LPs through MFN election.

Elected terms will be effective either retroactively to the date of the LP\'s admission to the Fund or prospectively from the date of the election, as specified in each side letter. We recommend that economic terms (e.g., fee reductions) be effective retroactively, while operational terms (e.g., enhanced reporting) be effective prospectively.

An alternative approach would be to lower the Tier 1 threshold from \$75,000,000 to \$50,000,000, which would automatically include Northgate in Tier 1 and grant it the full suite of Tier 1 concessions. However, we do not recommend this approach for the following reasons: (a) it would expand the Tier 1 population to include any future LP that commits \$50,000,000 or more, potentially granting the full Tier 1 package---including LPAC eligibility and no-fee/no-carry co-investment---to a significantly larger group of LPs than intended; (b) it would reduce the differentiation between Tier 1 and Tier 2, diminishing the incentive for commitments at the \$75,000,000+ level; and (c) it may set an expectation among prospective LPs that a \$50,000,000 commitment entitles them to the same treatment as a \$100,000,000 commitment, which could create negotiation difficulties during the fundraising process.

Sagebrush\'s representatives should be instructed not to offer or imply concessions beyond the approved menu without prior approval from CLSO GP and consultation with Calderwood & Harkness. Ashworth & Lyle LLP (Sara Phan) may review the framework for placement agent compliance implications, including any concerns under SEC or FINRA regulations regarding the marketing of side letter terms to prospective investors.
