matches.line: **[FORM OF WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF MEETING OF THE LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE OF ARDENT CAPITAL PARTNERS III LP]{.underline}**
**Effective as of February 14, 2024**

This Written Consent (this \"Consent\") is executed by the undersigned members of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\") of Ardent Capital Partners III LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Fund\" or \"Ardent Capital Partners III LP\"). The LPAC is duly constituted pursuant to Section 9.4 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund, dated as of April 15, 2019 (as amended, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"LPA\"). Each capitalized term used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meaning ascribed to such term in the LPA.

Section 9.4 of the LPA authorizes the LPAC to act by written consent in lieu of a meeting, provided that such written consent is executed by all members of the LPAC then serving and is delivered to the General Partner in accordance with the notice provisions of the LPA. Section 9.4 further requires the prior written consent of the LPAC for certain material actions proposed to be taken by the General Partner, including, without limitation, material changes to the management structure of the Fund, material amendments to the organizational documents of the General Partner or the Management Company, changes to the carried interest allocation among the principals of the Fund\'s management platform, and the departure or replacement of senior investment professionals (other than Key Persons, whose departure is separately addressed under Section 5.2 of the LPA).

The matters set forth herein were presented to, discussed by, and reviewed by the members of the LPAC at a virtual meeting of the LPAC held on February 14, 2024, at which representatives of the General Partner and its legal counsel were present and responded to questions from the LPAC members. Following such discussion and review, the undersigned members of the LPAC hereby adopt the following recitals and resolutions by written consent effective as of the date first written above.

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner has proposed a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of the Fund\'s management platform (the \"Restructuring\"), as more fully described in the materials provided to the LPAC and summarized herein;

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner notified the LPAC of the Restructuring by letter dated February 5, 2024 (the \"Notification Letter\"), and has provided the LPAC with a detailed presentation memorandum summarizing the Restructuring, including the proposed entity structure, ownership realignment, economic reallocation, and departure arrangements (the \"LPAC Presentation Memorandum\"), copies of which have been made available to each LPAC member through the Fund\'s secure data room;

**WHEREAS**, David Kellner, Senior Partner, has informed the General Partner of his intention to retire from the Ardent platform effective as of March 31, 2024, and, following such retirement, Mr. Kellner will transition to a Senior Advisor role pursuant to a Senior Advisor Agreement to be entered into between Mr. Kellner and the Management Company, under which Mr. Kellner will provide transitional advisory services to the Fund\'s investment team on a part-time, non-exclusive basis for a period of up to twelve (12) months following his departure;

**WHEREAS**, Joanna Trask, Partner, has informed the General Partner of her intention to depart from the Ardent platform effective as of April 15, 2024, and Ms. Trask will not assume any continuing advisory or consultative role with the Fund, the General Partner, or the Management Company following her departure;

**WHEREAS**, the LPAC has been informed and acknowledges that neither Mr. Kellner nor Ms. Trask is a \"Key Person\" as defined in Section 5.2 of the LPA (the designated Key Persons being Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan), and accordingly the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, individually or in the aggregate, do not constitute a \"Key Person Event\" under Section 5.2 of the LPA and do not trigger the suspension of the investment period, the Key Person cure period, or any other remedial provisions set forth in Section 5.2;

**WHEREAS**, the Restructuring requires the adoption and execution of Amendment No. 1 to the LPA (the \"LPA Amendment\") to reflect, among other things, (a) the restructured ownership of the General Partner through the HoldCo and GP Intermediate structure, (b) updated defined terms, including revised definitions of \"General Partner,\" \"Management Company,\" \"Principals,\" and related terms, (c) updated GP commitment provisions to reflect the assumption of the departing principals\' unfunded capital commitments, aggregating Three Million Four Hundred Two Thousand Dollars (\$3,402,000), by the remaining HoldCo members on a pro rata basis in accordance with their respective HoldCo membership interests, and (d) conforming amendments to Section 5.2 (Key Person), Section 8.3 (Transfer of GP Interest), and Section 9.4 (LPAC Consent) of the LPA;
**WHEREAS**, the Restructuring requires the negotiation, execution, and delivery of the following documents (collectively, the \"Restructuring Documents\"):

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner has represented to the LPAC, both in the Notification Letter and in the LPAC Presentation Memorandum and at the virtual LPAC meeting held on February 14, 2024, that the Restructuring will not result in any change to:

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the foregoing recitals and upon the representations made by the General Partner to the LPAC, the undersigned members of the LPAC hereby adopt the following resolutions by written consent effective as of the date first written above:

**RESOLVED**, that the LPAC hereby consents to the formation of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC as a Delaware limited liability company to serve as the parent holding company of the General Partner (through GP Intermediate) and the Management Company, with membership interests in HoldCo to be held by Marcus Aldridge (42%), Priya Narayanan (36%), Robert Hsiao (14%), Elena Marchetti (4%), and Samuel Okonkwo (4%), and with governance, voting, and distribution rights as set forth in the Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Agreement of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC, a summary of which has been provided to the LPAC as part of the LPAC Presentation Memorandum.

**RESOLVED**, that the LPAC hereby consents to the formation of Ardent GP Intermediate LLC as a Delaware limited liability company to serve as an intermediate holding entity between HoldCo (as its sole member) and the General Partner, and that the LPAC further consents to the admission of GP Intermediate as the sole member of the General Partner following the withdrawal of the Current Principals as individual members thereof, all as set forth in the applicable Restructuring Documents.

**RESOLVED**, that the LPAC hereby consents to the execution and delivery of the Second Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Agreement of Ardent Capital GP III LLC, in substantially the form summarized in the LPAC Presentation Memorandum, providing for, among other things:
> \(i\) the withdrawal of David Kellner and Joanna Trask as members of the General Partner, effective as of their respective departure dates;

and the LPAC further confirms that the adoption of such Second Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Agreement shall be consistent with the obligations and protections of the limited partners under the LPA.

**RESOLVED**, that the LPAC hereby consents to the execution and delivery of the Second Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Agreement of Ardent Capital Management LLC, in substantially the form summarized in the LPAC Presentation Memorandum, providing for, among other things:

and the LPAC further acknowledges that the restructuring of the Management Company\'s membership and governance shall not affect the Management Company\'s obligations to the Fund under the Investment Management Agreement or otherwise modify the duties owed by the Management Company to the Fund and its limited partners.

**RESOLVED**, that the LPAC hereby consents to Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Ardent Capital Partners III LP, in substantially the form to be circulated to the limited partners for their consent or acknowledgment in accordance with the amendment provisions of the LPA, providing for, among other things:

> \(iii\) conforming amendments to Section 5.2 (Key Person) to clarify that the designated Key Persons remain Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan, to Section 8.3 (Transfer of GP Interest) to reflect the indirect holding of the General Partner\'s interest through GP Intermediate and HoldCo, and to Section 9.4 (LPAC Consent) to update cross-references and ensure consistency with the restructured organizational structure;

and the LPAC further acknowledges that the LPA Amendment shall be subject to such additional limited partner consent or acknowledgment requirements as may be set forth in the amendment provisions of the LPA and shall not become effective until all such requirements have been satisfied.

**RESOLVED**, that the LPAC hereby consents to the Amended and Restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement, providing for the reallocation of the carried interest pool (twenty percent (20%) of net profits) among the Continuing Principals and next-generation principals as follows:

with appropriate carve-outs and reserves for (a) David Kellner\'s retained vested carried interest (100% of vested carry as of March 31, 2024) and (b) Joanna Trask\'s retained vested carried interest (60% of vested carry as of April 15, 2024), in each case subject to clawback obligations as set forth in their respective Separation and Release Agreements and in accordance with the clawback provisions of Section 6.4 of the LPA; and the LPAC further acknowledges that the aggregate carried interest payable by the Fund to the General Partner and its affiliates shall not be increased as a result of the reallocation and that the reallocation is solely an internal matter among the principals of the Fund\'s management platform.

**RESOLVED**, that the LPAC hereby consents to the departure of David Kellner as a member of the General Partner and the Management Company, effective as of March 31, 2024, and the LPAC hereby acknowledges that:

> \(iv\) the terms of Mr. Kellner\'s separation, including all economic, restrictive covenant, non-solicitation, and confidentiality arrangements, are set forth in the Separation and Release Agreement between the General Partner, the Management Company, and Mr. Kellner, and the related Senior Advisor Agreement, summaries of which have been provided to the LPAC;
and the LPAC further acknowledges that it has had the opportunity to review and discuss the terms of Mr. Kellner\'s departure with the General Partner and its legal counsel.

**RESOLVED**, that the LPAC hereby consents to the departure of Joanna Trask as a member of the General Partner and the Management Company, effective as of April 15, 2024, and the LPAC hereby acknowledges that:

> \(iii\) the terms of Ms. Trask\'s separation, including all economic, restrictive covenant, non-solicitation, and confidentiality arrangements, are set forth in the Separation and Release Agreement between the General Partner, the Management Company, and Ms. Trask, a summary of which has been provided to the LPAC;
and the LPAC further acknowledges that it has had the opportunity to review and discuss the terms of Ms. Trask\'s departure with the General Partner and its legal counsel.

**RESOLVED**, that the LPAC hereby consents to the execution and delivery by the General Partner, on behalf of the Fund (to the extent applicable), and by the Management Company and the other parties thereto, of all Restructuring Documents, including without limitation all certificates of formation, certificates of amendment, operating agreements, amendments, separation agreements, advisory agreements, carried interest allocation agreements, management fee sharing agreements, and all other certificates, instruments, and agreements contemplated thereby or otherwise necessary or advisable to effectuate the Restructuring, in each case in substantially the form described in or consistent with the LPAC Presentation Memorandum, subject to such modifications as the General Partner may determine in good faith to be necessary or appropriate and that are not materially adverse to the interests of the limited partners of the Fund.

**RESOLVED**, that the LPAC hereby authorizes the General Partner and each of its authorized officers, members, managers, and representatives to take all such further actions and to negotiate, execute, and deliver all such further documents, instruments, certificates, and agreements as may be necessary or desirable to carry out the purposes and intent of the foregoing resolutions, including without limitation the filing of any certificates or other documents with any governmental authority, the engagement of legal counsel, accountants, and other advisors, and the making of any notices, disclosures, or filings required by applicable law, regulation, or the terms of the LPA or any side letter.
The undersigned members of the LPAC hereby acknowledge receipt and review of the following materials in connection with the Restructuring:
> \(i\) the LPAC Notification and Consent Solicitation Letter dated February 5, 2024, from the General Partner to the members of the LPAC;

> \(ii\) the LPAC Presentation Memorandum, including all exhibits and appendices thereto, summarizing the Restructuring, the proposed entity structure, the economic realignment, and the departure arrangements; and

The LPAC\'s consent set forth herein is given solely pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA and in respect of the specific matters described in the resolutions above. This Consent shall not be deemed to constitute a waiver of any other rights of the LPAC or any individual LPAC member under the LPA, nor shall it be deemed a waiver of any rights, claims, or remedies of any limited partner of the Fund under the LPA, any side letter, or applicable law.

Nothing in this Consent shall modify, limit, or waive any rights, obligations, or protections of any limited partner under any side letter or supplemental agreement executed in connection with such limited partner\'s subscription to the Fund, including without limitation any most-favored-nation (\"MFN\") rights, expanded key-person provisions, enhanced fee transparency or fee reduction provisions, co-investment rights or obligations, information rights, restructuring consent or notification provisions, or any other supplemental or protective provisions contained in any such side letter or supplemental agreement. The General Partner shall comply with any notification, consent, or other requirements applicable to the Restructuring under any such side letter or supplemental agreement.

The LPAC reserves all rights to request additional information from the General Partner regarding the implementation and consummation of the Restructuring, including without limitation the right to request copies of executed Restructuring Documents (subject to any applicable confidentiality restrictions), updates on the transition of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, and confirmation of the completion of the Restructuring and the effectiveness of the LPA Amendment.

This Consent may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which, when taken together, shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page to this Consent by facsimile or electronic transmission (including portable document format (.pdf) or any electronic signature complying with the U.S. federal ESIGN Act of 2000 or the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act) shall be deemed delivery of an original executed counterpart and shall be effective as an original signature for all purposes.
**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the undersigned members of the LPAC have executed this Written Consent effective as of February 14, 2024.
**LPAC MEMBERS. RIDGELINE PUBLIC EMPLOYEES\' RETIREMENT SYSTEM** Commitment to Fund: \$225,000,000

The undersigned, in its capacity as sole general partner of the Fund, hereby acknowledges receipt of the foregoing Written Consent of the LPAC, confirms that the Written Consent has been executed by all members of the LPAC then serving, and agrees that the Restructuring shall be implemented in accordance with the terms and conditions described herein and in the Restructuring Documents.

Line 13: This First Amendment (the \"**Amendment**\") to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP, a Delaware limited partnership (EIN: 85-2103748) (the \"**Partnership**\" or \"**Fund IV**\"), dated as of the final close date of June 15, 2021 (as the same may have been supplemented or modified prior to the date hereof, the \"**Partnership Agreement**\"), is entered into as of \[●\], 2025 (the \"**Execution Date**\"), by and among:
Line 39: > **(ii)** *Impact of OECD Pillar Two GloBE Rules.* The forthcoming implementation of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (\"**OECD**\") Pillar Two Global Anti-Base Erosion (\"**GloBE**\") rules, which become effective for Solara\'s Luxembourg entities from fiscal year 2025 onward, substantially diminishes the tax efficiency benefits historically associated with the Luxembourg SCSp structures. The qualified domestic minimum top-up tax and income inclusion rules under Pillar Two will subject income allocated through the Luxembourg vehicles to additional taxation, thereby eliminating much of the tax benefit that originally motivated the use of such structures.
Line 43: > **(iv)** *LP-Requested Governance Simplification.* Multiple Limited Partners, including institutional investors and their advisory committees, have requested that Solara simplify the governance and reporting framework across the platform, reduce the number of separate fund vehicles to which they must commit capital, and streamline the decision-making processes associated with cross-vehicle transactions and co-investment opportunities.
Line 45: **E.** *Description of the Reorganization.* The Reorganization involves a multi-step transaction designed to consolidate the offshore parallel fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure. The Reorganization consists of five integrated steps planned for execution in the fourth quarter of 2025, with a target effective date of December 1, 2025 (the \"**Target Effective Date**\"), as follows:
Line 83: **I.** *LPAC and LP Consent.* At a duly convened meeting of the LP Advisory Committee (\"**LPAC**\") held on April 22, 2025, the LPAC --- which was advised by Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP, counsel to the LPAC (with Diana Carruthers serving as key attorney and principal point of contact) --- provided preliminary consent to the Reorganization. The members of the LPAC voting in favor of such preliminary consent represent seventy-eight percent (78%) in interest of the Partners. The Partnership Agreement requires the consent of the Limited Partners for certain actions, including the amendment thereof and the authorization of transactions of the nature contemplated by the Reorganization. The General Partner is soliciting the consent of the Limited Partners to this Amendment and the transactions contemplated hereby.
Line 85: **J.** *Lender and Third-Party Consents.* The Reorganization requires consent under the Partnership\'s One Billion One Hundred Million Dollar (\$1,100,000,000) revolving subscription credit facility (the \"**Subscription Facility**\") with Ashford National Bank, N.A. (\"**Ashford**\"), administered by Thomas Greenleaf, Managing Director, Fund Finance, whose offices are located at 225 West Wacker Drive, Suite 5000, Chicago, IL 60606. The Subscription Facility contains change-of-control, borrowing base, and collateral assignment provisions that are implicated by the Reorganization, and accordingly, lender consent and possible facility amendments are required prior to the consummation of the Reorganization Steps. Notification and/or endorsement is also required from Hawkstone Specialty Insurance Co. (\"**Hawkstone**\"), the provider of the Partnership\'s directors\' and officers\' liability and errors and omissions insurance coverage, which has an aggregate policy limit of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000). The principal contact at Hawkstone is Neil Braddock, Senior Underwriter. Additionally, fund administration transition coordination is required with Clarendon Fund Services Ltd. (\"**Clarendon**\"), the Partnership\'s fund administrator, with Rachel Okonkwo, Client Relationship Director, serving as the principal liaison.
Line 87: **K.** *Authorization.* The General Partner has determined, in its reasonable business judgment and in the exercise of its fiduciary duties under applicable law and the Partnership Agreement, that the Reorganization and this Amendment are in the best interests of the Partnership and the Partners, and has authorized the execution and delivery of this Amendment and the related Transaction Documents (as defined below).
Line 99: > \"**Amendment Effective Date**\" means the date on which the requisite LP consent has been obtained in accordance with the Partnership Agreement and this Amendment has been duly executed and delivered by the General Partner and the requisite Limited Partners.
Line 121: > \"**Target Effective Date**\" means December 1, 2025, or such other date as the General Partner may determine in accordance with the terms of this Amendment.
Line 125: > \"**Transaction Documents**\" means, collectively, (a) the limited partnership agreement of the Master Fund, (b) the check-the-box election forms (IRS Form 8832) for each newly formed entity, (c) certificates of formation and certificates of limited partnership for each newly formed entity, (d) contribution agreements between each contributing Legacy Offshore Vehicle and the Master Fund, (e) lender consent agreements and any amendments to the Subscription Facility, (f) LP consent forms, (g) dissolution instruments for each Legacy Offshore Vehicle, (h) insurance endorsement requests and confirmations, (i) fund administrator transition agreements, and (j) all other agreements, instruments, certificates, and documents executed, delivered, or filed in connection with the Reorganization.
Line 141: > **(i)** Form or cause the formation of the Master Fund, the Master Fund GP, the International Feeder, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, including the preparation, execution, and filing of all necessary certificates of formation, certificates of limited partnership, and other organizational documents with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, the Registrar of Exempted Limited Partnerships of the Cayman Islands, or any other applicable governmental authority;
Line 143: > **(ii)** File or cause to be filed IRS Form 8832 check-the-box elections, pursuant to Treasury Regulations Section 301.7701-3, for each of the newly formed entities to be classified as partnerships for U.S. federal income tax purposes, with effective dates coordinated with the respective Reorganization Steps;
Line 153: > **(vii)** Obtain lender consent from Ashford National Bank, N.A. under the Subscription Facility and negotiate and execute any amendments, waivers, or modifications to the Subscription Facility as may be necessary or advisable to reflect the post-Reorganization structure, including modifications to borrowing base definitions, change-of-control provisions, collateral assignment provisions, and related terms;
Line 155: > **(viii)** Obtain any insurance endorsements, regulatory approvals, or third-party consents as may be necessary or advisable in connection with the Reorganization, including without limitation endorsements from Hawkstone Specialty Insurance Co. to add newly formed entities as additional insureds under the existing directors\' and officers\' liability and errors and omissions insurance policies;
Line 169: > **(a)** The Partnership (Fund IV LP) shall co-invest alongside the Master Fund with respect to current and future portfolio investments, pursuant to co-investment arrangements to be entered into between the Partnership (acting through the General Partner) and the Master Fund (acting through the Master Fund GP). Such co-investment arrangements shall be designed to ensure that the Partnership and its Limited Partners continue to participate in the investment opportunities and portfolio performance consistent with the Partnership\'s stated investment mandate, sector focus, and return objectives.
Line 173: > **(c)** The General Partner shall have the authority to enter into co-investment agreements, side letters, and related arrangements with the Master Fund on behalf of the Partnership, provided that any such arrangements are consistent in all material respects with the investment mandate, concentration limits, and fee arrangements set forth in the Partnership Agreement. The General Partner shall provide the Limited Partners with copies of any co-investment agreements entered into with the Master Fund within thirty (30) days of execution.
Line 211: The Partnership Agreement\'s existing transfer restrictions, including any provisions requiring General Partner consent to transfers of limited partnership interests, right-of-first-refusal provisions, and restrictions on transfers that would result in a termination of the Partnership under IRC § 708(b)(1)(B) (as in effect prior to its repeal), shall continue to apply in full force and effect to interests in the Partnership following the Reorganization; *provided, however,* that the migration of limited partners from Legacy Offshore Vehicles into the International Feeder or Tax-Exempt Feeder pursuant to Step 5 of the Reorganization shall not be deemed a \"transfer,\" \"assignment,\" \"sale,\" \"exchange,\" or other disposition for purposes of any transfer restriction provisions of the Partnership Agreement or any side letter, subscription agreement, or other agreement entered into in connection with the Partnership.
Line 215: The General Partner is authorized to negotiate and execute amendments, modifications, waivers, consents, and supplemental agreements to the One Billion One Hundred Million Dollar (\$1,100,000,000) revolving subscription credit facility with Ashford National Bank, N.A. as may be necessary or advisable to reflect the post-Reorganization structure of the Partnership and the fund platform. Without limiting the foregoing, such amendments may include modifications to (i) the definition of \"borrowing base\" and the inclusion or exclusion of capital commitments held through the Master Fund or the Feeders, (ii) change-of-control provisions to accommodate the Reorganization, (iii) collateral assignment provisions and security interest terms, (iv) the addition of the Master Fund or the Feeders as borrowers or guarantors, and (v) any financial covenants, reporting requirements, or administrative provisions affected by the Reorganization.
Line 217: The General Partner shall provide the Limited Partners with notice of any material amendments to the Subscription Facility resulting from the Reorganization within thirty (30) days of the execution of such amendments. For the purposes of this Section 2.7, \"material amendments\" shall include any amendment that results in a change to the aggregate commitment amount, the interest rate or pricing terms, the maturity date, or the borrowing base methodology of the Subscription Facility.
Line 223: The Limited Partners hereby ratify, confirm, and approve the General Partner\'s authority to take all actions described in Article II and the Recitals of this Amendment, and hereby grant the General Partner full power and authority to act on behalf of the Partnership in connection with the Reorganization and the execution and delivery of the Transaction Documents.
Line 251: **Section 3.2 --- Execution of Transaction Documents**
Line 261: > **(d)** Lender consent agreements and facility amendment agreements with Ashford National Bank, N.A. under the Subscription Facility;
Line 281: > **(a)** *Due Authorization.* The Reorganization has been duly authorized by the General Partner\'s governing body, acting by unanimous written consent, as approved on March 14, 2025. The General Partner has the requisite organizational power and authority to execute and deliver this Amendment and to perform its obligations hereunder and under the Transaction Documents.
Line 285: > **(c)** *No Material Adverse Effect.* The General Partner reasonably believes, based on the advice of its legal and tax advisors and on its own analysis and business judgment, that the Reorganization will not result in a material adverse effect on the Partnership, the Partners, or the Partnership\'s portfolio investments. The Reorganization is designed to be neutral to, or beneficial for, the economic interests of the Partners.
Line 289: > **(e)** *Third-Party Consents.* The General Partner has obtained, or will obtain prior to the consummation of the Reorganization, all necessary third-party consents required to implement the Reorganization, including lender consent from Ashford National Bank, N.A. under the Subscription Facility. To the General Partner\'s knowledge, there is no impediment to obtaining such consents other than the completion of customary administrative and documentary processes.
Line 313: **Section 5.1 --- Conditions to the Effectiveness of the Reorganization**
Line 317: > **(a)** *LP Consent.* Receipt of the requisite consent of the Limited Partners as required under the Partnership Agreement and this Amendment, which consent may be evidenced by execution of this Amendment, by a separate written consent instrument, or by any other means permitted under the Partnership Agreement.
Line 321: > **(c)** *Lender Consent.* Receipt of lender consent from Ashford National Bank, N.A. under the Subscription Facility, in form and substance satisfactory to the General Partner, including any necessary amendments, waivers, or modifications to the Subscription Facility.
Line 325: > **(e)** *Form 8832 Elections.* Filing of IRS Form 8832 check-the-box elections for each newly formed entity, with effective dates coordinated with the Reorganization Steps, and confirmation that such elections have been properly processed or, in the case of default classifications, that no election is required.
Line 337: The General Partner may, in its sole and absolute discretion, waive any condition set forth in Section 5.1; *provided, however,* that the conditions set forth in Sections 5.1(a) (LP Consent), 5.1(c) (Lender Consent), and 5.1(d) (Formation of New Entities) may not be waived and must be satisfied in full prior to the consummation of the Reorganization. Any waiver of a condition precedent by the General Partner shall be documented in writing and shall be provided to the Limited Partners promptly following such waiver.
Line 343: The indemnification and exculpation provisions of the Partnership Agreement, including without limitation all provisions relating to the limitation of liability of the General Partner and its officers, directors, managers, members, employees, agents, and affiliates, and all provisions relating to the indemnification of the General Partner and such persons for losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses incurred in connection with the business and affairs of the Partnership, shall continue to apply in full force and effect following the execution of this Amendment and shall extend, without limitation, to all actions taken and omissions made by the General Partner and its officers, agents, counsel, and advisors in connection with the Reorganization, the execution and delivery of this Amendment, and the negotiation, execution, delivery, and performance of the Transaction Documents. The foregoing shall apply to the fullest extent permitted by the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act and applicable law.

matches.line: This First Amendment (the \"**Amendment**\") to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP, a Delaware limited partnership (EIN: 85-2103748) (the \"**Partnership**\" or \"**Fund IV**\"), dated as of the final close date of June 15, 2021 (as the same may have been supplemented or modified prior to the date hereof, the \"**Partnership Agreement**\"), is entered into as of \[●\], 2025 (the \"**Execution Date**\"), by and among:

> **(ii)** *Impact of OECD Pillar Two GloBE Rules.* The forthcoming implementation of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (\"**OECD**\") Pillar Two Global Anti-Base Erosion (\"**GloBE**\") rules, which become effective for Solara\'s Luxembourg entities from fiscal year 2025 onward, substantially diminishes the tax efficiency benefits historically associated with the Luxembourg SCSp structures. The qualified domestic minimum top-up tax and income inclusion rules under Pillar Two will subject income allocated through the Luxembourg vehicles to additional taxation, thereby eliminating much of the tax benefit that originally motivated the use of such structures.

> **(iv)** *LP-Requested Governance Simplification.* Multiple Limited Partners, including institutional investors and their advisory committees, have requested that Solara simplify the governance and reporting framework across the platform, reduce the number of separate fund vehicles to which they must commit capital, and streamline the decision-making processes associated with cross-vehicle transactions and co-investment opportunities.

**E.** *Description of the Reorganization.* The Reorganization involves a multi-step transaction designed to consolidate the offshore parallel fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure. The Reorganization consists of five integrated steps planned for execution in the fourth quarter of 2025, with a target effective date of December 1, 2025 (the \"**Target Effective Date**\"), as follows:

**I.** *LPAC and LP Consent.* At a duly convened meeting of the LP Advisory Committee (\"**LPAC**\") held on April 22, 2025, the LPAC --- which was advised by Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP, counsel to the LPAC (with Diana Carruthers serving as key attorney and principal point of contact) --- provided preliminary consent to the Reorganization. The members of the LPAC voting in favor of such preliminary consent represent seventy-eight percent (78%) in interest of the Partners. The Partnership Agreement requires the consent of the Limited Partners for certain actions, including the amendment thereof and the authorization of transactions of the nature contemplated by the Reorganization. The General Partner is soliciting the consent of the Limited Partners to this Amendment and the transactions contemplated hereby.

**J.** *Lender and Third-Party Consents.* The Reorganization requires consent under the Partnership\'s One Billion One Hundred Million Dollar (\$1,100,000,000) revolving subscription credit facility (the \"**Subscription Facility**\") with Ashford National Bank, N.A. (\"**Ashford**\"), administered by Thomas Greenleaf, Managing Director, Fund Finance, whose offices are located at 225 West Wacker Drive, Suite 5000, Chicago, IL 60606. The Subscription Facility contains change-of-control, borrowing base, and collateral assignment provisions that are implicated by the Reorganization, and accordingly, lender consent and possible facility amendments are required prior to the consummation of the Reorganization Steps. Notification and/or endorsement is also required from Hawkstone Specialty Insurance Co. (\"**Hawkstone**\"), the provider of the Partnership\'s directors\' and officers\' liability and errors and omissions insurance coverage, which has an aggregate policy limit of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000). The principal contact at Hawkstone is Neil Braddock, Senior Underwriter. Additionally, fund administration transition coordination is required with Clarendon Fund Services Ltd. (\"**Clarendon**\"), the Partnership\'s fund administrator, with Rachel Okonkwo, Client Relationship Director, serving as the principal liaison.

**K.** *Authorization.* The General Partner has determined, in its reasonable business judgment and in the exercise of its fiduciary duties under applicable law and the Partnership Agreement, that the Reorganization and this Amendment are in the best interests of the Partnership and the Partners, and has authorized the execution and delivery of this Amendment and the related Transaction Documents (as defined below).

> \"**Amendment Effective Date**\" means the date on which the requisite LP consent has been obtained in accordance with the Partnership Agreement and this Amendment has been duly executed and delivered by the General Partner and the requisite Limited Partners.
> \"**Target Effective Date**\" means December 1, 2025, or such other date as the General Partner may determine in accordance with the terms of this Amendment.

> \"**Transaction Documents**\" means, collectively, (a) the limited partnership agreement of the Master Fund, (b) the check-the-box election forms (IRS Form 8832) for each newly formed entity, (c) certificates of formation and certificates of limited partnership for each newly formed entity, (d) contribution agreements between each contributing Legacy Offshore Vehicle and the Master Fund, (e) lender consent agreements and any amendments to the Subscription Facility, (f) LP consent forms, (g) dissolution instruments for each Legacy Offshore Vehicle, (h) insurance endorsement requests and confirmations, (i) fund administrator transition agreements, and (j) all other agreements, instruments, certificates, and documents executed, delivered, or filed in connection with the Reorganization.

> **(i)** Form or cause the formation of the Master Fund, the Master Fund GP, the International Feeder, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, including the preparation, execution, and filing of all necessary certificates of formation, certificates of limited partnership, and other organizational documents with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, the Registrar of Exempted Limited Partnerships of the Cayman Islands, or any other applicable governmental authority;

> **(ii)** File or cause to be filed IRS Form 8832 check-the-box elections, pursuant to Treasury Regulations Section 301.7701-3, for each of the newly formed entities to be classified as partnerships for U.S. federal income tax purposes, with effective dates coordinated with the respective Reorganization Steps;

> **(vii)** Obtain lender consent from Ashford National Bank, N.A. under the Subscription Facility and negotiate and execute any amendments, waivers, or modifications to the Subscription Facility as may be necessary or advisable to reflect the post-Reorganization structure, including modifications to borrowing base definitions, change-of-control provisions, collateral assignment provisions, and related terms;

> **(viii)** Obtain any insurance endorsements, regulatory approvals, or third-party consents as may be necessary or advisable in connection with the Reorganization, including without limitation endorsements from Hawkstone Specialty Insurance Co. to add newly formed entities as additional insureds under the existing directors\' and officers\' liability and errors and omissions insurance policies;

> **(a)** The Partnership (Fund IV LP) shall co-invest alongside the Master Fund with respect to current and future portfolio investments, pursuant to co-investment arrangements to be entered into between the Partnership (acting through the General Partner) and the Master Fund (acting through the Master Fund GP). Such co-investment arrangements shall be designed to ensure that the Partnership and its Limited Partners continue to participate in the investment opportunities and portfolio performance consistent with the Partnership\'s stated investment mandate, sector focus, and return objectives.

> **(c)** The General Partner shall have the authority to enter into co-investment agreements, side letters, and related arrangements with the Master Fund on behalf of the Partnership, provided that any such arrangements are consistent in all material respects with the investment mandate, concentration limits, and fee arrangements set forth in the Partnership Agreement. The General Partner shall provide the Limited Partners with copies of any co-investment agreements entered into with the Master Fund within thirty (30) days of execution.

The Partnership Agreement\'s existing transfer restrictions, including any provisions requiring General Partner consent to transfers of limited partnership interests, right-of-first-refusal provisions, and restrictions on transfers that would result in a termination of the Partnership under IRC § 708(b)(1)(B) (as in effect prior to its repeal), shall continue to apply in full force and effect to interests in the Partnership following the Reorganization; *provided, however,* that the migration of limited partners from Legacy Offshore Vehicles into the International Feeder or Tax-Exempt Feeder pursuant to Step 5 of the Reorganization shall not be deemed a \"transfer,\" \"assignment,\" \"sale,\" \"exchange,\" or other disposition for purposes of any transfer restriction provisions of the Partnership Agreement or any side letter, subscription agreement, or other agreement entered into in connection with the Partnership.

The General Partner is authorized to negotiate and execute amendments, modifications, waivers, consents, and supplemental agreements to the One Billion One Hundred Million Dollar (\$1,100,000,000) revolving subscription credit facility with Ashford National Bank, N.A. as may be necessary or advisable to reflect the post-Reorganization structure of the Partnership and the fund platform. Without limiting the foregoing, such amendments may include modifications to (i) the definition of \"borrowing base\" and the inclusion or exclusion of capital commitments held through the Master Fund or the Feeders, (ii) change-of-control provisions to accommodate the Reorganization, (iii) collateral assignment provisions and security interest terms, (iv) the addition of the Master Fund or the Feeders as borrowers or guarantors, and (v) any financial covenants, reporting requirements, or administrative provisions affected by the Reorganization.

The General Partner shall provide the Limited Partners with notice of any material amendments to the Subscription Facility resulting from the Reorganization within thirty (30) days of the execution of such amendments. For the purposes of this Section 2.7, \"material amendments\" shall include any amendment that results in a change to the aggregate commitment amount, the interest rate or pricing terms, the maturity date, or the borrowing base methodology of the Subscription Facility.

The Limited Partners hereby ratify, confirm, and approve the General Partner\'s authority to take all actions described in Article II and the Recitals of this Amendment, and hereby grant the General Partner full power and authority to act on behalf of the Partnership in connection with the Reorganization and the execution and delivery of the Transaction Documents.
**Section 3.2 --- Execution of Transaction Documents**
> **(d)** Lender consent agreements and facility amendment agreements with Ashford National Bank, N.A. under the Subscription Facility;

> **(a)** *Due Authorization.* The Reorganization has been duly authorized by the General Partner\'s governing body, acting by unanimous written consent, as approved on March 14, 2025. The General Partner has the requisite organizational power and authority to execute and deliver this Amendment and to perform its obligations hereunder and under the Transaction Documents.

> **(c)** *No Material Adverse Effect.* The General Partner reasonably believes, based on the advice of its legal and tax advisors and on its own analysis and business judgment, that the Reorganization will not result in a material adverse effect on the Partnership, the Partners, or the Partnership\'s portfolio investments. The Reorganization is designed to be neutral to, or beneficial for, the economic interests of the Partners.

> **(e)** *Third-Party Consents.* The General Partner has obtained, or will obtain prior to the consummation of the Reorganization, all necessary third-party consents required to implement the Reorganization, including lender consent from Ashford National Bank, N.A. under the Subscription Facility. To the General Partner\'s knowledge, there is no impediment to obtaining such consents other than the completion of customary administrative and documentary processes.
**Section 5.1 --- Conditions to the Effectiveness of the Reorganization**

> **(a)** *LP Consent.* Receipt of the requisite consent of the Limited Partners as required under the Partnership Agreement and this Amendment, which consent may be evidenced by execution of this Amendment, by a separate written consent instrument, or by any other means permitted under the Partnership Agreement.

> **(c)** *Lender Consent.* Receipt of lender consent from Ashford National Bank, N.A. under the Subscription Facility, in form and substance satisfactory to the General Partner, including any necessary amendments, waivers, or modifications to the Subscription Facility.

> **(e)** *Form 8832 Elections.* Filing of IRS Form 8832 check-the-box elections for each newly formed entity, with effective dates coordinated with the Reorganization Steps, and confirmation that such elections have been properly processed or, in the case of default classifications, that no election is required.

The General Partner may, in its sole and absolute discretion, waive any condition set forth in Section 5.1; *provided, however,* that the conditions set forth in Sections 5.1(a) (LP Consent), 5.1(c) (Lender Consent), and 5.1(d) (Formation of New Entities) may not be waived and must be satisfied in full prior to the consummation of the Reorganization. Any waiver of a condition precedent by the General Partner shall be documented in writing and shall be provided to the Limited Partners promptly following such waiver.

The indemnification and exculpation provisions of the Partnership Agreement, including without limitation all provisions relating to the limitation of liability of the General Partner and its officers, directors, managers, members, employees, agents, and affiliates, and all provisions relating to the indemnification of the General Partner and such persons for losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses incurred in connection with the business and affairs of the Partnership, shall continue to apply in full force and effect following the execution of this Amendment and shall extend, without limitation, to all actions taken and omissions made by the General Partner and its officers, agents, counsel, and advisors in connection with the Reorganization, the execution and delivery of this Amendment, and the negotiation, execution, delivery, and performance of the Transaction Documents. The foregoing shall apply to the fullest extent permitted by the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act and applicable law.
**Section 7.1 --- Effectiveness**

This Amendment shall become effective upon the later of (a) its execution and delivery by the General Partner and (b) the receipt of the requisite consent of the Limited Partners holding the required percentage in interest as specified in the Partnership Agreement (such later date, the \"**Amendment Effective Date**\"). This Amendment shall not be effective as to any Reorganization Step until the conditions precedent set forth in Article V with respect to such Reorganization Step have been satisfied or waived in accordance with Section 5.2. The Amendment Effective Date shall be documented by written confirmation from the General Partner to the Limited Partners.

Except as expressly amended, supplemented, or modified hereby, the Partnership Agreement shall remain in full force and effect and is hereby ratified and confirmed in all respects. All terms, conditions, covenants, representations, warranties, and agreements set forth in the Partnership Agreement that are not expressly amended by this Amendment shall continue unchanged. Each reference in the Partnership Agreement to \"this Agreement,\" \"herein,\" \"hereof,\" \"hereunder,\" or words of similar import shall, from and after the Amendment Effective Date, be deemed to be a reference to the Partnership Agreement as amended by this Amendment.

This Amendment may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. The exchange of copies of this Amendment and of signature pages by facsimile transmission, by electronic mail in portable document format (\".pdf\"), or by any other electronic means intended to preserve the original graphic and pictorial appearance of a document shall have the same effect as physical delivery of the paper document bearing an original signature. Electronic signatures transmitted by Brightwater Software, Ashford Health IT, or similar electronic signature platforms, and PDF copies of manually executed signature pages, shall be deemed original signatures for all purposes of this Amendment and applicable law, including the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act, as adopted in the State of Delaware.

All notices, requests, demands, consents, waivers, and other communications required or permitted to be given under this Amendment shall be in writing and shall be given in accordance with the notice provisions of the Partnership Agreement. The General Partner\'s address for notices under this Amendment is:

Each Partner agrees to execute and deliver such further instruments, documents, and agreements, and to take such further actions, as may be reasonably necessary or advisable to carry out the purposes and intent of this Amendment and the Reorganization, including the execution of any additional consent forms, tax election forms, organizational documents, and ancillary agreements as may be required in connection with the Transaction Documents or the implementation of the Reorganization Steps.

Nothing in this Amendment, express or implied, is intended to, or shall, confer upon any person other than the Partners (and their respective successors and permitted assigns) any rights, benefits, or remedies of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Amendment; *provided, however,* that Ashford National Bank, N.A. and Sentinel Capital Markets LLC, in their capacities as lender and placement agent, respectively, shall be entitled to rely on the representations, authorizations, and covenants contained herein to the extent set forth in any lender consent, facility amendment, or placement agent agreement executed in connection with the Reorganization.

This Amendment may be further amended, supplemented, or modified only by a written instrument duly executed by the General Partner and the Limited Partners holding the requisite percentage in interest as specified in the Partnership Agreement. No oral agreement, course of dealing, or trade usage shall operate to amend, supplement, or modify any provision of this Amendment.

**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the undersigned have executed this First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP as of the date first written above.

This First Amendment (this \"Amendment\") to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Partnership\" or \"Fund V\"), is entered into as of \[●\], 2025 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as general partner of the Partnership (the \"General Partner\" or \"Solara GP\"), and the limited partners of the Partnership (collectively, the \"Limited Partners\" and, together with the General Partner, the \"Partners\").

**WHEREAS**, the LP Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\") of the Partnership met on April 22, 2025, and, following a presentation by the General Partner and review of materials prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP, provided preliminary consent to the Reorganization, with Limited Partners holding approximately 78% in interest of the capital commitments to the Partnership voting in favor of the Reorganization;

**WHEREAS**, the Reorganization is motivated by the following considerations: (i) operational cost reduction --- the Solara platform currently incurs approximately \$3,800,000 annually in duplicative offshore administration, audit, regulatory filing, and compliance fees across the parallel fund structures, which costs are expected to be materially reduced through consolidation; (ii) the impact of forthcoming Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (\"OECD\") Pillar Two Global Anti-Base Erosion (\"GloBE\") rules, which become effective for the Luxembourg SCSp entities from fiscal year 2025 and which diminish certain tax benefits that were originally expected to be derived from the Luxembourg structures; (iii) simplified compliance under the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (\"FATCA\") (IRC §§ 1471--1474) and the Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\") reporting requirements, enabling more efficient tax information exchange across the Solara platform; and (iv) LP-requested governance simplification, as multiple Limited Partners have expressed a preference for a streamlined fund structure that reduces complexity in reporting, distributions, and investment monitoring;

**WHEREAS**, the Reorganization involves the domestication and effective merger of the Cayman Islands and Luxembourg parallel fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure, specifically involving the formation and utilization of the following new entities:

> **Step 1** (target effective date: September 15, 2025) --- Formation of the Master Fund GP, the Consolidated Master Fund, the International Feeder, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, including the filing of certificates of formation and certificates of limited partnership with the Delaware Secretary of State for the Delaware entities and the registration of the Cayman entities with the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, and the filing of Internal Revenue Service Form 8832 entity classification elections (check-the-box elections) for each new entity to be classified as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes under Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-3;

> **Step 2** (target effective date: October 1, 2025) --- Contribution by Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP (\"Fund IV-A Cayman\") of all of its portfolio company assets (aggregate fair market value of \$2,310,000,000; adjusted tax basis of \$1,620,000,000; built-in gain of \$690,000,000) to the Consolidated Master Fund in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Consolidated Master Fund;

> **Step 3** (target effective date: October 15, 2025) --- Contribution by Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp (\"Fund IV-B Lux\") of all of its portfolio company assets (aggregate fair market value of €1,070,000,000 / approximately \$1,160,000,000; adjusted tax basis of €782,000,000 / approximately \$844,600,000; built-in gain of €288,000,000 / approximately \$311,000,000) to the Consolidated Master Fund in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Consolidated Master Fund;

> **Step 4** (target effective date: November 1, 2025) --- Contribution by Fund V-A Cayman of all of its portfolio company assets (aggregate fair market value of \$2,890,000,000; adjusted tax basis of \$2,340,000,000; built-in gain of \$550,000,000) to the Consolidated Master Fund in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Consolidated Master Fund, and contribution by Fund V-B Lux of all of its portfolio company assets (aggregate fair market value of €1,290,000,000 / approximately \$1,390,000,000; adjusted tax basis of €1,140,000,000 / approximately \$1,230,000,000; built-in gain of €150,000,000 / approximately \$162,000,000) to the Consolidated Master Fund in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Consolidated Master Fund; and

> **Step 5** (target effective date: December 1, 2025) --- Dissolution of Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux (along with Fund IV-A Cayman and Fund IV-B Lux) and distribution of their respective limited partnership interests in the Consolidated Master Fund to their existing limited partners, with non-U.S. limited partners rolling into the International Feeder and U.S. tax-exempt limited partners rolling into the Tax-Exempt Feeder;

**WHEREAS**, Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP (Diana Carruthers, Partner) serves as outside counsel to the LPAC and has reviewed the proposed Reorganization for LP consent purposes and has provided the LPAC with an independent assessment of the potential risks, benefits, and alternatives associated with the Reorganization;

**WHEREAS**, the Partnership Agreement requires the consent of the Limited Partners holding a specified percentage in interest of capital commitments for certain amendments to the Partnership Agreement and for certain significant transactions, and this Amendment is being submitted to the Limited Partners for their approval in accordance with such requirements;

\"**Reorganization Documents**\" means, collectively, all agreements, instruments, certificates, consents, elections, filings, and other documents to be executed, delivered, and filed in connection with the Reorganization, including, without limitation, the limited partnership agreement of the Consolidated Master Fund, the operating agreement of the Master Fund GP, the limited partnership agreements of the International Feeder and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, contribution agreements, assignment and assumption agreements, Form 8832 entity classification elections, the PLR Request, lender consent letters, insurance endorsements, and any other documents reasonably necessary to consummate the Reorganization.

\(b\) In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the terms and provisions of this Amendment and the terms and provisions of the Partnership Agreement (as in effect immediately prior to the effectiveness of this Amendment), the terms and provisions of this Amendment shall control and prevail.
**Section 2.1 --- Consent to the Reorganization**
The Limited Partners hereby consent to the Reorganization as described in the Recitals to this Amendment, including, without limitation, the following actions:

> \(a\) The contribution by Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux of all of their respective portfolio company assets to the Consolidated Master Fund in exchange for limited partnership interests therein, as contemplated by Step 4 of the Reorganization (target effective date: November 1, 2025);

> \(b\) The dissolution of Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux and the distribution of their respective partnership interests in the Consolidated Master Fund to their respective limited partners, as contemplated by Step 5 of the Reorganization (target effective date: December 1, 2025);

> \(d\) The establishment of the post-Reorganization structure whereby Fund V LP will co-invest directly alongside the Consolidated Master Fund on a proportionate basis, rather than alongside separate parallel offshore vehicles, in a manner designed to preserve the economic rights, investment exposure, and proportionate sharing of gains, losses, and distributions applicable to the Limited Partners.

The consent of the Limited Partners provided pursuant to this Section 2.1 is granted with the understanding that the Reorganization is subject to the conditions precedent set forth in Article V of this Amendment and that the General Partner retains the authority to modify the timing and structure of the Reorganization steps as provided in Section 2.4.

> \(b\) **Negotiation and Execution of Reorganization Documents.** Negotiate, execute, and deliver the limited partnership agreement of the Consolidated Master Fund, the operating agreement of the Master Fund GP, the limited partnership agreements of the International Feeder and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, and all other Reorganization Documents, on such terms and conditions as the General Partner determines in its reasonable discretion to be in the best interests of the Partnership and the Limited Partners;

> \(c\) **Entity Classification Elections.** File Internal Revenue Service Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) for the Consolidated Master Fund, the International Feeder, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, in each case electing classification as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes under Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-3, and take all actions necessary to ensure the timely filing and effectiveness of such elections;

> \(g\) **Asset Contributions and Reorganization Steps.** Cause the contribution of Fund V parallel vehicle portfolio company assets to the Consolidated Master Fund and take all actions necessary or advisable to consummate Steps 4 and 5 of the Reorganization, including the execution of contribution agreements, assignment and assumption agreements, and instruments of transfer;

> \(j\) **Lender Consents.** Execute amendments, consents, and waivers under existing credit facilities as necessary to permit the consummation of the Reorganization, including obtaining consent from Ashford National Bank, N.A. (Thomas Greenleaf, Managing Director, Fund Finance) and Sentinel Capital Markets LLC (Laura Pak, Vice President) under the Partnership\'s \$1,500,000,000 Fund V subscription revolving credit facility, and negotiate such modifications to the credit facility documentation as may be required to reflect the post-Reorganization structure;

> \(o\) **General Authority.** Take all other actions as may be reasonably necessary, appropriate, or desirable to consummate the Reorganization, including the execution and delivery of any additional agreements, instruments, certificates, consents, and filings, and the engagement of additional advisors, service providers, and professionals as the General Partner may determine in its reasonable discretion to be necessary or advisable.

> \(h\) **No IRC § 1446 Withholding.** No withholding under IRC § 1446(a) is required with respect to the Step 4 Contributions or the Step 5 distributions, as the Step 4 Contributions are tax-free contributions that do not give rise to effectively connected taxable income allocable to foreign partners, and the Step 5 distributions are tax-free distributions under IRC § 731(a).

The authorization granted to the General Partner pursuant to this Article II extends to actions taken prior to, on, or after the Effective Date in furtherance of the Reorganization. Any actions taken by the General Partner prior to the Effective Date that were within the scope of the authorization granted by this Article II are hereby ratified and confirmed.

The General Partner may modify the timing of the Reorganization steps described in the Recitals, provided that the target effective date for the Step 5 Dissolutions remains on or about December 1, 2025, or such other date as the General Partner determines in its reasonable discretion, taking into account the progress of the PLR Request, the receipt of lender consents, the availability of regulatory approvals, and other relevant factors. The General Partner shall provide the LPAC with reasonable advance notice of any material changes to the Reorganization timeline.

The General Partner may adjust the structure of the Reorganization as reasonably necessary to address feedback received from the IRS during the pre-submission conference (which has been requested for July 22, 2025) or in response to the PLR Request, or to address changes in applicable tax law, regulation, or administrative guidance, provided that such adjustments do not materially adversely affect the economic rights, investment exposure, or tax position of the Limited Partners. If any structural adjustment is required that would, in the General Partner\'s reasonable judgment, materially adversely affect the Limited Partners, the General Partner shall seek LPAC consent prior to implementing such adjustment.

The transfer restrictions and withdrawal provisions in the Partnership Agreement are hereby amended to permit the limited partner migration contemplated in Step 5 of the Reorganization without requiring the individual transfer consent procedures that would otherwise apply under the Partnership Agreement. Specifically:

> \(a\) The migration of non-U.S. limited partners from Fund V-A Cayman to the International Feeder shall not be treated as a \"transfer\" requiring the General Partner\'s consent or the satisfaction of any other transfer conditions under the Partnership Agreement; and

> \(b\) The migration of U.S. tax-exempt limited partners from Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux to the Tax-Exempt Feeder shall not be treated as a \"transfer\" requiring the General Partner\'s consent or the satisfaction of any other transfer conditions under the Partnership Agreement.

Any admission of a Limited Partner or former limited partner of the Legacy Offshore Vehicles into the International Feeder or the Tax-Exempt Feeder in connection with the Reorganization shall not be treated as a new admission, a transfer, or a secondary transaction requiring consent under the Partnership Agreement. For all purposes of the Partnership Agreement and the Reorganization Documents, such migrations and admissions shall be treated as part of the integrated Reorganization transaction and shall not give rise to any transfer fees, consent fees, or other charges that might otherwise be assessed in connection with transfers or admissions under the Partnership Agreement.
**Section 3.6 --- Amendment to LPAC Provisions**

The LPAC provisions of the Partnership Agreement are hereby amended to reflect that the LPAC\'s oversight and consent authority extends to matters involving the Consolidated Master Fund, the International Feeder, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder insofar as such matters affect the Partnership, the Limited Partners, or the economic terms of their investment in the Partnership.

Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP (Diana Carruthers, Partner) shall continue to serve as outside counsel to the LPAC and shall provide independent advice to the LPAC with respect to matters arising under the Consolidated Master Fund structure and the feeder vehicles.

The preliminary consent provided by the LPAC at the meeting held on April 22, 2025, at which Limited Partners holding approximately 78% in interest of the capital commitments to the Partnership voted in favor of the Reorganization, is hereby confirmed and ratified. Such consent shall be deemed to satisfy any LPAC consent requirements under the Partnership Agreement with respect to the Reorganization, including the formation of the new entities, the Step 4 Contributions, the Step 5 Dissolutions, and the related limited partner migrations.
The General Partner hereby represents and warrants to the Limited Partners as of the Effective Date as follows:

> \(b\) **Due Authorization.** The execution and delivery of this Amendment by the General Partner and the consummation of the Reorganization have been duly authorized by all necessary limited liability company action on the part of the General Partner, including the approval of the board of the General Partner obtained at a duly convened meeting held on March 14, 2025, and no further action on the part of the General Partner is required to authorize this Amendment or the Reorganization.

> \(d\) **No Violation.** The execution and delivery of this Amendment and the consummation of the Reorganization will not (i) violate any provision of the organizational documents of the General Partner, the Partnership, or any Legacy Offshore Vehicle, (ii) violate any applicable law, statute, rule, regulation, order, judgment, or decree of any governmental authority, (iii) result in a breach of, or default under, any material agreement, contract, or instrument to which the Partnership or the General Partner is a party or by which any of their respective assets are bound, or (iv) result in the creation or imposition of any lien, encumbrance, or security interest on any assets of the Partnership.

> \(f\) **Lender Consents.** The General Partner will obtain all required consents under the Partnership\'s \$1,500,000,000 Fund V subscription revolving credit facility from Ashford National Bank, N.A. (Thomas Greenleaf, Managing Director, Fund Finance) and Sentinel Capital Markets LLC (Laura Pak, Vice President) prior to the consummation of Step 4 of the Reorganization. The General Partner has no reason to believe that such consents will not be obtained on a timely basis and on terms acceptable to the General Partner.

Each Limited Partner, by executing the Form of LP Consent attached hereto as Exhibit A or otherwise consenting to this Amendment in the manner specified in the Partnership Agreement, hereby represents and warrants as of the date of such execution or consent as follows:

> \(a\) **Authority.** Such Limited Partner has the requisite power and authority (corporate, partnership, trust, or otherwise, as applicable) to execute and deliver the Form of LP Consent and to consent to this Amendment and the Reorganization, and such execution, delivery, and consent have been duly authorized by all necessary action on the part of such Limited Partner.
**Section 5.1 --- Conditions to Effectiveness of the Reorganization**

The obligations of the General Partner to consummate the Reorganization (but not the effectiveness of this Amendment itself, which shall become effective upon its execution by the General Partner and the receipt of LP consent as provided herein) are subject to the satisfaction or waiver (in accordance with Section 5.2) of the following conditions:

> \(a\) **LP Consent.** Receipt of consent to this Amendment and the Reorganization from Limited Partners holding at least the percentage in interest of capital commitments required under the Partnership Agreement for amendments and major transactions of the type contemplated hereby;

> \(c\) **Entity Classification Elections.** Filing and effectiveness of Internal Revenue Service Form 8832 entity classification elections for each of the newly formed entities, electing partnership classification under Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-3;

> \(d\) **Lender Consents.** Receipt of all required consents and waivers under the Partnership\'s \$1,500,000,000 Fund V subscription revolving credit facility from Ashford National Bank, N.A. and Sentinel Capital Markets LLC, on terms reasonably satisfactory to the General Partner;

> \(f\) **No Material Adverse Tax Law Change.** No material adverse change in applicable U.S. federal income tax law, Treasury Regulations, IRS guidance, or judicial interpretation that would materially affect the intended tax-free treatment of the Reorganization as described in Section 2.3 of this Amendment shall have occurred between the Effective Date and the consummation of the relevant Reorganization step;

The General Partner may, in its sole and absolute discretion, waive any one or more of the conditions precedent set forth in Section 5.1 at any time, except that the conditions set forth in Section 5.1(a) (LP Consent) and Section 5.1(f) (No Material Adverse Tax Law Change) may not be waived by the General Partner. Any waiver of a condition precedent by the General Partner shall not constitute a waiver of any other condition or any right of the General Partner under this Amendment or the Partnership Agreement.

Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the indemnification and exculpation provisions of the Partnership Agreement shall extend to, and shall apply with respect to, all actions taken and decisions made by the General Partner, its affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, managers, members, employees, and agents in connection with the Reorganization, including, without limitation, the negotiation, execution, and delivery of the Reorganization Documents, the formation of the new entities, the submission and prosecution of the PLR Request, the Step 4 Contributions, the Step 5 Dissolutions, and all other actions taken in furtherance of the Reorganization.

To the extent not already covered by the indemnification and exculpation provisions of the Partnership Agreement, the Partnership shall indemnify and hold harmless the General Partner and its officers, directors, managers, members, and employees, including Viktor Raines (Managing Partner and Founder), Meredith Tsao (Chief Operating Officer), Douglas Wexford (Chief Financial Officer), Priya Narasimhan (General Counsel), and Stefan Dalmqvist (Head of Tax), from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses of investigation and litigation) arising out of or relating to the Reorganization, the execution and delivery of this Amendment and the Reorganization Documents, the submission and prosecution of the PLR Request, and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby, except to the extent that such losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, or expenses are finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction (from which no further appeal may be taken) to have resulted from the General Partner\'s fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence.
**Section 7.5 --- Counterparts and Electronic Execution**

This Amendment may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which when so executed shall be deemed to be an original, and all of which taken together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Signatures to this Amendment delivered by facsimile transmission, by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf), or by any other electronic means intended to preserve the original graphic and pictorial appearance of a document shall have the same force and effect as original signatures and shall be binding upon the parties. The parties agree that this Amendment may be executed and delivered by electronic signature in accordance with the Delaware Uniform Electronic Transactions Act, 6 Del. C. § 12A-101 *et seq.*, and the federal Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act, 15 U.S.C. § 7001 *et seq.*

All notices, requests, demands, consents, and other communications required or permitted to be given under this Amendment shall be given in the manner and to the addresses specified in the Partnership Agreement for the delivery of notices. In addition, the following notice addresses shall apply for purposes of this Amendment:

Each party hereto agrees to execute and deliver such additional documents, instruments, certificates, agreements, and consents, and to take such additional actions, as may be reasonably necessary or desirable to give full effect to the Reorganization and this Amendment and to carry out the intent and purposes hereof. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, each Limited Partner agrees to execute such additional instruments as may be reasonably requested by the General Partner to facilitate the formation of the new entities, the Step 4 Contributions, the Step 5 Dissolutions, and the post-Reorganization structure.

This Amendment may be further amended, modified, or supplemented only in accordance with the procedures and requirements set forth in the Partnership Agreement for amending the Partnership Agreement, including any required approvals of the Limited Partners and the LPAC.
**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the General Partner has caused this Amendment to be executed as of the date first written above.
**LIMITED PARTNER CONSENT**

Each Limited Partner of the Partnership, by executing the Form of LP Consent attached hereto as Exhibit A or by otherwise consenting to this Amendment in the manner specified in the Partnership Agreement, hereby executes and agrees to be bound by the terms and provisions of this Amendment. The signature of each Limited Partner on the Form of LP Consent shall constitute such Limited Partner\'s execution of, and agreement to, this Amendment as if such Limited Partner had signed this Amendment directly.
The General Partner is authorized to accept the executed Forms of LP Consent and to record the consent of each Limited Partner on the books and records of the Partnership.

> 2\. Consents to the Amendment and the Reorganization described therein, including the formation of the Consolidated Master Fund and the related feeder vehicles, the Step 4 Contributions, the Step 5 Dissolutions, and the post-Reorganization structure;
