Line 13: **RE:** Summary of and Responses to LP Advisory Committee Counsel Comments on Draft Private Letter Ruling Request (Version 3.0) --- Cross-Border Fund-Platform Reorganization of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP
Line 21: This memorandum summarizes and responds to the comments received from Diana Carruthers, Partner (Fund Formation & Tax) at Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP, 200 South Biscayne Boulevard, Suite 4000, Miami, FL 33131, acting in her capacity as outside counsel to the LP Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") of Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP (\"Fund IV\") and Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP (\"Fund V\"), regarding Draft Private Letter Ruling Request Version 3.0 (the \"Draft\" or \"Draft v3.0\"). The Draft was circulated to LPAC counsel on or about July 1, 2025, with a requested comment deadline of July 15, 2025. LPAC counsel\'s comments were received by email on or about July 14, 2025, one day prior to the stated deadline.
Line 23: As discussed in prior correspondence and at the April 22, 2025 LPAC meeting, the LPAC previously provided preliminary consent, representing approximately 78% in interest of the aggregate limited partner commitments across Fund IV and Fund V, for the proposed cross-border fund-platform reorganization (the \"Reorganization\"). That preliminary consent was granted subject to the LPAC\'s right to review and comment on the draft PLR request and the related LP Tax Impact Summary Letter prior to final submission to the Internal Revenue Service.
Line 25: LPAC counsel\'s comments, which are summarized in detail in Section III below and indexed in Appendix A, focus on three principal areas of concern:
Line 33: This memorandum addresses each comment in order, sets forth Calderwood & Harkness\'s proposed response or revision to the Draft, and recommends specific changes to be incorporated into Draft PLR Request Version 4.0 (the \"Final Circulated Draft\" or \"Draft v4.0\"). In addition, this memorandum addresses certain ancillary observations and general drafting comments provided by LPAC counsel that do not fall within the three principal categories.
Line 35: **Summary of Recommendations.** Calderwood & Harkness recommends accepting or partially accepting LPAC counsel\'s suggestions on all three principal topics, with certain modifications as described herein, and proposes additional representations and factual detail in the PLR request to address LPAC concerns. Specifically:
Line 37: > • With respect to the § 731(c) analysis, we recommend expanding the factual representations regarding the absence of a secondary trading market for Master Fund interests and adding an explicit alternative-basis analysis under the § 731(c)(3)(A)(iii) exception. We accept LPAC counsel\'s suggestion in full on this point.

Reg. § 1.752-4 tiered partnership rules, and adding a representation that the five-step Reorganization constitutes an integrated transaction for § 752 netting purposes. We partially accept LPAC counsel\'s suggestion on this point.

However, we decline to include an investor-specific § 897(l) ruling request in the PLR submission. We partially accept LPAC counsel\'s suggestion on this point.
Line 43: None of the comments received from LPAC counsel raise any issue that Calderwood & Harkness believes would prevent or materially delay the PLR submission. We request client authorization to proceed with the revisions described herein and to coordinate with Bramhall & Quelwick LLP on the FIRPTA analysis, subject to appropriate privilege protocols as described in Section VI below.
Line 61: The five steps of the Reorganization are sequenced as follows, with individual steps occurring between September 15 and December 1, 2025, and a target effective date of December 1, 2025:

Line 97: As noted above, LPAC counsel\'s comments relate principally to Rulings 4, 5, and 7, with ancillary observations touching on FIRPTA (IRC § 897), which is addressed as a supporting analysis within the PLR request though not the subject of a standalone ruling request.
Line 99: **[C. LPAC Counsel Engagement]{.underline}**
Line 101: Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP serves as outside counsel to the LPAC of both Fund IV and Fund V. The firm was retained by the LPAC pursuant to the LPAC Counsel Retainer Agreement dated March 8, 2025, with fees and expenses reimbursed by the Fund as a fund-level expense under Section 7.3 of the respective limited partnership agreements. Diana Carruthers is the lead partner on the engagement and serves as the primary point of contact for all LPAC-related tax matters in connection with the Reorganization.
Line 103: LPAC counsel\'s role is to review the proposed Reorganization on behalf of the limited partners for LP consent purposes. Their comments reflect concerns raised by or on behalf of the LPAC members, including concerns that may have been communicated to LPAC counsel by individual LPs or their independent advisors. LPAC counsel\'s comments are advisory in nature and do not constitute a consent or objection to the Reorganization; the formal consent mechanism is set forth in the LP Consent Solicitation Letter and Form of LP Consent, which will be circulated following completion of Draft v4.0.
Line 105: We note an important coordination matter: Bramhall & Quelwick LLP (Jason Tremaine, Partner, International Tax; 44 Montgomery Street, Suite 3600, San Francisco, CA 94104) has been independently retained by Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund (Anders Bjørkman, Head of Alternative Investments) to evaluate the U.S. withholding tax and treaty implications of the Reorganization as they apply specifically to Nordhaven SWF. Bramhall & Quelwick was not retained by the LPAC and does not serve as LPAC counsel; however, certain of LPAC counsel\'s comments --- particularly those in Comment Category 3 (FIRPTA / IRC § 897) --- reflect input from Bramhall & Quelwick that was shared with LPAC counsel through the LPAC process. Calderwood & Harkness has been in preliminary communication with Jason Tremaine regarding coordination of the FIRPTA and treaty analysis, as discussed further in Section III.C.2 below.
Line 109: LPAC counsel\'s comments reference, or were submitted on behalf of, the following representative limited partners. For ease of reference, we list each LP, its investor type, principal contact, and commitment levels across the relevant fund vehicles:
Line 121: **[III. Summary of LPAC Counsel Comments and Calderwood & Harkness Responses]{.underline}**
Line 123: This Section III constitutes the core of this memorandum. It summarizes each of the three principal comment categories raised by LPAC counsel and sets forth Calderwood & Harkness\'s analysis and proposed response for each. A complete index of all discrete comments is provided in Appendix A.
Line 127: **A. LPAC Counsel\'s Comment**
Line 131: Specifically, LPAC counsel\'s concern has three components:
Line 133: **First**, LPAC counsel noted that IRC § 731(c)(2)(A) defines \"marketable securities\" to include \"financial instruments (as defined in section 1092(d)(1)) . . . which are, as of the date of the distribution, actively traded (within the meaning of section 1092(d)(1)).\" LPAC counsel questioned whether the Consolidated Master Fund LP interests could be viewed as \"readily tradable on a secondary market\" or \"the substantial equivalent thereof\" if such a secondary market for LP interests currently exists or were to develop in the future. LPAC counsel cited the growth of the secondary market for private fund interests generally, including platforms such as those operated by major secondary market intermediaries, as a basis for this concern. LPAC counsel noted that the Draft v3.0 analysis addresses this issue but does so in a conclusory manner without sufficient factual support.
Line 135: **Second**, LPAC counsel questioned whether the § 731(c)(3)(A)(iii) exception for certain partnership distributions of partnership interests might apply as a fallback position, independent of the primary \"not actively traded\" position. The § 731(c)(3)(A)(iii) exception provides that § 731(c) does not apply to a distribution of an interest in a partnership if, at the time of the distribution, such partnership is not an \"investment partnership\" as defined in § 731(c)(3)(C). LPAC counsel requested that Calderwood & Harkness address this exception explicitly in the PLR request as an alternative basis for nonrecognition treatment under Ruling 4, rather than relying solely on the position that the Master Fund LP interests are not \"marketable securities.\"
Line 137: **Third**, LPAC counsel noted that several LPs --- particularly Pinnacle State Employees\' Retirement System (with combined commitments of \$615 million across Fund IV and Fund V) and Grandview University Endowment (with combined commitments of \$305 million across Fund IV and Fund V) --- have expressed concern about the potential for unexpected gain recognition in Step 5. These investors originally invested through the offshore parallel structures in part to achieve UBTI blocker benefits, and any gain recognition in Step 5 would undermine those benefits by creating taxable income at the investor level in the year of the Reorganization. LPAC counsel emphasized that these investors require a high degree of confidence that the Step 5 distributions will be tax-free before they will provide final consent to the Reorganization.
Line 141: Calderwood & Harkness agrees that a robust § 731(c) analysis is essential and that Draft v3.0 adequately concludes that the Consolidated Master Fund LP interests are not \"marketable securities\" under § 731(c)(2). However, we concur with LPAC counsel that the analysis can be significantly strengthened through additional factual representations and the inclusion of an explicit fallback analysis under § 731(c)(3)(A)(iii). We address each component of LPAC counsel\'s comment below.
Line 147: We acknowledge LPAC counsel\'s observation that secondary markets for private fund interests have grown in recent years. However, the existence of intermediaries that facilitate occasional, bilateral secondary transactions in private fund interests does not, in our view, render those interests \"actively traded\" within the meaning of § 1092(d)(1). The secondary market intermediaries to which LPAC counsel alludes facilitate negotiated, privately arranged transactions on a deal-by-deal basis, typically subject to GP consent and transfer restrictions, and do not provide the continuous, readily available pricing and liquidity that characterize \"actively traded\" financial instruments. This position is consistent with the IRS\'s application of the \"actively traded\" standard in the publicly traded partnership context under IRC § 7704, where the presence of occasional secondary transfers has not been treated as creating an established securities market absent qualifying market-maker activity. See Treas. Reg. § 1.7704-1(c) (defining \"readily tradable on a secondary market or the substantial equivalent thereof\" for § 7704 purposes).
Line 155: > \(iii\) The limited partnership agreement of the Consolidated Master Fund LP will include customary transfer restrictions requiring the prior written consent of the Master Fund GP (Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC) for any transfer, assignment, or other disposition of Master Fund LP interests, and will prohibit transfers that would cause the Master Fund to be treated as a \"publicly traded partnership\" within the meaning of IRC § 7704.
Line 177: **Recommendation.** Calderwood & Harkness recommends accepting LPAC counsel\'s suggestion to expand the § 731(c) discussion in the PLR request. The proposed enhancements strengthen the ruling request without introducing any inconsistency with the existing positions in Draft v3.0, and will provide additional comfort to Pinnacle State Employees\' Retirement System, Grandview University Endowment, and other LPs that the Step 5 distributions will be tax-free.
Line 181: **A. LPAC Counsel\'s Comment**
Line 183: Diana Carruthers raised a concern regarding the impact of the Reorganization on individual LP-level liability allocations under IRC § 752. The Reorganization involves the assumption by (or allocation to) the Consolidated Master Fund LP of approximately \$1.34 billion in aggregate liabilities currently borne by the four Legacy Offshore Vehicles. LPAC counsel\'s comment has four components.
Line 185: **First**, LPAC counsel noted that under IRC § 752(b), a decrease in a partner\'s share of partnership liabilities is treated as a deemed cash distribution to that partner under IRC § 731. Conversely, under IRC § 752(a), an increase in a partner\'s share of partnership liabilities is treated as a deemed cash contribution by that partner under IRC § 722. If the deemed cash distribution under § 752(b) resulting from a decrease in a partner\'s liability share exceeds that partner\'s adjusted basis in its partnership interest, the excess is treated as gain from the sale or exchange of a partnership interest under IRC § 731(a)(1). LPAC counsel expressed concern that the Reorganization --- which involves the consolidation of four separate offshore vehicle liability pools into a single Master Fund liability pool --- could cause significant shifts in individual LP liability shares, potentially producing § 752(b) deemed distributions that exceed certain LPs\' adjusted bases.
Line 187: **Second**, LPAC counsel requested that Calderwood & Harkness prepare a detailed partner-by-partner analysis (or at minimum, a category-by-category analysis) showing the net effect of § 752(a) deemed contributions and § 752(b) deemed distributions for representative LPs. LPAC counsel specifically identified the following investors for whom the analysis was requested:
Line 197: **Third**, LPAC counsel asked Calderwood & Harkness to confirm that the netting rules under Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f) apply to treat offsetting deemed contributions and deemed distributions within the same transaction as netted, so that only the net increase or net decrease is treated as a contribution or distribution, respectively. LPAC counsel also requested an explanation of how tiered partnership liability allocations work for LPs who will hold their Master Fund interests through the Cayman feeder vehicles --- i.e., the limited partners of the International Feeder and the Tax-Exempt Feeder --- where the liability allocation must be traced through two tiers (the feeder level and the Master Fund level).
Line 199: **Fourth**, LPAC counsel expressed particular concern regarding the five-step sequencing of the Reorganization. Steps 2 through 5 are currently scheduled to occur over approximately two months (October 1 through December 1, 2025), and LPAC counsel questioned whether the IRS might view each step as a separate transaction for § 752 purposes rather than as part of a single integrated transaction. If the steps are treated separately, transient liability allocation shifts occurring between steps (e.g., after the Step 2 contribution by Fund IV-A Cayman on October 1 but before the Step 4 contribution by Fund V-A Cayman on November 1) could produce temporary § 752(b) deemed distributions that are not offset by corresponding § 752(a) deemed contributions until a subsequent step. This could result in gain recognition at the individual LP level during the interim period, even if the net effect of the entire Reorganization would not produce gain recognition.
Line 203: Calderwood & Harkness acknowledges that the § 752 analysis is among the most complex aspects of the Reorganization and that the Draft v3.0 analysis, which addresses the liability shifts at the aggregate level, is sound but can benefit from additional granularity. We address each component of LPAC counsel\'s comment below.
Line 213: LPAC counsel requested a partner-by-partner analysis showing the net § 752 effect for each representative LP. While we understand the motivation for this request, we note that a partner-by-partner analysis requires access to each individual LP\'s adjusted basis in its partnership interest --- information that is not within Calderwood & Harkness\'s possession and that each LP maintains independently based on its own tax reporting and capital account records. The PLR request, which addresses the structural tax treatment of the Reorganization at the entity level, does not and should not opine on whether any individual LP will recognize gain, as this is inherently a fact-specific determination that depends on each LP\'s own adjusted basis.
Line 237: We will request that the IRS confirm in its ruling on Ruling 5 that Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f) netting applies across all five steps, viewed as a single integrated transaction, so that transient liability allocation shifts occurring between individual steps do not produce unintended gain recognition. This is a critical point, as it directly addresses LPAC counsel\'s concern about the two-month sequencing period from October 1 to December 1, 2025.
Line 255: **Recommendation.** Calderwood & Harkness recommends partially accepting LPAC counsel\'s suggestion. We will provide a category-level analysis with appropriate caveats, rather than a partner-by-partner analysis that would require individual LP basis information outside our possession and that falls outside the proper scope of the PLR request. This approach balances LPAC counsel\'s legitimate interest in additional granularity with the practical and structural constraints of the PLR process.
Line 259: **A. LPAC Counsel\'s Comment**
Line 261: Diana Carruthers raised a concern on behalf of the LPAC, specifically reflecting input from Bramhall & Quelwick LLP (Jason Tremaine, Partner, International Tax), regarding the FIRPTA (Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act) / IRC § 897 implications of the Reorganization for non-U.S. investors. The comment has three principal components.
Line 263: **First**, the concern centers on whether certain portfolio company interests held by the Legacy Offshore Vehicles --- particularly interests in NovaBright Data Systems Inc. and Thorngate Fiber Networks LP --- constitute \"United States real property interests\" (USRPIs) under IRC § 897(c)(1)(A)(i). LPAC counsel observed that data centers and fiber-optic network infrastructure may include significant interests in U.S. real property, including owned or leased land and buildings (in the case of data centers) and easements, rights-of-way, and physical conduit infrastructure (in the case of fiber-optic networks). If these portfolio company interests are USRPIs, the contributions of such interests to the Consolidated Master Fund LP in Steps 2 through 4 could potentially trigger FIRPTA gain recognition for non-U.S. partners of the contributing Legacy Offshore Vehicles.
Line 265: LPAC counsel provided the following specific data points in support of this concern:
Line 271: **Second**, if any transferred portfolio company interests are USRPIs, the § 1446 withholding analysis addressed in Ruling 7 would need to account for FIRPTA withholding under IRC § 1446(f) on transfers of partnership interests. Section 1446(f) imposes a 10% withholding obligation on the transferee of a partnership interest if any portion of the gain on the transfer would be treated as effectively connected income (\"ECI\") under § 864(c)(8) by reason of the partnership\'s holding of USRPIs. LPAC counsel questioned whether the nonrecognition treatment under § 721(a) eliminates the § 1446(f) withholding obligation, or whether a withholding obligation nevertheless arises that must be specifically excepted.
Line 273: **Third**, LPAC counsel requested that Calderwood & Harkness address whether Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund qualifies for the sovereign wealth fund FIRPTA exemption under IRC § 897(l). Section 897(l), added by the Protecting Americans from Tax Hikes (PATH) Act of 2015, exempts \"qualified foreign pension funds\" and their wholly owned subsidiaries from the application of § 897. If Nordhaven SWF qualifies as a \"qualified foreign pension fund\" within the meaning of § 897(l)(2), it would be exempt from FIRPTA regardless of whether the portfolio company interests constitute USRPIs. LPAC counsel requested that, if applicable, representations regarding Nordhaven SWF\'s § 897(l) eligibility be included in the PLR request to provide additional comfort. LPAC counsel noted that this request reflects input from Bramhall & Quelwick LLP, which intends to provide a separate opinion letter to Nordhaven SWF on the § 897(l) issue and has requested coordination between Calderwood & Harkness and Bramhall & Quelwick on the FIRPTA and § 1446 positions.
Line 277: Calderwood & Harkness acknowledges the importance of the FIRPTA analysis for non-U.S. investors and agrees that the Draft v3.0 FIRPTA discussion, which addresses FIRPTA at a relatively high level of generality, can and should be expanded. We address each component of LPAC counsel\'s comment below.
Line 307: With respect to LPAC counsel\'s question regarding IRC § 1446(f) withholding, Calderwood & Harkness\'s position is that § 1446(f) withholding does not apply to the Steps 2 through 4 contributions or the Step 5 distributions because these are nonrecognition transactions that do not generate gain. Section 1446(f) imposes a withholding obligation on the \"transferee\" of a partnership interest if any portion of the gain on the transfer would be treated as ECI under § 864(c)(8). If there is no gain by reason of § 721(a) or § 731(a), there is no ECI, and no withholding obligation arises. This conclusion is further supported by the temporary and proposed regulations under § 1446(f), which provide exceptions for certain nonrecognition transactions. See Treas. Reg. § 1.1446(f)-2(b) (providing rules for determining the amount subject to withholding, which is based on the amount realized less the transferor\'s adjusted basis --- resulting in zero withholding when no gain is recognized).
Line 327: Moreover, even if Nordhaven SWF does qualify as a QFPF under § 897(l), we do not believe it is appropriate to include a § 897(l) ruling request in the PLR submission for the Reorganization. The PLR request addresses the structural tax treatment of the Reorganization at the entity and transaction level --- it is not designed to opine on the individual tax attributes or exemptions applicable to any single limited partner. Including a § 897(l) ruling request for Nordhaven SWF would fundamentally change the character of the PLR from a structural ruling request to an investor-specific ruling request, which could complicate the IRS review process and potentially delay the ruling.
Line 339: Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Jason Tremaine at Bramhall & Quelwick LLP on the FIRPTA and § 1446 positions, sharing the relevant portions of the PLR analysis (subject to client consent from Solara Digital Infrastructure LP and appropriate privilege protocols) to ensure consistency between the PLR request and Bramhall & Quelwick\'s opinion to Nordhaven SWF. Leonard Cross has already initiated this coordination through email correspondence with Jason Tremaine dated June 28 and July 3, 2025, regarding the Nordhaven SWF treaty analysis and the interplay between the U.S.-Nordhaven income tax treaty and the FIRPTA provisions.
Line 341: We note that the privilege protocol for sharing work product between Calderwood & Harkness (as fund counsel) and Bramhall & Quelwick (as Nordhaven SWF\'s independent counsel) requires the prior consent of both clients --- Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (through Priya Narasimhan, General Counsel) and Nordhaven SWF (through Anders Bjørkman, Head of Alternative Investments). We recommend that the client provide such consent promptly to enable efficient coordination. A common interest agreement may be appropriate depending on the scope of the information sharing; we can prepare a draft common interest agreement for the client\'s review if requested.
Line 355: **Recommendation.** Calderwood & Harkness recommends partially accepting LPAC counsel\'s suggestion. We will expand the structural FIRPTA analysis and the § 897(e) discussion in the PLR request, and will coordinate with Bramhall & Quelwick on the Nordhaven SWF-specific analysis. However, we decline to include an investor-specific § 897(l) analysis or ruling request in the PLR submission, as this falls outside the appropriate scope of the structural ruling request and is more properly addressed by Nordhaven SWF\'s independent counsel.
Line 357: **[IV. Additional LPAC Counsel Observations]{.underline}**
Line 359: In addition to the three principal comment categories addressed in Section III above, LPAC counsel provided several ancillary observations and recommendations that we address briefly in this Section IV.

matches.line: **RE:** Summary of and Responses to LP Advisory Committee Counsel Comments on Draft Private Letter Ruling Request (Version 3.0) --- Cross-Border Fund-Platform Reorganization of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP

This memorandum summarizes and responds to the comments received from Diana Carruthers, Partner (Fund Formation & Tax) at Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP, 200 South Biscayne Boulevard, Suite 4000, Miami, FL 33131, acting in her capacity as outside counsel to the LP Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") of Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP (\"Fund IV\") and Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP (\"Fund V\"), regarding Draft Private Letter Ruling Request Version 3.0 (the \"Draft\" or \"Draft v3.0\"). The Draft was circulated to LPAC counsel on or about July 1, 2025, with a requested comment deadline of July 15, 2025. LPAC counsel\'s comments were received by email on or about July 14, 2025, one day prior to the stated deadline.

As discussed in prior correspondence and at the April 22, 2025 LPAC meeting, the LPAC previously provided preliminary consent, representing approximately 78% in interest of the aggregate limited partner commitments across Fund IV and Fund V, for the proposed cross-border fund-platform reorganization (the \"Reorganization\"). That preliminary consent was granted subject to the LPAC\'s right to review and comment on the draft PLR request and the related LP Tax Impact Summary Letter prior to final submission to the Internal Revenue Service.
LPAC counsel\'s comments, which are summarized in detail in Section III below and indexed in Appendix A, focus on three principal areas of concern:

This memorandum addresses each comment in order, sets forth Calderwood & Harkness\'s proposed response or revision to the Draft, and recommends specific changes to be incorporated into Draft PLR Request Version 4.0 (the \"Final Circulated Draft\" or \"Draft v4.0\"). In addition, this memorandum addresses certain ancillary observations and general drafting comments provided by LPAC counsel that do not fall within the three principal categories.

**Summary of Recommendations.** Calderwood & Harkness recommends accepting or partially accepting LPAC counsel\'s suggestions on all three principal topics, with certain modifications as described herein, and proposes additional representations and factual detail in the PLR request to address LPAC concerns. Specifically:

> • With respect to the § 731(c) analysis, we recommend expanding the factual representations regarding the absence of a secondary trading market for Master Fund interests and adding an explicit alternative-basis analysis under the § 731(c)(3)(A)(iii) exception. We accept LPAC counsel\'s suggestion in full on this point.

> • With respect to the § 752 analysis, we recommend providing a category-level (rather than individual partner-level) impact analysis supplementing PLR Exhibit E, expanding the discussion of the Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f) netting rules and the Treas. Reg. § 1.752-4 tiered partnership rules, and adding a representation that the five-step Reorganization constitutes an integrated transaction for § 752 netting purposes. We partially accept LPAC counsel\'s suggestion on this point.

> • With respect to the FIRPTA / § 897 analysis, we recommend expanding the structural FIRPTA analysis to specifically address the USRPI characterization of NovaBright and Thorngate, adding a detailed § 897(e) nonrecognition analysis, and coordinating with Bramhall & Quelwick LLP on the Nordhaven SWF-specific analysis. However, we decline to include an investor-specific § 897(l) ruling request in the PLR submission. We partially accept LPAC counsel\'s suggestion on this point.

None of the comments received from LPAC counsel raise any issue that Calderwood & Harkness believes would prevent or materially delay the PLR submission. We request client authorization to proceed with the revisions described herein and to coordinate with Bramhall & Quelwick LLP on the FIRPTA analysis, subject to appropriate privilege protocols as described in Section VI below.
The five steps of the Reorganization are sequenced as follows, with individual steps occurring between September 15 and December 1, 2025, and a target effective date of December 1, 2025:

> **Ruling 7 --- IRC § 1446 Withholding Not Required.** That the contributions in Steps 2 through 4 and the distributions in Step 5 do not give rise to withholding obligations under IRC § 1446(a) (withholding on effectively connected income allocated to foreign partners) or IRC § 1446(f) (withholding on transfers of partnership interests), because the underlying transactions are nonrecognition transactions that do not generate effectively connected taxable income or gain.

As noted above, LPAC counsel\'s comments relate principally to Rulings 4, 5, and 7, with ancillary observations touching on FIRPTA (IRC § 897), which is addressed as a supporting analysis within the PLR request though not the subject of a standalone ruling request.
**[C. LPAC Counsel Engagement]{.underline}**

Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP serves as outside counsel to the LPAC of both Fund IV and Fund V. The firm was retained by the LPAC pursuant to the LPAC Counsel Retainer Agreement dated March 8, 2025, with fees and expenses reimbursed by the Fund as a fund-level expense under Section 7.3 of the respective limited partnership agreements. Diana Carruthers is the lead partner on the engagement and serves as the primary point of contact for all LPAC-related tax matters in connection with the Reorganization.

LPAC counsel\'s role is to review the proposed Reorganization on behalf of the limited partners for LP consent purposes. Their comments reflect concerns raised by or on behalf of the LPAC members, including concerns that may have been communicated to LPAC counsel by individual LPs or their independent advisors. LPAC counsel\'s comments are advisory in nature and do not constitute a consent or objection to the Reorganization; the formal consent mechanism is set forth in the LP Consent Solicitation Letter and Form of LP Consent, which will be circulated following completion of Draft v4.0.

We note an important coordination matter: Bramhall & Quelwick LLP (Jason Tremaine, Partner, International Tax; 44 Montgomery Street, Suite 3600, San Francisco, CA 94104) has been independently retained by Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund (Anders Bjørkman, Head of Alternative Investments) to evaluate the U.S. withholding tax and treaty implications of the Reorganization as they apply specifically to Nordhaven SWF. Bramhall & Quelwick was not retained by the LPAC and does not serve as LPAC counsel; however, certain of LPAC counsel\'s comments --- particularly those in Comment Category 3 (FIRPTA / IRC § 897) --- reflect input from Bramhall & Quelwick that was shared with LPAC counsel through the LPAC process. Calderwood & Harkness has been in preliminary communication with Jason Tremaine regarding coordination of the FIRPTA and treaty analysis, as discussed further in Section III.C.2 below.

LPAC counsel\'s comments reference, or were submitted on behalf of, the following representative limited partners. For ease of reference, we list each LP, its investor type, principal contact, and commitment levels across the relevant fund vehicles:
**[III. Summary of LPAC Counsel Comments and Calderwood & Harkness Responses]{.underline}**

This Section III constitutes the core of this memorandum. It summarizes each of the three principal comment categories raised by LPAC counsel and sets forth Calderwood & Harkness\'s analysis and proposed response for each. A complete index of all discrete comments is provided in Appendix A.
**A. LPAC Counsel\'s Comment**
Specifically, LPAC counsel\'s concern has three components:

**First**, LPAC counsel noted that IRC § 731(c)(2)(A) defines \"marketable securities\" to include \"financial instruments (as defined in section 1092(d)(1)) . . . which are, as of the date of the distribution, actively traded (within the meaning of section 1092(d)(1)).\" LPAC counsel questioned whether the Consolidated Master Fund LP interests could be viewed as \"readily tradable on a secondary market\" or \"the substantial equivalent thereof\" if such a secondary market for LP interests currently exists or were to develop in the future. LPAC counsel cited the growth of the secondary market for private fund interests generally, including platforms such as those operated by major secondary market intermediaries, as a basis for this concern. LPAC counsel noted that the Draft v3.0 analysis addresses this issue but does so in a conclusory manner without sufficient factual support.

**Second**, LPAC counsel questioned whether the § 731(c)(3)(A)(iii) exception for certain partnership distributions of partnership interests might apply as a fallback position, independent of the primary \"not actively traded\" position. The § 731(c)(3)(A)(iii) exception provides that § 731(c) does not apply to a distribution of an interest in a partnership if, at the time of the distribution, such partnership is not an \"investment partnership\" as defined in § 731(c)(3)(C). LPAC counsel requested that Calderwood & Harkness address this exception explicitly in the PLR request as an alternative basis for nonrecognition treatment under Ruling 4, rather than relying solely on the position that the Master Fund LP interests are not \"marketable securities.\"

**Third**, LPAC counsel noted that several LPs --- particularly Pinnacle State Employees\' Retirement System (with combined commitments of \$615 million across Fund IV and Fund V) and Grandview University Endowment (with combined commitments of \$305 million across Fund IV and Fund V) --- have expressed concern about the potential for unexpected gain recognition in Step 5. These investors originally invested through the offshore parallel structures in part to achieve UBTI blocker benefits, and any gain recognition in Step 5 would undermine those benefits by creating taxable income at the investor level in the year of the Reorganization. LPAC counsel emphasized that these investors require a high degree of confidence that the Step 5 distributions will be tax-free before they will provide final consent to the Reorganization.

Calderwood & Harkness agrees that a robust § 731(c) analysis is essential and that Draft v3.0 adequately concludes that the Consolidated Master Fund LP interests are not \"marketable securities\" under § 731(c)(2). However, we concur with LPAC counsel that the analysis can be significantly strengthened through additional factual representations and the inclusion of an explicit fallback analysis under § 731(c)(3)(A)(iii). We address each component of LPAC counsel\'s comment below.

We acknowledge LPAC counsel\'s observation that secondary markets for private fund interests have grown in recent years. However, the existence of intermediaries that facilitate occasional, bilateral secondary transactions in private fund interests does not, in our view, render those interests \"actively traded\" within the meaning of § 1092(d)(1). The secondary market intermediaries to which LPAC counsel alludes facilitate negotiated, privately arranged transactions on a deal-by-deal basis, typically subject to GP consent and transfer restrictions, and do not provide the continuous, readily available pricing and liquidity that characterize \"actively traded\" financial instruments. This position is consistent with the IRS\'s application of the \"actively traded\" standard in the publicly traded partnership context under IRC § 7704, where the presence of occasional secondary transfers has not been treated as creating an established securities market absent qualifying market-maker activity. See Treas. Reg. § 1.7704-1(c) (defining \"readily tradable on a secondary market or the substantial equivalent thereof\" for § 7704 purposes).

> \(iii\) The limited partnership agreement of the Consolidated Master Fund LP will include customary transfer restrictions requiring the prior written consent of the Master Fund GP (Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC) for any transfer, assignment, or other disposition of Master Fund LP interests, and will prohibit transfers that would cause the Master Fund to be treated as a \"publicly traded partnership\" within the meaning of IRC § 7704.

**Recommendation.** Calderwood & Harkness recommends accepting LPAC counsel\'s suggestion to expand the § 731(c) discussion in the PLR request. The proposed enhancements strengthen the ruling request without introducing any inconsistency with the existing positions in Draft v3.0, and will provide additional comfort to Pinnacle State Employees\' Retirement System, Grandview University Endowment, and other LPs that the Step 5 distributions will be tax-free.
**A. LPAC Counsel\'s Comment**

Diana Carruthers raised a concern regarding the impact of the Reorganization on individual LP-level liability allocations under IRC § 752. The Reorganization involves the assumption by (or allocation to) the Consolidated Master Fund LP of approximately \$1.34 billion in aggregate liabilities currently borne by the four Legacy Offshore Vehicles. LPAC counsel\'s comment has four components.

**First**, LPAC counsel noted that under IRC § 752(b), a decrease in a partner\'s share of partnership liabilities is treated as a deemed cash distribution to that partner under IRC § 731. Conversely, under IRC § 752(a), an increase in a partner\'s share of partnership liabilities is treated as a deemed cash contribution by that partner under IRC § 722. If the deemed cash distribution under § 752(b) resulting from a decrease in a partner\'s liability share exceeds that partner\'s adjusted basis in its partnership interest, the excess is treated as gain from the sale or exchange of a partnership interest under IRC § 731(a)(1). LPAC counsel expressed concern that the Reorganization --- which involves the consolidation of four separate offshore vehicle liability pools into a single Master Fund liability pool --- could cause significant shifts in individual LP liability shares, potentially producing § 752(b) deemed distributions that exceed certain LPs\' adjusted bases.

**Second**, LPAC counsel requested that Calderwood & Harkness prepare a detailed partner-by-partner analysis (or at minimum, a category-by-category analysis) showing the net effect of § 752(a) deemed contributions and § 752(b) deemed distributions for representative LPs. LPAC counsel specifically identified the following investors for whom the analysis was requested:

**Third**, LPAC counsel asked Calderwood & Harkness to confirm that the netting rules under Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f) apply to treat offsetting deemed contributions and deemed distributions within the same transaction as netted, so that only the net increase or net decrease is treated as a contribution or distribution, respectively. LPAC counsel also requested an explanation of how tiered partnership liability allocations work for LPs who will hold their Master Fund interests through the Cayman feeder vehicles --- i.e., the limited partners of the International Feeder and the Tax-Exempt Feeder --- where the liability allocation must be traced through two tiers (the feeder level and the Master Fund level).

**Fourth**, LPAC counsel expressed particular concern regarding the five-step sequencing of the Reorganization. Steps 2 through 5 are currently scheduled to occur over approximately two months (October 1 through December 1, 2025), and LPAC counsel questioned whether the IRS might view each step as a separate transaction for § 752 purposes rather than as part of a single integrated transaction. If the steps are treated separately, transient liability allocation shifts occurring between steps (e.g., after the Step 2 contribution by Fund IV-A Cayman on October 1 but before the Step 4 contribution by Fund V-A Cayman on November 1) could produce temporary § 752(b) deemed distributions that are not offset by corresponding § 752(a) deemed contributions until a subsequent step. This could result in gain recognition at the individual LP level during the interim period, even if the net effect of the entire Reorganization would not produce gain recognition.

Calderwood & Harkness acknowledges that the § 752 analysis is among the most complex aspects of the Reorganization and that the Draft v3.0 analysis, which addresses the liability shifts at the aggregate level, is sound but can benefit from additional granularity. We address each component of LPAC counsel\'s comment below.

LPAC counsel requested a partner-by-partner analysis showing the net § 752 effect for each representative LP. While we understand the motivation for this request, we note that a partner-by-partner analysis requires access to each individual LP\'s adjusted basis in its partnership interest --- information that is not within Calderwood & Harkness\'s possession and that each LP maintains independently based on its own tax reporting and capital account records. The PLR request, which addresses the structural tax treatment of the Reorganization at the entity level, does not and should not opine on whether any individual LP will recognize gain, as this is inherently a fact-specific determination that depends on each LP\'s own adjusted basis.

We will request that the IRS confirm in its ruling on Ruling 5 that Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f) netting applies across all five steps, viewed as a single integrated transaction, so that transient liability allocation shifts occurring between individual steps do not produce unintended gain recognition. This is a critical point, as it directly addresses LPAC counsel\'s concern about the two-month sequencing period from October 1 to December 1, 2025.

**Recommendation.** Calderwood & Harkness recommends partially accepting LPAC counsel\'s suggestion. We will provide a category-level analysis with appropriate caveats, rather than a partner-by-partner analysis that would require individual LP basis information outside our possession and that falls outside the proper scope of the PLR request. This approach balances LPAC counsel\'s legitimate interest in additional granularity with the practical and structural constraints of the PLR process.
**A. LPAC Counsel\'s Comment**

Diana Carruthers raised a concern on behalf of the LPAC, specifically reflecting input from Bramhall & Quelwick LLP (Jason Tremaine, Partner, International Tax), regarding the FIRPTA (Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act) / IRC § 897 implications of the Reorganization for non-U.S. investors. The comment has three principal components.

**First**, the concern centers on whether certain portfolio company interests held by the Legacy Offshore Vehicles --- particularly interests in NovaBright Data Systems Inc. and Thorngate Fiber Networks LP --- constitute \"United States real property interests\" (USRPIs) under IRC § 897(c)(1)(A)(i). LPAC counsel observed that data centers and fiber-optic network infrastructure may include significant interests in U.S. real property, including owned or leased land and buildings (in the case of data centers) and easements, rights-of-way, and physical conduit infrastructure (in the case of fiber-optic networks). If these portfolio company interests are USRPIs, the contributions of such interests to the Consolidated Master Fund LP in Steps 2 through 4 could potentially trigger FIRPTA gain recognition for non-U.S. partners of the contributing Legacy Offshore Vehicles.
LPAC counsel provided the following specific data points in support of this concern:

**Second**, if any transferred portfolio company interests are USRPIs, the § 1446 withholding analysis addressed in Ruling 7 would need to account for FIRPTA withholding under IRC § 1446(f) on transfers of partnership interests. Section 1446(f) imposes a 10% withholding obligation on the transferee of a partnership interest if any portion of the gain on the transfer would be treated as effectively connected income (\"ECI\") under § 864(c)(8) by reason of the partnership\'s holding of USRPIs. LPAC counsel questioned whether the nonrecognition treatment under § 721(a) eliminates the § 1446(f) withholding obligation, or whether a withholding obligation nevertheless arises that must be specifically excepted.

**Third**, LPAC counsel requested that Calderwood & Harkness address whether Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund qualifies for the sovereign wealth fund FIRPTA exemption under IRC § 897(l). Section 897(l), added by the Protecting Americans from Tax Hikes (PATH) Act of 2015, exempts \"qualified foreign pension funds\" and their wholly owned subsidiaries from the application of § 897. If Nordhaven SWF qualifies as a \"qualified foreign pension fund\" within the meaning of § 897(l)(2), it would be exempt from FIRPTA regardless of whether the portfolio company interests constitute USRPIs. LPAC counsel requested that, if applicable, representations regarding Nordhaven SWF\'s § 897(l) eligibility be included in the PLR request to provide additional comfort. LPAC counsel noted that this request reflects input from Bramhall & Quelwick LLP, which intends to provide a separate opinion letter to Nordhaven SWF on the § 897(l) issue and has requested coordination between Calderwood & Harkness and Bramhall & Quelwick on the FIRPTA and § 1446 positions.

Calderwood & Harkness acknowledges the importance of the FIRPTA analysis for non-U.S. investors and agrees that the Draft v3.0 FIRPTA discussion, which addresses FIRPTA at a relatively high level of generality, can and should be expanded. We address each component of LPAC counsel\'s comment below.

With respect to LPAC counsel\'s question regarding IRC § 1446(f) withholding, Calderwood & Harkness\'s position is that § 1446(f) withholding does not apply to the Steps 2 through 4 contributions or the Step 5 distributions because these are nonrecognition transactions that do not generate gain. Section 1446(f) imposes a withholding obligation on the \"transferee\" of a partnership interest if any portion of the gain on the transfer would be treated as ECI under § 864(c)(8). If there is no gain by reason of § 721(a) or § 731(a), there is no ECI, and no withholding obligation arises. This conclusion is further supported by the temporary and proposed regulations under § 1446(f), which provide exceptions for certain nonrecognition transactions. See Treas. Reg. § 1.1446(f)-2(b) (providing rules for determining the amount subject to withholding, which is based on the amount realized less the transferor\'s adjusted basis --- resulting in zero withholding when no gain is recognized).

Moreover, even if Nordhaven SWF does qualify as a QFPF under § 897(l), we do not believe it is appropriate to include a § 897(l) ruling request in the PLR submission for the Reorganization. The PLR request addresses the structural tax treatment of the Reorganization at the entity and transaction level --- it is not designed to opine on the individual tax attributes or exemptions applicable to any single limited partner. Including a § 897(l) ruling request for Nordhaven SWF would fundamentally change the character of the PLR from a structural ruling request to an investor-specific ruling request, which could complicate the IRS review process and potentially delay the ruling.

Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Jason Tremaine at Bramhall & Quelwick LLP on the FIRPTA and § 1446 positions, sharing the relevant portions of the PLR analysis (subject to client consent from Solara Digital Infrastructure LP and appropriate privilege protocols) to ensure consistency between the PLR request and Bramhall & Quelwick\'s opinion to Nordhaven SWF. Leonard Cross has already initiated this coordination through email correspondence with Jason Tremaine dated June 28 and July 3, 2025, regarding the Nordhaven SWF treaty analysis and the interplay between the U.S.-Nordhaven income tax treaty and the FIRPTA provisions.

We note that the privilege protocol for sharing work product between Calderwood & Harkness (as fund counsel) and Bramhall & Quelwick (as Nordhaven SWF\'s independent counsel) requires the prior consent of both clients --- Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (through Priya Narasimhan, General Counsel) and Nordhaven SWF (through Anders Bjørkman, Head of Alternative Investments). We recommend that the client provide such consent promptly to enable efficient coordination. A common interest agreement may be appropriate depending on the scope of the information sharing; we can prepare a draft common interest agreement for the client\'s review if requested.

**Recommendation.** Calderwood & Harkness recommends partially accepting LPAC counsel\'s suggestion. We will expand the structural FIRPTA analysis and the § 897(e) discussion in the PLR request, and will coordinate with Bramhall & Quelwick on the Nordhaven SWF-specific analysis. However, we decline to include an investor-specific § 897(l) analysis or ruling request in the PLR submission, as this falls outside the appropriate scope of the structural ruling request and is more properly addressed by Nordhaven SWF\'s independent counsel.
**[IV. Additional LPAC Counsel Observations]{.underline}**

In addition to the three principal comment categories addressed in Section III above, LPAC counsel provided several ancillary observations and recommendations that we address briefly in this Section IV.

LPAC counsel provided several minor drafting comments on PLR Draft v3.0 that do not raise substantive tax issues but reflect constructive suggestions for improving the clarity and internal consistency of the PLR request. These include:

> • Requests for clarification of certain defined terms, including the definition of \"Legacy Offshore Vehicles\" (which LPAC counsel suggested should expressly list all four vehicles rather than relying on a cross-reference to the recitals), the definition of \"Reorganization\" (which LPAC counsel suggested should be expanded to encompass all five steps rather than being limited to Steps 2 through 5 as currently drafted), and the definition of \"Affiliated Entities\" (which LPAC counsel noted is used in several sections but is not defined in the glossary).

> • Minor factual corrections regarding investor commitment amounts that LPAC counsel cross-checked against fund subscription documents. Specifically, LPAC counsel noted a discrepancy in the stated commitment amount for Kestrel Pacific Insurance Group in Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp: the Draft states €270 million, while the subscription documents reflect €275 million. LPAC counsel also noted that the aggregate commitment figures in PLR Exhibit B (Schedule of LP Commitments) do not sum correctly due to what appears to be a rounding error in the conversion of Euro-denominated commitments to U.S. dollar equivalents.

LPAC counsel recommended that Calderwood & Harkness prepare a plain-language LP Tax Impact Summary Letter for distribution to all limited partners, separate from the PLR request itself, describing the anticipated U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Reorganization for each investor category. LPAC counsel specifically suggested that the LP Tax Impact Summary Letter address:

Calderwood & Harkness agrees that preparation of an LP Tax Impact Summary Letter is a best practice in the context of a complex fund-platform reorganization of this nature, and we have already planned this deliverable as part of the engagement work plan (see Engagement Work Plan, Item 6, dated May 27, 2025). The LP Tax Impact Summary Letter will be drafted to be accessible to a sophisticated but non-specialist audience (e.g., CIOs, directors of investments, and in-house counsel at LP institutions) and will include appropriate disclaimers as recommended by LPAC counsel. We anticipate that the LP Tax Impact Summary Letter will be circulated to all limited partners concurrently with, or shortly after, the LP Consent Solicitation Letter and Form of LP Consent.
**[C. Timing of PLR Submission Relative to LP Consent]{.underline}**

LPAC counsel raised an important process-related question regarding the sequencing of the PLR submission and the LP consent process. Specifically, LPAC counsel noted that some limited partners may wish to condition their consent to the Reorganization on the IRS issuing a favorable ruling on all eight requested rulings, and asked Calderwood & Harkness to address in the consent solicitation materials how the Reorganization will proceed if the IRS declines to rule on one or more of the eight requests or issues an adverse ruling.

This is a legitimate concern. The PLR process is inherently uncertain --- the IRS may decline to rule on any or all of the requested rulings, may issue a ruling that is less favorable than requested, or may request additional information or representations that materially alter the terms of the ruling. Moreover, the timeline for IRS review of PLR requests in the international tax area is unpredictable, and there is no guarantee that a ruling will be issued prior to the target Step 2 execution date of October 1, 2025.

Calderwood & Harkness recommends that the LP Consent Solicitation Letter and Form of LP Consent include a **\"conditional consent\" mechanism** that addresses these contingencies. Specifically, we recommend the following approach:

> \(i\) The Form of LP Consent will provide that each LP\'s consent is conditioned on the IRS issuing a favorable ruling on the \"material ruling requests\" --- defined as Rulings 1 (§ 721(a) tax-free contributions), 3 (§ 367 inapplicability), 4 (§ 731(a) tax-free distributions), and 5 (§ 752 liability shifting) --- prior to the target Step 2 execution date of October 1, 2025.

> \(ii\) If the IRS does not issue a favorable ruling on all four material ruling requests by October 1, 2025, the GP (Viktor Raines, Managing Partner, Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC) will have the right, but not the obligation, to either (A) extend the target execution date by up to 90 days (to January 1, 2026) to allow additional time for IRS review, or (B) terminate the Reorganization without LP liability.

> \(iii\) Rulings 2 (§ 721(b) investment company exception), 6 (§ 704(c) carryover), 7 (§ 1446 withholding), and 8 (entity classification) are considered supportive but not material to the LP consent condition, on the basis that Calderwood & Harkness has a high degree of confidence in the positions underlying these rulings and can proceed on the basis of a reasoned tax opinion if the IRS declines to rule on these specific points.

> \(iv\) If the IRS issues an adverse ruling on any of the four material ruling requests, the GP will terminate the Reorganization unless the LPAC, by vote of LPs holding at least 66⅔% in interest, affirmatively consents to proceed notwithstanding the adverse ruling.

This approach preserves the 78% in interest preliminary consent threshold achieved at the April 22, 2025 LPAC meeting while providing LP protection against adverse tax outcomes. Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the LP Consent Solicitation Letter and Form of LP Consent incorporating this conditional consent mechanism and will circulate drafts to the client and LPAC counsel for review.

Calderwood & Harkness will monitor the status of the PLR request following submission and provide regular updates to the client and LPAC counsel.

matches.line: **[FORM OF CONSENT OF LIMITED PARTNER]{.underline}**
**Consent to Cross-Border Fund-Platform Reorganization and Related Amendments to Limited Partnership Agreements**

This Form of Consent of Limited Partner (this \"Consent\") is delivered by the undersigned limited partner (the \"Consenting LP\") in connection with the proposed cross-border fund-platform reorganization (the \"Reorganization\") of the fund vehicles sponsored by Solara Digital Infrastructure LP, a Delaware limited partnership (\"Solara\" or \"SDILP\"), with its principal offices at 1200 Market Street, Suite 3400, Wilmington, DE 19801. The Reorganization is being undertaken by Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (\"Solara GP\" or the \"General Partner\"), in its capacity as general partner of the applicable fund vehicles described herein.

This Consent is delivered in response to, and should be read in conjunction with, the LP Consent Solicitation Letter dated \[**\_***\_*\], 2025 (the \"Solicitation Letter\") transmitted by the General Partner to all limited partners of the applicable fund vehicles. The Solicitation Letter was prepared with the assistance of Calderwood & Harkness LLP, U.S. tax counsel to Solara, and describes in detail the structure, rationale, anticipated timeline, and tax consequences of the Reorganization. The Consenting LP further acknowledges receipt of the LP Tax Impact Summary Letter accompanying the Solicitation Letter, which sets forth the anticipated U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Reorganization for each category of investor (U.S. taxable, U.S. tax-exempt, and non-U.S.). Reference is also made to the LPAC Presentation --- Reorganization Overview presented at the April 22, 2025 meeting of the LP Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\"), at which preliminary consent of 78% in interest was obtained from attending LPAC members.
**[Section 1: Identification of Consenting LP]{.underline}**
The Consenting LP shall complete the following information in its entirety. All fields are required unless otherwise indicated.
**Full Legal Name of Consenting LP:**

See Exhibit B for definitions of each investor category. The Consenting LP\'s investor category will determine the post-Reorganization fund vehicle into which the Consenting LP\'s interest will migrate.

The Consenting LP should check each fund vehicle in which it holds a limited partnership interest and state its capital commitment in the appropriate column. If the Consenting LP holds interests in more than one fund vehicle, each applicable fund vehicle should be identified separately below.

**Note:** For purposes of the Reorganization, a EUR/USD exchange rate of 1.08 is being applied uniformly to all EUR-denominated amounts. This exchange rate is based on the three-month trailing average as of March 31, 2025, as agreed upon by the General Partner and the LPAC at the April 22, 2025 meeting. All references in this Consent to dollar amounts with respect to assets held by the Luxembourg SCSp vehicles reflect this exchange rate unless otherwise stated.

**Instruction:** The Consenting LP should check each fund vehicle in which it currently holds a limited partnership interest and state the amount of the Consenting LP\'s capital commitment to such fund vehicle as set forth in the Consenting LP\'s subscription agreement and applicable LPA. If the Consenting LP is uncertain as to the amount of its capital commitment, it should contact Priya Narasimhan, General Counsel, at the address set forth in Section 8.2 below.

> \(ii\) **OECD Pillar Two GloBE Rules.** The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (\"OECD\") Pillar Two Global Anti-Base Erosion (\"GloBE\") rules are effective for Luxembourg entities from fiscal year 2025 onward. The Reorganization is designed to eliminate exposure to the GloBE rules by consolidating fund activities into Delaware-domiciled vehicles, thereby simplifying the multinational tax compliance framework applicable to the fund platform.

> \(iv\) **LP-Requested Governance Simplification.** At the April 22, 2025 LPAC meeting and in prior discussions with the General Partner, a significant number of limited partners expressed a preference for a simplified governance structure that would consolidate investor reporting, capital call procedures, distribution mechanics, and advisory committee functions across the fund platform.
The Reorganization will be implemented through a five-step transaction structure, with a target effective date of December 1, 2025. Each step is described in detail below.

The full text of the draft amendments to the Fund IV LPA and the Fund V LPA (together, the \"LPA Amendments\") has been circulated separately with the Solicitation Letter. A summary of the specific LPA provisions being amended is set forth in Exhibit A to this Consent.

The Consenting LP is advised that Calderwood & Harkness LLP, as U.S. tax counsel to Solara, is preparing and intends to submit a private letter ruling request (the \"PLR Request\") to the Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\"), Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (CC:INTL), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (CC:PSI). The target submission date for the PLR Request is August 15, 2025.

The PLR Request has been reviewed by the LP Advisory Committee through its independent counsel, Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP (Diana Carruthers, Partner), who has had the opportunity to provide comments and ask questions of Calderwood & Harkness LLP and the General Partner regarding the PLR Request.

The Consenting LP should note that the consummation of the Reorganization may or may not be conditioned on receipt of a favorable private letter ruling from the IRS, as determined by the General Partner in its sole discretion. The General Partner reserves the right to proceed with the Reorganization without a favorable PLR if the General Partner determines, in consultation with Calderwood & Harkness LLP, that the legal analysis supporting the intended tax-free treatment is sufficiently well-established, or to abandon or delay the Reorganization if the IRS declines to issue a favorable ruling.

The Consenting LP hereby acknowledges receipt and review of the LP Tax Impact Summary Letter prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP, which describes the anticipated U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Reorganization for each investor category (U.S. taxable, U.S. tax-exempt, and non-U.S.). Without limiting the generality of such acknowledgment, the Consenting LP specifically acknowledges the following key tax treatment points as set forth in the LP Tax Impact Summary Letter:

The Consenting LP acknowledges and agrees that the LP Tax Impact Summary Letter is provided for informational purposes only and does not constitute tax advice to the Consenting LP. The LP Tax Impact Summary Letter is addressed solely to the General Partner and Solara Digital Infrastructure LP, and no limited partner may rely on the LP Tax Impact Summary Letter as a basis for any tax return position or any other tax-related purpose.

The Consenting LP further acknowledges that it has been advised to consult with its own independent tax advisors regarding the U.S. federal, state, local, and non-U.S. tax consequences of the Reorganization to the Consenting LP in its particular circumstances, including the consequences of the Consenting LP\'s migration to the International Feeder, the Tax-Exempt Feeder, or continued direct investment through the Domestic Fund Vehicles, as applicable.
**[Section 6: Consent]{.underline}**
**6.1 Grant of Consent**
The Consenting LP hereby irrevocably consents to each of the following:

> \(a\) **The Reorganization.** The Reorganization, including each of Steps 1 through 5 as described in Section 3.2 of this Consent, including the formation of the new entities, the contribution of portfolio assets by the Legacy Offshore Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund LP, the dissolution of the Legacy Offshore Vehicles, and the migration of the Consenting LP\'s interest to the applicable post-Reorganization fund vehicle.

> \(b\) **The LPA Amendments.** The amendments to the LPA of each fund vehicle identified in Section 2 in which the Consenting LP holds a limited partnership interest, in substantially the form circulated with the Solicitation Letter (collectively, the \"LPA Amendments\"), including:

> \(i\) The amendment to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP (the \"Fund IV LPA Amendment\"), if the Consenting LP holds an interest in any Fund IV vehicle;

> \(ii\) The amendment to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP (the \"Fund V LPA Amendment\"), if the Consenting LP holds an interest in any Fund V vehicle; and

> \(iii\) Such amendments, resolutions, or other actions as may be required under the governing documents of Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP, Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp, Fund V-A (Cayman) LP, or Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp (as applicable to the Consenting LP), in each case in substantially the form circulated with the Solicitation Letter or as otherwise approved by the General Partner and the LPAC.

> \(d\) **Dissolution and Distribution.** The dissolution of the applicable Legacy Offshore Vehicles and the distribution to the Consenting LP of its pro rata share of partnership interests in the Consolidated Master Fund LP (or, as applicable, interests in the International Feeder or the Tax-Exempt Feeder), as described in Step 5 of Section 3.2.

> \(e\) **LP Migration.** The migration of the Consenting LP\'s interest to the International Feeder (if the Consenting LP is a non-U.S. investor), the Tax-Exempt Feeder (if the Consenting LP is a U.S. tax-exempt investor), or the Consenting LP\'s continued direct co-investment alongside the Consolidated Master Fund LP through the existing Domestic Fund Vehicles (if the Consenting LP is a U.S. taxable investor), as applicable and as described in Step 5 of Section 3.2.

> \(f\) **Authorization of General Partner.** The authorization of the General Partner (Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC) and its officers, including Viktor Raines, Managing Partner, and Meredith Tsao, Chief Operating Officer, to execute and deliver all documents, instruments, certificates, agreements, and filings, and to take all actions, in each case as may be necessary, desirable, or appropriate to consummate the Reorganization and the LPA Amendments, including the execution and delivery of (i) the limited partnership agreement of the Consolidated Master Fund LP, (ii) the limited partnership agreements of the International Feeder and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, (iii) the operating agreement of Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC, (iv) contribution agreements, assignment and assumption agreements, and related transfer documents, (v) IRS Form 8832 elections, (vi) dissolution and wind-down documents for the Legacy Offshore Vehicles, and (vii) any and all other documents, instruments, and agreements contemplated by the Reorganization.
**6.2 Scope of Consent**

This Consent is given pursuant to and in accordance with the amendment and consent provisions of the applicable LPA(s), including, without limitation, the provisions summarized in Exhibit A to this Consent. The Consenting LP has reviewed the applicable amendment and consent provisions and confirms that this Consent is delivered in compliance therewith.

This Consent shall be irrevocable upon delivery to the General Partner, unless and until the General Partner determines to abandon or materially modify the Reorganization as described in Section 3.2 of this Consent, in which case the General Partner shall notify the Consenting LP in writing of such abandonment or material modification, and this Consent shall thereupon be deemed null and void. For the avoidance of doubt, a modification to the Reorganization shall be deemed \"material\" only if it alters the fundamental economic or tax consequences of the Reorganization to the Consenting LP, as determined by the General Partner in its reasonable discretion after consultation with Calderwood & Harkness LLP and the LPAC.

This Consent relates solely to the Reorganization and the LPA Amendments as described herein and does not constitute consent to any other amendment, modification, supplement, or waiver of any provision of the applicable LPA(s) or any other governing document of any fund vehicle. The General Partner\'s rights to seek additional consents from the Consenting LP in the future with respect to other matters are expressly preserved.
**[Section 7: Representations of the Consenting LP]{.underline}**
The Consenting LP hereby represents and warrants to the General Partner as follows, as of the date of the Consenting LP\'s execution and delivery of this Consent:

> \(a\) **Authority.** The Consenting LP has full power and authority to execute and deliver this Consent and to perform its obligations hereunder. If the Consenting LP is an entity (including, without limitation, a corporation, limited liability company, limited partnership, trust, pension fund, endowment, sovereign wealth fund, or other organization), the execution and delivery of this Consent has been duly authorized by all necessary corporate, partnership, limited liability company, trust, or other organizational action on the part of the Consenting LP, and no further action, approval, or consent is required by the Consenting LP or any other person or entity in connection with the execution, delivery, and performance of this Consent.

> \(b\) **Binding Effect.** This Consent constitutes the legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Consenting LP, enforceable against the Consenting LP in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, or similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity (regardless of whether enforcement is sought in a proceeding in equity or at law).

> \(c\) **LP Status.** The Consenting LP is a limited partner in good standing under the LPA(s) of each fund vehicle identified in Section 2 of this Consent. The Consenting LP has not transferred, assigned, pledged, hypothecated, or otherwise encumbered its limited partnership interest in any such fund vehicle, except as previously disclosed to and approved in writing by the General Partner in accordance with the applicable LPA. The Consenting LP\'s capital commitment and percentage interest in each applicable fund vehicle are accurately reflected in the records of the General Partner.

> \(d\) **Receipt of Information.** The Consenting LP has received and reviewed the Solicitation Letter, the LP Tax Impact Summary Letter, and such other information regarding the Reorganization as the Consenting LP has requested from the General Partner or its counsel. The Consenting LP has had a reasonable opportunity to ask questions of the General Partner and its counsel regarding the Reorganization and the LPA Amendments and has received satisfactory answers to all such questions. The Consenting LP is making the decision to execute and deliver this Consent based upon its own independent investigation and analysis of the information provided and such other factors as the Consenting LP deems relevant.

> \(e\) **Independent Tax Advice.** The Consenting LP has had the opportunity to consult with its own independent tax advisors regarding the U.S. federal, state, local, and non-U.S. tax consequences of the Reorganization to the Consenting LP in its particular circumstances, including the consequences of the Consenting LP\'s migration to the International Feeder, the Tax-Exempt Feeder, or continued direct investment through the Domestic Fund Vehicles, as applicable. The Consenting LP acknowledges that neither the General Partner, Solara Digital Infrastructure LP, Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, nor any of their respective affiliates, officers, directors, members, partners, employees, agents, or advisors has provided tax advice to the Consenting LP in connection with the Reorganization. The Consenting LP further acknowledges that the LP Tax Impact Summary Letter does not constitute tax advice to the Consenting LP and that no limited partner may rely on the LP Tax Impact Summary Letter as a basis for any tax return position.

> \(f\) **Investor Category.** The Consenting LP\'s investor category as indicated in Section 1 of this Consent is accurate as of the date hereof. The Consenting LP will promptly notify the General Partner in writing if the Consenting LP\'s investor category changes prior to the effective date of the Reorganization.

> \(g\) **No Violation.** The execution and delivery of this Consent by the Consenting LP and the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Reorganization do not and will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach or default under any provision of the Consenting LP\'s organizational documents (if the Consenting LP is an entity), (ii) violate any law, rule, regulation, order, judgment, injunction, or decree applicable to the Consenting LP, or (iii) violate, conflict with, result in a breach of, constitute a default under, or give rise to any right of termination, cancellation, or acceleration under any agreement, instrument, contract, license, permit, order, judgment, or decree to which the Consenting LP is a party or by which the Consenting LP or any of its assets or properties is bound.

This Consent shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to principles of conflicts of law that would require or permit the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. Each of the parties hereto irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware declines to accept jurisdiction, any state or federal court located in New Castle County, Delaware) for the purposes of any suit, action, or other proceeding arising out of or relating to this Consent.

**If to the Consenting LP:** To the address and contact information set forth in Section 1 of this Consent.
