matches.line: By way of background, BFO received the Fund IV Confidential Private Placement Memorandum, dated December 15, 2023 (the \"PPM\"), and the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Fund IV, dated December 20, 2023 (the \"LPA\"), on or about January 8, 2024. These materials were transmitted electronically via Meridian Peak\'s secure data room, together with related subscription documents, investor questionnaire forms, and ancillary fund documentation.

Following an initial internal review of the PPM, the LPA, and related materials by BFO\'s investment professionals and in-house legal team, BFO engaged Calderwood & Harkness LLP on January 24, 2024 to advise BFO in connection with the proposed commitment and, specifically, to negotiate a side letter to the LPA (the \"Side Letter\") on BFO\'s behalf with respect to certain economic, governance, reporting, and regulatory terms.

At the time negotiations were paused on March 28, 2024, certain material terms remained in brackets in the most recent draft of the Side Letter, including, without limitation, the excuse and exclusion cap percentage, the precise scope of the co-investment allocation methodology, and other items that had not been resolved to both parties\' mutual satisfaction. No final, execution-ready version of the Side Letter was produced.

Accordingly, BFO will not be subscribing for a limited partnership interest in Fund IV and will not be participating in Fund IV\'s anticipated initial closing, which we understand is expected to occur on or about April 30, 2024, or in any subsequent closing of Fund IV.

As a direct result of BFO\'s decision not to proceed with the proposed commitment, all draft Side Letter provisions negotiated between the parties are of no further force or effect and have lapsed in their entirety, effective as of the date of this letter. For clarity and completeness, the lapsed provisions include, without limitation, the following:

> \(f\) **Key Person Event Enhancements.** All provisions modifying the key person provisions set forth in the LPA with respect to BFO, including the provision requiring a ninety (90) day automatic suspension of the investment period upon the departure, death, disability, or material reduction in involvement of either Conrad J. Ellsworth or Priya Narayan from Fund IV investment activities, and the related cure and notice mechanisms negotiated in connection therewith.

> \(h\) **Confidentiality Carve-Outs.** All provisions expanding or modifying the confidentiality obligations set forth in the LPA as applied to BFO, including carve-outs permitting disclosure to BFO\'s affiliates, advisors, auditors, and regulatory authorities in the ordinary course.

> \(i\) **Accelerated Schedule K-1 Delivery.** All provisions requiring the General Partner to deliver, or cause to be delivered, Schedule K-1 (IRS Form 1065) and related tax information to BFO within seventy-five (75) days following the end of each fiscal year of Fund IV, in advance of the delivery timeline set forth in the LPA.
**[No Executed Agreements; No Binding Obligations]{.underline}**
> \(i\) No subscription agreement or subscription booklet was executed by or on behalf of BFO in connection with Fund IV at any time during the course of negotiations.

> \(ii\) No capital commitment --- whether binding, conditional, or otherwise --- has been made by BFO to Fund IV, the General Partner, or the Adviser, whether pursuant to the LPA, any Side Letter, or any other agreement or instrument.

BFO acknowledges and expects that the terms of the parties\' negotiations, including all draft Side Letter provisions, term sheets, markups, and related communications (whether written or oral), will be treated as confidential by Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, Meridian Peak, the General Partner, and Fund IV in accordance with customary practice applicable to fund subscription negotiations. BFO similarly will maintain the confidentiality of all Fund IV materials received by BFO and its advisors in connection with this process, including the PPM, the LPA, subscription documents, data room materials, and all related fund documentation, and will not disclose the terms thereof to any third party except as may be required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, or to BFO\'s professional advisors on a need-to-know basis subject to customary confidentiality undertakings.

We note that BFO and Calderwood & Harkness LLP will retain copies of Fund IV documents received during the course of this process --- including the PPM, the LPA, subscription documents, and related materials --- in their respective files, as required by applicable law, professional responsibility obligations, and firm and institutional document-retention policies. Neither BFO nor Calderwood & Harkness LLP will use or disclose such materials for any purpose other than as may be required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, or in connection with BFO\'s internal recordkeeping. Should Meridian Peak or its counsel wish to discuss further arrangements regarding the retention or return of specific materials, we are happy to accommodate any reasonable request.

In closing, on behalf of BFO and this firm, we wish to express our sincere appreciation for the professionalism, responsiveness, and constructive engagement demonstrated by Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP and the Meridian Peak team throughout the negotiation process. The negotiations were conducted in good faith and in a manner reflecting well on all parties involved. We reiterate that BFO\'s decision to decline the proposed commitment should not be taken as a negative assessment of Fund IV, its investment thesis, or the capabilities of Meridian Peak and its principals. BFO values the relationship it has developed with Meridian Peak during this process and does not foreclose the possibility of future engagement on matters of mutual interest.

Sato, in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding a ten percent (10%) membership interest) of DCM, will serve as the primary point of contact for the Clients in connection with this engagement. > \(b\) **Section 8.04(b) --- Trigger Conditions.** C&H will analyze the trigger conditions set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA in light of the facts surrounding Mr. Whitmore\'s incapacitation. Specifically, Section 8.04(b) provides that a Key Person Event is deemed to occur when the Key Person becomes unable, whether by reason of death, disability, incapacity, departure, or otherwise, to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. **C.** *Proposed First Amendment.* In response to the Key Person Event and pursuant to its obligations under Section 8.04(c) of the Partnership Agreement, the General Partner has prepared and proposed a First Amendment to the Amended & Restated Limited Partnership Agreement (the \"Amendment\" or the \"First Amendment\"), a complete and final copy of which is attached hereto as **Exhibit A** and incorporated herein by reference. The Amendment, among other things, is designed to address the Key Person Event by establishing a successor governance framework for the Partnership, designating Successor Key Persons, creating a new Investment Committee structure, and making certain related adjustments to the carried interest allocation schedule and related economic terms. The Amendment, together with a Successor Key Person Proposal and Consent Solicitation Letter (the \"Solicitation Letter\"), was circulated to all Limited Partners of record on July 15, 2024, in the manner prescribed by Section 11.01 of the Partnership Agreement.

**D.** *Consent Required.* Section 14.01 of the Partnership Agreement provides that the Partnership Agreement may be amended, modified, or supplemented with the prior written consent of the General Partner and Limited Partners holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding, for purposes of such calculation, any co-investment commitments made by the General Partner, any Affiliate of the General Partner, or any principal, member, partner, officer, or employee thereof in their capacity as co-investors alongside the Fund). Additionally, Section 8.04(c) of the Partnership Agreement provides that one or more Successor Key Persons may be designated by the General Partner with the approval of Limited Partners holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (calculated on the same basis as set forth above). As of the date hereof, the aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments for voting purposes equal Two Billion Seven Hundred Ninety-Eight Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,798,250,000), being the total fund assets under management of Two Billion Eight Hundred Seventy Million Dollars (\$2,870,000,000) less the General Partner co-investment commitments of Fifty-Seven Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$57,400,000) attributable to Marcus J. Whitmore and Fourteen Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,350,000) attributable to Elaine R. Sato, in her capacity as Managing Member of DCM. Accordingly, the required consent threshold for each of the matters set forth herein is One Billion Eight Hundred Sixty-Five Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$1,865,500,000) (being 66⅔% of \$2,798,250,000).

**E.** *Consent Deadline.* The General Partner has established August 23, 2024 (being forty (40) calendar days from the date of circulation of the Amendment and the Solicitation Letter to the Limited Partners) as the deadline for the delivery of this Written Consent (the \"Consent Deadline\"). Any Written Consent not received by the General Partner or its designated counsel on or before the Consent Deadline shall not be counted toward the required consent threshold described in Recital D above, unless the General Partner, in its sole discretion, elects to extend the Consent Deadline by written notice to all Limited Partners.
**[RESOLUTIONS AND CONSENT]{.underline}**

NOW, THEREFORE, the undersigned Limited Partner of the Partnership, in consideration of the premises and intending to be legally bound hereby, and for the purpose of effecting the matters described below without a meeting of the Limited Partners in accordance with Section 14.01 of the Partnership Agreement, hereby consents to and approves the following resolutions:

**RESOLVED**, that the undersigned Limited Partner hereby consents to and approves the designation of each of the following individuals as \"Successor Key Persons\" under Section 8.04 of the Partnership Agreement, as amended by the First Amendment:

The terms and conditions of such designation, including the respective obligations of each Successor Key Person, the consequences of the departure, incapacitation, or removal of either Successor Key Person, and related governance matters, are more fully set forth in the Amendment attached hereto as **Exhibit A**. The undersigned Limited Partner acknowledges that it has reviewed the professional backgrounds, qualifications, and experience of each proposed Successor Key Person as described in the Solicitation Letter and any supplemental materials provided by the General Partner, and has determined, in its sole judgment, that the designation of Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons is in the best interests of the Partnership and the Limited Partners.

Huang, jointly, in replacement of Marcus J. Whitmore, effective upon the date on which the Amendment becomes effective (the \"Amendment Effective Date\"), with all references in the Partnership Agreement to the \"Key Person\" being deemed to refer to Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang in their joint capacity as Successor Key Persons.

The Investment Committee shall be comprised of the following members: (I) Elaine R. Sato, who shall serve as Chair of the Investment Committee; (II) Jonathan K. Huang; and (III) one independent member (the \"Independent IC Member\") to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee established under Section 9.03 of the Partnership Agreement, which Independent IC Member shall not be an employee, officer, member, partner, or Affiliate of the General Partner, and shall possess relevant experience in multi-strategy or credit-oriented investment management. Whitmore as \"Senior Advisor\" to the Partnership and the General Partner, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date. > darf-consent@calderwoodharkness.com
> \(iii\) **Facsimile Transmission.** Delivery of the fully executed Written Consent by facsimile transmission to:

We are pleased to confirm the engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") by Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"ManCo\" or the \"Client\") to serve as legal counsel in connection with the matters described herein. This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions upon which we will provide legal services to the Client in connection with this engagement.
**[1. Purpose and Engagement]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter confirms that Calderwood & Harkness has been engaged by the ManCo to serve as legal counsel in connection with a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$2.8 billion in total commitments. The ManCo is a Delaware limited liability company and a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") under CRD #298417. The Fund\'s sole general partner is Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company.

The engagement encompasses the formation of new holding entities, the negotiation of separation arrangements with departing principals, the realignment of carried interest and management fee economics among continuing and next-generation principals, the solicitation of necessary limited partner consents, compliance with existing side-letter obligations, and related tax structuring. The scope of the representation, the personnel assigned to the engagement, the fee arrangement, and other terms and conditions governing this engagement are set forth in the sections that follow.
**[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

The engagement will comprise the following principal workstreams, each of which is described in greater detail below. We understand that the scope of the engagement may evolve as the restructuring progresses; any material expansion of the scope described herein will be discussed with the Client in advance.
**2.1 Entity Restructuring**
Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the restructuring of the organizational hierarchy of the Ardent Capital platform, including:

\(a\) Advising on the formation of a new Delaware limited liability company, to be named Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\"), which will serve as a parent holding company for both the General Partner and the ManCo, thereby consolidating the principals\' economic interests and governance rights in a single vehicle at the top of the organizational structure.

\(b\) Advising on the formation of an intermediate entity, Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\"), as a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo and the sole member of the General Partner. GP Intermediate will serve as an interposing entity between HoldCo and the General Partner, facilitating the allocation of carried interest economics and providing structural flexibility for the admission of future principals and the potential establishment of successor funds.

matches.line: **RE:** Summary and Risk Assessment of Private Placement Memorandum --- Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P.

The purpose of this memorandum is to provide Briarwood Family Office LLC\'s (\"BFO\") investment team and general counsel with a comprehensive summary of the Private Placement Memorandum dated December 15, 2023 (the \"PPM\") for Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. (\"Fund IV\" or the \"Fund\"), and to identify key risk factors, regulatory considerations, and areas warranting further diligence or side-letter protection in connection with BFO\'s evaluation of a proposed capital commitment to Fund IV.

The PPM was received by BFO directly from Gavin R. The PPM contains an extensive risk factors section that identifies the material risks associated with an investment in Fund IV. The following summarizes the key risk categories and our assessment of their significance to BFO.

**Real Estate Market Cyclicality.** The PPM acknowledges that commercial real estate markets are inherently cyclical and subject to periods of significant volatility in asset values, rental rates, occupancy levels, and capitalization rates. Fund IV\'s investment period coincides with a period of elevated uncertainty in commercial real estate markets, driven in part by rising interest rates, shifting demand patterns (particularly in office markets), and evolving macroeconomic conditions. BFO should consider the risk that Fund IV may deploy capital near a cyclical peak or during a period of declining asset values.

**Interest Rate Risk.** The PPM identifies interest rate risk as a significant factor affecting Fund IV\'s investment performance. Rising interest rates increase borrowing costs at both the fund level and the property level, may compress asset valuations by increasing capitalization rates, and may reduce transaction volume in the broader market. Given the current interest rate environment, this risk factor is particularly salient for Fund IV\'s investment period.

**Valuation Uncertainty.** As noted above, Fund IV\'s portfolio investments will be valued at the General Partner\'s determination of fair market value, which is inherently subjective. The PPM notes that there can be no assurance that the valuations assigned to unrealized investments will ultimately be achieved upon realization, and that material downward revisions in valuation are possible.

**Geographic Concentration.** While the PPM describes the Fund\'s geographic focus as \"North America,\" which encompasses a broad range of markets, the concentration of investments within a single continental market means that the Fund\'s portfolio will be subject to correlated risks affecting North American real estate, including U.S. monetary policy, domestic economic conditions, and regulatory developments.

**Leverage Risk.** The PPM discloses that Fund IV will utilize leverage at both the fund level (through a subscription credit facility and other fund-level borrowing arrangements) and the property level (through mortgage debt and other asset-level financing). Leverage amplifies both gains and losses and introduces additional risk through the potential for margin calls, covenant violations, and forced asset dispositions in adverse market conditions. The PPM does not specify the maximum leverage ratios at the fund or property level; these are set forth in the LPA and analyzed in the LPA Review Memo.

**Illiquidity.** The PPM states that limited partnership interests in Fund IV are **not freely transferable** and that there is **no public market** for such interests. Limited partners should expect to hold their interests for the full term of the Fund (potentially up to twelve years, including extensions) and should not anticipate any opportunity for early liquidity, except in limited circumstances through permitted transfers as specified in the LPA. This illiquidity risk is fundamental to the nature of the investment and should be a primary consideration in BFO\'s portfolio construction and liquidity management analysis.

**Key Person Dependency.** The PPM acknowledges that Fund IV\'s investment program is substantially dependent on the continued involvement of Conrad J. Ellsworth and Priya Narayan. The departure, death, disability, or reduced involvement of either Key Person would have a material adverse effect on the Fund\'s investment program and performance. While the LPA contains Key Person Event provisions, these provisions may not fully protect limited partners against the consequences of a Key Person departure, particularly if the General Partner identifies and installs a replacement key person who lacks the experience, relationships, or capabilities of the departing principal.
**Conflicts of Interest.** The PPM identifies several categories of conflicts of interest that may arise in connection with the Sponsor\'s management of Fund IV:

> • *Allocation Conflicts:* The Sponsor manages multiple funds with overlapping investment strategies. To the extent that an investment opportunity is suitable for more than one fund, the General Partner must determine the allocation of that opportunity among competing vehicles. > • *Co-Investment by GP Affiliates:* The PPM discloses that the General Partner and its affiliates (including MPCA personnel) may co-invest alongside Fund IV in certain transactions. While such co-investment may align the interests of the Sponsor and its limited partners, it also creates potential conflicts regarding pricing, allocation, and exit timing.

> • *Fee and Expense Conflicts:* The Sponsor earns management fees and carried interest from Fund IV, and certain expenses of the Sponsor\'s operations may be allocated to the Fund. The PPM discloses the categories of expenses that are borne by the Fund and those that are borne by the Sponsor, but the line between these categories may be subject to interpretation in practice.

**Successor Fund Risk.** The PPM notes that the Sponsor may raise a successor fund (Fund V) during Fund IV\'s investment period, subject to limitations set forth in the LPA. The fundraising for and management of a successor fund would divert the Sponsor\'s attention and resources from Fund IV\'s investment activities and could create additional allocation conflicts between Fund IV and the successor fund. BFO should review the LPA\'s successor fund provisions carefully (as discussed in the LPA Review Memo) and consider whether additional protections are warranted in the side letter.

**Limited Governance Rights.** The PPM acknowledges that limited partners have **limited governance rights** under the LPA and limited ability to influence Fund IV\'s investment decisions, operational matters, or strategic direction. The General Partner has broad authority to manage the Fund\'s affairs, and limited partner consent or approval is required only for a narrow set of fundamental actions (e.g., amendment of certain material LPA provisions, removal of the General Partner for cause). Limited partners do not have the right to participate in the day-to-day management of the Fund, and the LPAC (if constituted) serves in an advisory capacity only, without binding authority over the General Partner.

As described in the PPM, a defaulting limited partner may be subject to forfeiture of up to **50%** of such limited partner\'s interest in the Fund, in addition to other remedies available to the General Partner. These provisions are designed to incentivize timely funding of capital calls but represent a significant risk to any limited partner that experiences liquidity constraints during the Fund\'s term. A detailed analysis of the default provisions is set forth in the LPA Review Memo.

**Exemption from Registration.** Fund IV\'s interests are offered solely under exemptions from registration under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. There is no public registration, no public prospectus, and no regulatory review of the PPM by the SEC or any state securities regulator. Limited partners must rely on their own due diligence and analysis, and must satisfy the eligibility requirements applicable to the relevant exemptions (including status as \"accredited investors\" and \"qualified purchasers\").

**Partnership Tax Treatment.** Fund IV is structured as a Delaware limited partnership and intends to be treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. As a pass-through entity, Fund IV does not pay entity-level federal income tax; instead, items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit are allocated to and reported by the limited partners on their respective tax returns. The PPM notes that there can be no assurance that the IRS will not challenge the Fund\'s classification as a partnership or the allocation of tax items among the partners.

**Effectively Connected Income (ECI).** The PPM notes that non-U.S. investors in Fund IV may be subject to U.S. federal income tax on income that is treated as effectively connected with a U.S. trade or business. While this risk is most directly relevant to non-U.S. investors, BFO should be aware that the Fund\'s investment in real estate operating companies and asset management platforms may generate income that raises ECI issues for certain investor categories.

**Unrelated Business Taxable Income (UBTI).** The PPM notes that the use of leverage in the Fund\'s investments may generate UBTI for tax-exempt investors. While BFO is not a tax-exempt entity, BFO should confirm with its tax advisors whether any component of its ownership structure (e.g., any underlying charitable trusts or foundations with interests in BFO) may be affected by UBTI considerations.

**State and Local Tax Filing Obligations.** The PPM discloses that limited partners may be required to file state and local tax returns in each jurisdiction where Fund IV holds investments. Given Fund IV\'s geographic focus on North American (primarily U.S.) commercial real estate, BFO should anticipate potential tax filing obligations in multiple states. BFO\'s tax advisors should evaluate the scope and cost of these obligations prior to commitment.

The PPM notes that Fund IV intends to limit participation by \"benefit plan investors\" (as defined in the Department of Labor\'s plan asset regulations under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended, and Section 4975 of the Internal Revenue Code) to below the **25% threshold** under DOL regulations, in order to avoid characterization of Fund IV\'s assets as \"plan assets\" for purposes of ERISA. If the Fund\'s assets were characterized as plan assets, the General Partner and the Sponsor would be subject to the fiduciary and prohibited transaction rules of ERISA, which would significantly constrain the Fund\'s investment activities and impose substantial compliance obligations.

**Relevance to BFO.** Although BFO is not itself an ERISA plan and is not a \"benefit plan investor,\" C&H recommends that BFO\'s side letter include **excuse rights** for any investment that would cause BFO (or any underlying beneficial owner of BFO) to be treated as holding \"plan assets\" under ERISA. This is a protective measure designed to insulate BFO from the risk that the Fund\'s investor composition changes over time in a manner that could trigger plan asset characterization.

The PPM\'s subscription documents include standard representations and warranties regarding compliance with U.S. sanctions laws, anti-money laundering laws, and related regulations. However, these representations apply to the investor\'s own status and do not address the Fund\'s investment-level compliance with sanctions requirements.

This will ensure that BFO is not required to fund capital calls for investments that could expose BFO to sanctions-related risk.

The PPM states that Fund IV filed a **Form D** with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (\"SEC\") on **January 2, 2024**, in connection with its offering of limited partnership interests under **Regulation D** of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the \"Securities Act\"). The offering is made in reliance on Rule 506 of Regulation D, which provides an exemption from the registration requirements of the Securities Act for offerings made solely to \"accredited investors\" as defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D.

In addition, the Fund requires that each investor qualify as a \"qualified purchaser\" as defined in Section 2(a)(51) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the \"Investment Company Act\"), in order for the Fund to rely on the **Section 3(c)(7) exclusion** from the definition of \"investment company\" under the Investment Company Act. The Section 3(c)(7) exclusion permits a fund to have an unlimited number of beneficial owners, provided that all such owners are \"qualified purchasers\" and that the fund does not make (and does not propose to make) a public offering of its securities.

The PPM and subscription documents include standard anti-money laundering (\"AML\") and know-your-customer (\"KYC\") representations and warranties that each investor must provide in connection with its subscription for limited partnership interests in Fund IV. These representations address, among other things, the investor\'s identity, source of funds, beneficial ownership structure, and compliance with applicable AML laws, including the Bank Secrecy Act and the USA PATRIOT Act.

The PPM notes that the Fund has taken steps to comply with applicable state securities laws (\"Blue Sky\" laws) in connection with the offering. Based on our review, we have not identified any specific state-level securities law issues that would affect BFO\'s participation in Fund IV. BFO is a **New York-based limited liability company**, and New York\'s state securities regime does not impose additional filing or consent requirements for investments of this type beyond those addressed through the federal Regulation D framework. The PPM does not indicate that the placement fee will be offset against management fees payable by the General Partner or the Sponsor. In the absence of such an offset, BFO would bear its proportionate share of the aggregate placement fees paid by the Fund in addition to its full management fee obligation, resulting in an effective \"double charge\" for the capital raise.

**C&H Recommendation:** The side letter should include a provision requiring **100% offset of the placement fee attributable to BFO\'s commitment (\$750,000)** against management fees payable by BFO. This offset should be applied as a dollar-for-dollar reduction in management fees commencing in the first year following BFO\'s admission to the Fund and continuing until the full \$750,000 has been credited. If the General Partner resists a 100% offset, BFO should negotiate for no less than a 50% offset as a fallback position.

**Carried Interest.** As described in Section II.D, the General Partner is entitled to a carried interest of **20%** of net profits above an **8% preferred return** (compounded annually), calculated on a **whole-fund European waterfall** basis.

**GP Clawback.** The PPM states that the General Partner is subject to a clawback obligation, which requires the General Partner to return excess carried interest distributions if, at the end of the Fund\'s term (or upon earlier liquidation), the cumulative distributions to limited partners are insufficient to provide a return of contributed capital and the 8% preferred return. The PPM indicates that the clawback obligation is calculated on an **after-tax basis**, meaning that the General Partner\'s obligation is reduced by an assumed tax liability on the carried interest previously received. The after-tax clawback is less favorable to limited partners than a gross (pre-tax) clawback, as it reduces the amount that limited partners can recover in a clawback scenario. BFO should seek a gross clawback (or a more favorable tax rate assumption) in the side letter or, at minimum, ensure that the assumed tax rate used in the after-tax calculation is reasonable and clearly specified in the LPA.

**Escrow Mechanism.** The PPM describes an escrow mechanism pursuant to which a portion of carried interest distributions will be deposited into an escrow account to secure the General Partner\'s clawback obligation. Market practice for escrow percentages ranges from 15% to 30% of carried interest distributions, and BFO should evaluate whether the specified percentage provides adequate protection in light of the Fund\'s risk profile and the General Partner\'s financial capacity to satisfy the clawback obligation.

2\. **Excuse and Exclusion Rights.** The PPM does not impose sector-specific exclusions at the fund level. matches.line: **RE:** Initial Client Intake --- Solara Digital Infrastructure LP Cross-Border Fund-Platform Reorganization; Private Letter Ruling Request

This memorandum summarizes the facts received from Solara Digital Infrastructure LP\'s (\"Solara\" or the \"Client\") in-house legal and tax teams during two initial intake calls conducted on May 22, 2025, and May 26, 2025, in advance of the formal matter opening on May 27, 2025. The May 22 call was approximately ninety minutes in duration and focused primarily on the existing fund structure and business rationale for the proposed reorganization. The May 26 call was approximately two hours in duration and covered the proposed multi-step transaction, the representative portfolio company holdings, the aggregate financial parameters of the reorganization, and outstanding data needs. Both calls were conducted by videoconference, with Robert Jansen and Garrett Simmons participating from Calderwood & Harkness\'s Washington, D.C. and New York offices, respectively.

The principal Solara contacts for the intake were Priya Narasimhan, General Counsel, and Stefan Dalmqvist, Head of Tax. Additional financial data, including aggregate fair market valuations, adjusted tax basis information, and liability schedules, were confirmed during the May 26 call by Douglas Wexford, Chief Financial Officer. Ms. Narasimhan and Mr. Dalmqvist indicated that their internal team has been developing the reorganization concept since early 2025 and has already obtained preliminary approval from the LP Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\"), as discussed in further detail below.

The purpose of this memorandum is to establish the factual foundation for the preparation and submission of a private letter ruling (\"PLR\") request to the Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\") Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (\"CC:INTL\"), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (\"CC:PSI\"). The PLR request will seek confirmation of the intended tax-free treatment of a multi-step cross-border reorganization of Solara\'s fund platform and the continued partnership classification of the resulting entities for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The reorganization involves the domestication and consolidation of four offshore fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure, with corresponding distributions to limited partners and migration of investor classes into appropriate feeder vehicles.
**A. Solara Digital Infrastructure LP**

The Client\'s full legal name is **Solara Digital Infrastructure LP**. It is a Delaware limited partnership organized under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 et seq.) and formed on March 17, 2014. Its principal office and headquarters are located at 1200 Market Street, Suite 3400, Wilmington, Delaware 19801. The Client\'s Employer Identification Number is 82-4917366.

As of March 31, 2025, Solara reports total assets under management (\"AUM\") of approximately \$14.7 billion across all fund vehicles. Solara is a private equity sponsor that targets investments in digital infrastructure assets, including data centers, fiber-optic networks, and edge computing facilities, as well as enterprise software-as-a-service (\"SaaS\") platforms. The firm\'s investment thesis centers on the secular growth of data consumption, cloud computing demand, and the buildout of next-generation telecommunications infrastructure. Solara pursues a control-oriented investment strategy, typically acquiring majority or significant minority stakes in operating companies within its target sectors.

Solara operates through a series of parallel fund structures established across three jurisdictions --- Delaware, the Cayman Islands, and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg --- to accommodate three distinct investor pools: U.S. taxable investors, U.S. tax-exempt investors, and non-U.S. investors. The rationale for this multi-jurisdictional structure, and the business drivers for the proposed reorganization that would simplify it, are discussed in Sections III and V below.
The following individuals constitute Solara\'s senior management team and have been identified as relevant contacts for purposes of this engagement:

> • **Viktor Raines** --- Managing Partner and Founder, age 52. Mr. Raines founded Solara in 2014 after serving as a Managing Director in the infrastructure and technology investment group at Havensgate Capital Partners, where he was responsible for approximately \$3 billion in deployed capital. Mr. Raines serves as the manager of Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC and is the authorized signatory for the general partner entity. He will be the signatory on the penalties of perjury statement required for the PLR submission.

> • **Priya Narasimhan** --- General Counsel, age 44. Ms. Narasimhan serves as Calderwood & Harkness\'s primary legal contact for the engagement. She oversees all legal affairs for the Solara platform and coordinates with external counsel across jurisdictions.

> • **Stefan Dalmqvist** --- Head of Tax, age 46. Mr. Dalmqvist is responsible for tax planning, compliance, and reporting across all fund vehicles. He is Calderwood & Harkness\'s primary technical contact for the engagement and has been the principal driver of the reorganization from a tax-planning perspective.

The general partner for Solara\'s Delaware fund vehicles is **Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company with EIN 82-4917365. The entity is manager-managed, with Viktor Raines serving as the sole manager. Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC was organized contemporaneously with Solara Digital Infrastructure LP in March 2014 and is classified as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes (it has more than one member, and no election to be treated as a corporation has been filed). The entity\'s registered agent is Capitol Registered Agents Inc., located at 850 New Burton Road, Suite 201, Dover, Delaware 19904.
As described in Section III below, separate general partner entities were established in the Cayman Islands and Luxembourg for the offshore fund vehicles.

**A. Overview.** Solara currently operates through six parallel fund vehicles spanning three jurisdictions --- Delaware, the Cayman Islands, and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. These six vehicles are divided across two vintage-year fund families: Fund IV (vintage 2021) and Fund V (vintage 2023). Each fund family consists of three parallel vehicles: a Delaware limited partnership for U.S. taxable investors, a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership for non-U.S. and U.S. tax-exempt investors, and a Luxembourg special limited partnership (société en commandite spéciale, or \"SCSp\") for certain European and Asian non-U.S. investors requiring access to Luxembourg\'s extensive bilateral tax treaty network or preferring a regulated European domicile for internal governance reasons.

As of the date of intake, the total number of portfolio companies held across all six vehicles is twenty-three (23), of which eleven (11) are held by Fund IV vehicles and twelve (12) are held by Fund V vehicles. Certain portfolio companies are held jointly across the Delaware and offshore vehicles within the same vintage, reflecting parallel investment structures in which each vehicle invests pro rata alongside the others in each portfolio investment.
The following subsections describe each of the six fund vehicles in detail.
**B. Fund IV Family**
The Fund IV family reached its final close on June 15, 2021, and comprises the following three vehicles:
**1. Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP.**
> • **General Partner:** Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC

Fund IV LP is the domestic anchor vehicle for the Fund IV family. It is the largest single vehicle by committed capital within Fund IV and serves as the lead investment vehicle, with the offshore parallel vehicles generally co-investing in identical portfolio company transactions on a pro rata basis according to each vehicle\'s available capital. The limited partnership agreement of Fund IV LP was most recently amended and restated as of June 15, 2021 (the \"Fund IV LPA\"), and governs investor rights, fee arrangements, carried interest allocations, and other material terms. A copy of the Fund IV LPA has been requested from the Client as part of our initial data request.
**2. Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP.**
> • **General Partner:** Solara Offshore GP Ltd., a Cayman Islands exempted company incorporated under the Cayman Islands Companies Act (As Revised)

Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP serves two primary investor populations: (a) non-U.S. investors, such as sovereign wealth funds and non-U.S. insurance companies, that invest through the Cayman vehicle for tax efficiency and to minimize direct U.S. filing obligations; and (b) U.S. tax-exempt investors, such as public pension funds and university endowments, that invest through the Cayman vehicle to achieve UBTI blocker benefits via offshore corporate subsidiary holding structures interposed between the fund and debt-financed portfolio investments. This vehicle co-invests alongside Fund IV LP in each Fund IV portfolio company on a pro rata basis.
**3. Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp.**
> • **General Partner (gérant commandité):** Solara Luxembourg Management S.à r.l., a Luxembourg société à responsabilité limitée; RCS number B 248194

Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp was established to accommodate non-U.S. investors --- principally European institutional investors and certain Asian investors --- that preferred investment through a Luxembourg-domiciled vehicle for treaty access, regulatory familiarity, or internal governance mandate reasons. The Luxembourg SCSp is a tax-transparent entity under Luxembourg domestic law and is treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. This vehicle co-invests alongside Fund IV LP and Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP in the Fund IV portfolio.
**C. Fund V Family**
The Fund V family reached its final close on September 30, 2023, and comprises the following three vehicles:
**1. Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP.**
> • **General Partner:** Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC

Fund V LP is the largest single fund vehicle in the Solara platform and represents the domestic anchor vehicle for the Fund V family. Given its relatively recent vintage, a substantial portion of committed capital remains undeployed. The limited partnership agreement of Fund V LP was executed as of September 30, 2023 (the \"Fund V LPA\"). Stefan Dalmqvist noted during the May 26 call that Fund V LP has the most recent and investor-favorable governance provisions among the Solara fund documents, and that the Consolidated Master Fund LP\'s partnership agreement will likely be modeled on the Fund V LPA.
**2. Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP.**
> • **General Partner:** Solara Offshore GP Ltd.
Fund V-A (Cayman) LP serves the same investor populations as Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP, as described above. The vehicle is registered with CIMA and administered by Clarendon Fund Services Ltd.
**3. Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp.**
> • **General Partner (gérant commandité):** Solara Luxembourg Management S.à r.l.

Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp serves the same investor profile as Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp. Stefan Dalmqvist noted during the intake call that the Luxembourg vehicles have attracted modestly higher capital commitments in Fund V relative to Fund IV, reflecting increased allocations from European institutional investors, but that the OECD Pillar Two developments discussed in Section V below have diminished the forward-looking rationale for maintaining separate Luxembourg-domiciled vehicles.
The Solara platform accommodates three principal categories of investors, each of which is directed to the appropriate fund vehicle based on its tax and regulatory profile:

**U.S. Taxable Investors.** U.S. taxable investors --- including high-net-worth individuals, family offices, and U.S. taxable institutional investors --- invest through the Delaware main funds (Fund IV LP and Fund V LP). These investors receive annual Schedule K-1s from the Delaware partnerships and report their allocable shares of fund income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit on their individual or entity-level U.S. federal income tax returns. A representative investor in this category is Argyle Family Office Holdings LLC, a Delaware-organized family office with its principal office in Greenwich, Connecticut. Argyle\'s principal is Elliot Argyle. Argyle committed \$95 million to Fund IV LP and \$130 million to Fund V LP.

**U.S. Tax-Exempt Investors.** U.S. tax-exempt investors --- including public pension funds, state retirement systems, university endowments, and certain foundations --- invest through the Cayman parallel vehicles (Fund IV-A Cayman and Fund V-A Cayman) to achieve UBTI blocker benefits. Specifically, these investors typically access the fund through one or more offshore corporate subsidiary holding structures interposed between the Cayman fund vehicle and the underlying debt-financed portfolio investments, thereby blocking unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") that would otherwise be generated by the use of fund-level or portfolio-level leverage. Representative investors in this category include:

> • **Pinnacle State Employees\' Retirement System** --- a public pension fund established under the laws of the State of Pinnacle. Pinnacle committed \$275 million to Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP and \$340 million to Fund V-A (Cayman) LP. The Chief Investment Officer is Margaret Faulkner.

> • **Grandview University Endowment** --- a university endowment established by Grandview University, a private university organized under the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. The key financial parameters of this contribution are as follows:

The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment of Step 2 is as a tax-free contribution under IRC § 721(a), which provides that no gain or loss shall be recognized to a partnership or to any of its partners in the case of a contribution of property to the partnership in exchange for an interest in the partnership. No gain or loss would be recognized by Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP as the contributing partner or by the Consolidated Master Fund LP as the receiving partnership.

> • **Carryover Basis.** Under IRC § 723, the Consolidated Master Fund LP will take a carryover basis in the contributed assets equal to the adjusted tax basis of such assets in the hands of Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP immediately prior to the contribution. This preserves the \$690 million built-in gain for future recognition upon a taxable disposition of the contributed assets.

> • **Holding Period Tacking.** Under IRC § 1223(2), the Consolidated Master Fund LP\'s holding period in the contributed assets will include the period during which Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP held such assets, provided the assets were capital assets or property described in IRC § 1231 in the hands of the contributing partner. This tacking is critical for preserving long-term capital gain treatment on future dispositions.

> • **Luxembourg Withholding Tax Analysis.** Under Luxembourg domestic law, the SCSp is a tax-transparent entity, and no Luxembourg capital gains tax is expected to apply at the SCSp level on the transfer of its portfolio assets to the Consolidated Master Fund LP. Specifically, Article 3(2) of the Luxembourg law of July 12, 2013 provides that the SCSp is not itself subject to Luxembourg income tax; rather, each partner is subject to tax in its jurisdiction of residence on its allocable share of SCSp income. Solara\'s Luxembourg counsel, Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l., will provide a formal opinion on this point. {"file_path":"response.md","content":"# Funds & Asset Management matters involving a signed-LPA fund with an LP advisory committee

## Answer

**4 qualifying Funds & Asset Management matters.** The count is by **matter**, not by fund vehicle. One qualifying matter (1041-00005) covers two fund vehicles, so the four matters cover **five qualifying fund vehicles** in total.

I treated an **Investor Advisory Committee (IAC)** as an LP advisory committee where the governing LPA establishes it as the investor advisory body. I excluded funds for which the file showed only a draft/proposed LPA or no signed LPA, even where the draft described an LPAC.

## Qualifying matters

| Matter | Fund | Why it qualifies | Key documents relied on |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1001-00002** | **Ardent Capital Partners III LP** | The fund’s LPAC is expressly established under Section 9.4 of its LPA. The LPAC gave written consent to the restructuring. The amendment identifies the underlying LPA as dated April 15, 2019, is effective February 28, 2024, and states that the necessary instruments were executed and delivered. | `documents/matters/1001-00002/LP Consent & Notification/lpac-form-of-written-consent.docx` — identifies the LPA as dated April 15, 2019 and is an executed LPAC consent effective February 14, 2024. `documents/matters/1001-00002/LP Consent & Notification/lpac-presentation-memo.docx` — presents the restructuring to the LPAC and describes the requested LPAC consent. `documents/matters/1001-00002/Amended Governing Documents/lpa-amendment-no-1.docx` — Amendment No. 1 to the LPA, effective February 28, 2024; confirms the LPAC’s consent and the continuing LPAC structure. |
| **1024-00002** | **Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (DARF)** | DARF’s governing body is called the **Investor Advisory Committee (IAC)**. The existing A&R LPA is dated March 15, 2017. The First Amendment became effective August 26, 2024 after the required LP consents; the amendment records that the IAC reviewed the proposal at a duly convened meeting and supported it. | `documents/matters/1024-00002/Engagement/engagement-letter-darf-gp-advisory.docx` — identifies the March 15, 2017 A&R LPA and the IAC under Section 9.02. `documents/matters/1024-00002/Transaction Documents/execution-first-amendment-ar-lpa.docx` — execution version of the First Amendment, effective August 26, 2024; records the IAC’s July 29, 2024 review and the 38-of-47 LP consents representing approximately 86.2% of voting commitments. `documents/matters/1024-00002/Closing/closing-certificate-consent-tabulation.docx` — certifies the consent tabulation and effectiveness of the First Amendment. |
| **1027-00002** | **Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P.** | The LPA establishes a three-member LPAC. Pellegrino’s executed side letter gives it the right to designate one LPAC member. The closing checklist expressly marks the LPA as fully executed by the GP and all LPs on January 30, 2026. | `documents/matters/1027-00002/Transaction Documents/co-invest-lpa-execution-version.docx` — execution version effective January 30, 2026; Article IX establishes the three-member LPAC and provides its functions and procedures. `documents/matters/1027-00002/Transaction Documents/side-letter-pellegrino.docx` — effective January 30, 2026; grants Pellegrino one LPAC seat and defines the LPAC as the committee established under the LPA. `documents/matters/1027-00002/Closing/closing-checklist.xlsx` — states that the LPA was fully executed by the GP and all LPs and marks it “Executed” on January 30, 2026; separately records Pellegrino’s LPAC appointment right. `documents/matters/1027-00002/Closing/enforceability-opinion-letter.docx` — delivered in connection with the January 30, 2026 closing and treats the LPA, side letter, and subscription agreement as executed transaction documents. |
| **1041-00005** | **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP and Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** | This is one matter involving two existing fund families. The intake materials identify Fund IV’s final close as June 15, 2021 and its A&R LPA as of that date; they identify Fund V’s final close as September 30, 2023 and state that the Fund V LPA was executed as of that date. The funds had an LPAC, which reviewed the proposed reorganization and gave preliminary consent. The draft amendments themselves were not treated as signed; the signed-LPA screen is satisfied by the pre-existing Fund IV/Fund V LPAs. | `documents/matters/1041-00005/Engagement & Client Management/initial-client-intake-memorandum.docx` — describes the six existing vehicles, Fund IV’s June 15, 2021 A&R LPA, Fund V’s September 30, 2023 executed LPA, and the LPAC’s preliminary approval. `documents/matters/1041-00005/LP Communications/lpac-presentation-reorganization-overview.pptx` — presentation to the LPAC; records the April 22, 2025 LPAC meeting and preliminary consent representing 78% in interest. `documents/matters/1041-00005/PLR Request Drafting/lpac-comment-summary-response-memo.docx` — identifies Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle as counsel to the LPACs of both Fund IV and Fund V and discusses their review of the reorganization. `documents/matters/1041-00005/LP Communications/draft-amendment-fund-iv-lpa.docx` and `.../draft-amendment-fund-v-lpa.docx` — draft amendments that confirm the existing LPACs and their consent role; these were not counted as signed amendments. `documents/matters/1041-00005/LP Communications/form-of-lp-consent.docx` — form consent referring to the applicable existing LPAs and the LPAC review/consent process. |

## Screening and reasoning

I used a two-part test:

1. **Signed-LPA requirement.** I required evidence that the fund’s LPA was an existing executed/effective agreement, not merely a draft, markup, execution-ready form, or future closing deliverable.
2. **Advisory-committee requirement.** I required the LPA or related governance documents to establish an LPAC, IAC, or equivalent investor advisory committee, or to show that such a committee actually reviewed or consented to a fund matter.

A client’s own subscription or side letter did **not** have to be signed for the matter to qualify if the underlying fund’s LPA was signed and the matter concerned that fund’s LPAC/IAC. Conversely, an LPAC reference in an unsigned draft LPA was not enough.

## Near-misses excluded

- **1026-00001 — Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P.** The LPA review memorandum discusses an LPAC, but the matter-closing memorandum says Fund IV’s first close had not occurred, BFO did not subscribe, no subscription agreement or capital commitment was made, and no transaction document other than the engagement letter was executed in the matter. I therefore did not treat the dated LPA review copy as a signed LPA and excluded the matter under the user’s instruction.
- **1002-00005 — Pinnacle Continuation Vehicle LP.** The relevant document is expressly a “Markup of Tax Provisions” to a “Draft Limited Partnership Agreement”; the engagement describes a proposed CV with target first/final closes. No signed LPA appears in the matter.
- **1003-00002 — Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP.** The initial and revised LPAs are expressly preliminary, nonbinding drafts “for discussion purposes only.” The first-close checklist still describes the LPA as draft/in progress and the LPAC charter as a future first-close deliverable. No signed LPA appears in the matter.
- **1004-00002 — Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP.** The only LPA is a “First Draft,” and the related fundraising and LPAC arrangements are prospective. No signed LPA appears in the matter.
- **1023-00001 — ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP.** The LP agreement is an execution version and the matter describes scheduled execution, but the governance memorandum expressly states: “No formal Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") is established.” The sole LP instead has direct consent rights, so it fails the committee prong even apart from the signing issue.

## Bottom line

**Qualifying matter count: 4.**

The qualifying matters are **1001-00002, 1024-00002, 1027-00002, and 1041-00005**."}
